children.title: Bounded-Oracle Normalizations
children.top_down_role: Comparison regimes controlled by bounds on oracle outputs.

knowledge_statements.title: Bounded-Oracle Normalizations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform dual-norm normalization for selected outputs of a convex first-order oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a finite-dimensional normed space, let \(Q\subseteq X\) be nonempty and convex, and let \(f:Q\to\mathbb{R}\) be convex. Define the relative convex subdifferential by \[\partial_Q f(x):=\{g\in X^*: f(y)\ge f(x)+\langle g,y-x\rangle\text{ for every }y\in Q\}.\] A bounded first-order oracle with scale \(G>0\) returns, at every queried point \(x\in Q\), a selected vector \(g(x)\in\partial_Q f(x)\) satisfying \[\lVert g(x)\rVert_{*}\le G.\] For \(\widehat f=f/G\), the corresponding output \(\widehat g(x)=g(x)/G\) belongs to \(\partial_Q\widehat f(x)\) and satisfies \(\lVert\widehat g(x)\rVert_{*}\le1\). This condition bounds the selected oracle outputs; it does not assert that every member of \(\partial_Q f(x)\) is bounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bounded convex first-order oracle selects, at each query point, a relative subgradient whose dual norm is at most a fixed scale. Dividing the objective and selected outputs by that positive scale gives a unit bound, without requiring every possible subgradient to be bounded.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a finite-dimensional normed space with dual space \(X^*\) and dual norm \(\lVert\cdot\rVert_*\).
\(Q\subseteq X\) is nonempty and convex, and \(f:Q\to\mathbb{R}\) is convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every queried \(x\in Q\), \(g(x)\in\partial_Q f(x)\) and \(\lVert g(x)\rVert_*=G\) are not required; rather, the normalization condition is \(g(x)\in\partial_Q f(x)\) and \(\lVert g(x)\rVert_*\le G\), which implies \(g(x)/G\in\partial_Q(f/G)(x)\) and \(\lVert g(x)/G\rVert_*\le1\).

notation.meaning: convex subdifferential of f relative to Q at x
selected first-order oracle output at x
dual norm on the dual space

children.title: Joint Domain–Oracle Bounds
children.top_down_role: Regimes combining geometric domain bounds with bounded oracle information.

knowledge_statements.title: Joint Domain–Oracle Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coupling of a bounded feasible domain with uniformly bounded selected outputs of a convex first-order oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a finite-dimensional normed space, let \(Q\subseteq X\) be nonempty and convex with \(\operatorname{diam}(Q)\le D\), and let \(f:Q\to\mathbb{R}\) be convex. For \(x\in Q\), define \[\partial_Q f(x):=\{g\in X^*: f(y)\ge f(x)+\langle g,y-x\rangle\text{ for every }y\in Q\}.\] Suppose that for every \(x\in Q\) the oracle selects \(g(x)\in\partial_Q f(x)\) with \(\lVert g(x)\rVert_\ast\le G\), where \(D,G>0\). Then every \(x,y\in Q\) satisfy \[\lvert f(x)-f(y)\rvert\le G\lVert x-y\rVert\le GD.\] Consequently, if \(x_*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{z\in Q}f(z)\), then \(0\le f(x)-f(x_*)\le GD\) for every \(x\in Q\). Thus \(GD\) is the joint objective-gap scale associated with these domain and oracle bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a convex feasible set has diameter at most D and the oracle can select a relative subgradient of dual norm at most G at every feasible point, then objective values differ by at most G times the point distance and hence by at most GD. Every feasible objective gap is therefore at most GD.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a finite-dimensional normed space with dual space \(X^*\).
\(Q\subseteq X\) is nonempty and convex, with \(\operatorname{diam}(Q)\le D\).
\(f:Q\to\mathbb{R}\) is convex, and for every \(x\in Q\) a selected \(g(x)\in\partial_Q f(x)\) satisfies \(\lVert g(x)\rVert_*\le G\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For all \(x,y\in Q\), \(\lvert f(x)-f(y)\rvert\le G\lVert x-y\rVert\le GD\).

notation.meaning: convex subdifferential of f relative to Q at x
uniform bound on selected oracle outputs

knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Dual Initialization Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted product-space initialization used in primal-dual performance estimation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider a saddle problem on finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces with a primal solution \(x_*\), a dual solution \(y_*\), initial points \(x_0,y_0\), and parameters \(\tau,
\sigma>0\). A quadratic primal-dual initialization model with radius \(R>0\) imposes \[\frac{\lVert x_0-x_*\rVert^2}{2\tau}+\frac{\lVert y_0-y_*\rVert^2}{2\sigma}\le R^2.\] For algorithms involving a linear coupling operator \(K\), this initial-data condition is paired separately with the step-size admissibility condition \(\tau\sigma\lVert K\rVert^2<1\). The radius bound and step-size condition encode distinct restrictions and should remain separate in a performance-estimation model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Primal-dual initialization bounds a weighted product-space distance from an initial pair to a saddle pair, separately from any coupling-dependent step-size restriction.
assumptions_latex: \(x_*,y_*\) form a primal-dual solution pair.

\(\tau,
\sigma,R>0\).
\(K\) is linear when the coupling condition is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\frac{\lVert x_0-x_*\rVert^2}{2\tau}+\frac{\lVert y_0-y_*\rVert^2}{2\sigma}\le R^2\), with \(\tau\sigma\lVert K\rVert^2<1\) imposed independently when required.

notation.meaning: primal and dual metric or step parameters

knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Value Criteria
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Suboptimality certificate for a candidate iterate or prescribed algorithm output.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:Q\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and attain its minimum \(f_*:=\min_{x\in Q}f(x)\). For a candidate output \(x_N\in Q\cap\operatorname{dom}f\) and tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge0\), the objective-value criterion is \[f(x_N)-f_*\le\varepsilon.\] A reported upper bound \(U_N\) is a verifiable performance certificate whenever the available interpolation, oracle, or dual-feasibility constraints imply \(f(x_N)-f_*\le U_N\); the target is certified at tolerance \(\varepsilon\) if \(U_N\le\varepsilon\). The criterion measures function-value suboptimality and does not by itself control distance to the solution set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An output satisfies the objective-value criterion when its value exceeds the optimum by at most the prescribed tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper and attains its minimum over \(Q\).
\(x_N\in Q\cap\operatorname{dom}f\).
\(\varepsilon\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x_N)-f_*\le\varepsilon\).

knowledge_statements.title: Solution-Distance Criteria
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distance-to-solution-set certificate for a candidate algorithm output.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\) be a subset of a finite-dimensional normed space, and suppose that the solution set \(X_*:=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in Q}f(x)\) is nonempty and closed. For an output \(x_N\in Q\) and a tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge0\), the solution-distance criterion is \[\operatorname{dist}(x_N,X_*):=\inf_{x_*\in X_*}\lVert x_N-x_*\rVert\le\varepsilon.\] Because \(X_*\) is nonempty and closed in a finite-dimensional space, the distance is attained; hence the criterion is equivalent to the existence of an \(x_*\in X_*\) satisfying \(\lVert x_N-x_*\rVert\le\varepsilon\). The criterion remains meaningful when the minimizer is nonunique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An output meets the solution-distance criterion when its distance to the entire nonempty closed solution set is at most the prescribed tolerance; this also covers nonunique minimizers.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\) is contained in a finite-dimensional normed space.
\(X_*:=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in Q}f(x)\) is nonempty and closed.
\(x_N\in Q\) and \(\varepsilon\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}(x_N,X_*)\le\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: distance from x to the solution set

knowledge_statements.title: Objective–Distance Comparison Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-sided objective-gap and solution-distance comparison under smooth strong convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) be differentiable, \(L\)-smooth, and \(\mu\)-strongly convex on a Hilbert space, with \(0<\mu\le L\). Its minimizer \(x_*\) is unique, and every \(x\in X\) satisfies \[\frac{\mu}{2}\lVert x-x_*\rVert^2\le f(x)-f(x_*)\le\frac{L}{2}\lVert x-x_*\rVert^2.\] Hence an objective guarantee \(f(x)-f(x_*)\le\varepsilon\) implies \(\lVert x-x_*\rVert\le\sqrt{2\varepsilon/
\mu}\), while a distance guarantee \(\lVert x-x_*\rVert\le r\) implies an objective gap at most \(Lr^2/2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Smooth strong convexity makes objective gap and squared solution distance equivalent up to the curvature constants.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is differentiable, \(L\)-smooth, and \(\mu\)-strongly convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\frac{\mu}{2}\lVert x-x_*\rVert^2\le f(x)-f(x_*)\le\frac{L}{2}\lVert x-x_*\rVert^2\) for every \(x\in X\).

knowledge_statements.title: Gradient-Mapping Criteria
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proximal-gradient residual criterion for composite minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=f+h\) on a finite-dimensional Hilbert space, where \(f\) is differentiable and \(h\) is proper, closed, and convex. For \(\eta>0\), define \[x^+=\operatorname{prox}_{\eta h}(x-\eta\nabla f(x)),\qquad G_\eta(x)=\frac{x-x^+}{\eta}.\] A candidate point \(x\) satisfies the gradient-mapping criterion at tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge0\) when \(\lVert G_\eta(x)\rVert\le\varepsilon\). Moreover, \(G_\eta(x)=0\) if and only if \(0\in\nabla f(x)+\partial h(x)\), so a zero gradient mapping exactly certifies first-order stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The gradient-mapping criterion bounds the proximal-gradient residual; a zero mapping is equivalent to composite first-order stationarity.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is differentiable and \(h\) is proper, closed, and convex.
\(\eta>0\) and \(\varepsilon\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lVert G_\eta(x)\rVert\le\varepsilon\), with \(G_\eta(x)=0\iff0\in\nabla f(x)+\partial h(x)\).

notation.meaning: gradient mapping with step parameter eta
proximal operator of eta times h

knowledge_statements.title: Stationarity Criteria
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limiting-subdifferential residual criterion for composite first-order stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=f+h\) on a finite-dimensional Hilbert space, where \(f\) is continuously differentiable and \(h\) is proper, closed, and convex. Let \(\partial F(x)\) denote the limiting subdifferential of \(F\) at \(x\). For \(x\in\operatorname{dom}h\) and \(\varepsilon\ge0\), the stationarity criterion is \[\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial F(x)):=\inf_{v\in\partial F(x)}\lVert v\rVert\le\varepsilon,\qquad \partial F(x)=\nabla f(x)+\partial h(x).\] Equivalently, there exists \(u\in\partial h(x)\) such that \(\lVert\nabla f(x)+u\rVert\le\varepsilon\). At \(\varepsilon=0\), this becomes the exact first-order stationarity inclusion \(0\in\partial F(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A point is approximately stationary when the limiting subdifferential of the composite objective contains a vector whose norm is at most the tolerance. At zero tolerance this is the exact stationarity inclusion.
assumptions_latex: The underlying space is a finite-dimensional Hilbert space.
\(f\) is continuously differentiable and \(h\) is proper, closed, and convex.
\(x\in\operatorname{dom}h\) and \(\varepsilon\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial F(x))\le\varepsilon\), where \(\partial F\) is the limiting subdifferential.

notation.meaning: limiting subdifferential of F at x
convex subdifferential of h at x

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Point Residual Criteria
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Absolute and normalized residual tests for a single-valued fixed-point operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be a real Hilbert space, let \(T:H\to H\), and let \(x\in H\). The absolute fixed-point residual criterion with tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge 0\) is \[\|x-Tx\|\le \varepsilon.\] Given a scale \(s(x)>0\), the normalized criterion is \[\frac{\|x-Tx\|}{s(x)}\le \varepsilon.\] When \(\varepsilon=0\), either criterion is equivalent to \(x\in\operatorname{Fix}T\). For positive tolerance, the residual certifies approximate satisfaction of the fixed-point equation in the chosen norm and scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A point passes when its displacement under the fixed-point map is below an absolute or normalized tolerance; zero residual is exactly the fixed-point condition.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space.
\(T:H\to H\) is single-valued.
\(s(x)>0\) whenever the normalized criterion is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|x-Tx\|\le\varepsilon\), or \(\|x-Tx\|/s(x)\le\varepsilon\); at \(\varepsilon=0\), \(x\in\operatorname{Fix}T\).

notation.meaning: The set of points fixed by T.

knowledge_statements.title: Operator-Residual Criteria
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual tests for a possibly set-valued monotone inclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be a real Hilbert space, let \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\), and let \(x\in\operatorname{dom}A\). Define the operator residual by \[\rho_A(x):=\operatorname{dist}(0,Ax)=\inf_{a\in Ax}\|a\|.\] The operator-residual criterion with tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge0\) is \(\rho_A(x)\le\varepsilon\). If an explicit vector \(a\in Ax\) satisfies \(\|a\|\le\varepsilon\), then it is a directly verifiable witness for the criterion. At tolerance zero, \(\rho_A(x)=0\) implies \(0\in Ax\) whenever \(Ax\) is closed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Operator stationarity is measured by the distance from zero to the operator value; a small graph element is a verifiable residual witness.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space.
\(A:H\rightrightarrows H\) and \(x\in\operatorname{dom}A\).
\(Ax\) is closed for the zero-residual equivalence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_A(x)\le\varepsilon\); if \(\varepsilon=0\) and \(Ax\) is closed, then \(0\in Ax\).

notation.meaning: Distance from zero to the set Ax.

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Point–Operator Residual Transfers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Resolvent correspondence between fixed-point displacement and an inclusion residual witness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\), let \(\gamma>0\), and suppose the resolvent \(T=J_{\gamma A}:=(I+\gamma A)^{-1}\) is single-valued at \(x\in H\). Set \(z=Tx\) and \(r=x-Tx\). The resolvent identity gives \[\frac{r}{\gamma}\in Az,\qquad x=z+\gamma\frac{r}{\gamma}.\] Consequently, \[\operatorname{dist}(0,Az)\le\frac{\|x-Tx\|}{\gamma}.\] Thus a fixed-point residual bound \(\|x-Tx\|\le\varepsilon\) transfers to an operator-residual bound at \(z\) of at most \(\varepsilon/\gamma\), and \(x=Tx\) is equivalent to \(0\in Ax\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a resolvent map, fixed-point displacement divided by the stepsize is an explicit operator residual at the mapped point.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space and \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\).
\(J_{\gamma A}\) is single-valued at \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x-Tx)/\gamma\in A(Tx)\) and \(\operatorname{dist}(0,A(Tx))\le\|x-Tx\|/\gamma\).

notation.meaning: The resolvent of the scaled operator γA.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Dual Gap Criteria
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Restricted saddle-function gap used as a finite certificate criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) and \(Y\) be nonempty sets, and let \(L:X\times Y\to\mathbb{R}\) be convex in its first argument and concave in its second. For \((x,y)\in X\times Y\), define \[G_{X,Y}(x,y):=\sup_{v\in Y}L(x,v)-\inf_{u\in X}L(u,y).\] Provided both terms are finite, the primal-dual gap criterion with tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge0\) is \(G_{X,Y}(x,y)\le\varepsilon\). The gap is nonnegative. If it is zero and both extrema are attained, then \((x,y)\) is a saddle point of \(L\) on \(X\times Y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A primal-dual pair passes when its restricted saddle gap is finite and at most the tolerance; zero attained gap certifies a saddle point.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(Y\) are nonempty.
\(L\) is real-valued, convex-concave on \(X\times Y\).
The displayed supremum and infimum are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\le G_{X,Y}(x,y)\le\varepsilon\); at attained zero gap, \((x,y)\) is a saddle point.

notation.meaning: The convex-concave saddle function or Lagrangian.

children.title: Feasibility Criteria
children.top_down_role: Performance quantities measuring violation of constraints or inclusion conditions.

knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility Criteria
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normed residual criteria for conic primal and dual feasibility in finite-dimensional Euclidean spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E\) and \(F\) be finite-dimensional real Euclidean spaces, let \(A:E\to F\) be linear with adjoint \(A^*:F\to E\), let \(b\in F\) and \(c\in E\), and let \(K\subseteq F\) be a nonempty closed convex cone with dual cone \(K^*:=\{y\in F:\langle y,k\rangle\ge0\text{ for every }k\in K\}\). For \(x\in E\) and \(y\in F\), define \[r_p(x):=\operatorname{dist}(Ax-b,-K),\qquad r_d(y):=\bigl(\|c-A^*y\|^2+\operatorname{dist}(y,K^*)^2\bigr)^{1/2}.\] Given tolerances \(\varepsilon_p,\varepsilon_d\ge0\), the pair \((x,y)\) satisfies the feasibility criterion when \(r_p(x)\le\varepsilon_p\) and \(r_d(y)\le\varepsilon_d\). At zero tolerances, these inequalities are equivalent to \(Ax-b\in-K\), \(A^*y=c\), and \(y\in K^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In a finite-dimensional conic primal-dual system, primal feasibility is measured by distance to the negative constraint cone, while dual feasibility combines the equality residual with distance to the dual cone. Both residuals vanish exactly at a feasible primal-dual pair.
assumptions_latex: \(E\) and \(F\) are finite-dimensional real Euclidean spaces.
\(A:E\to F\) is linear, \(b\in F\), and \(c\in E\).
\(K\subseteq F\) is a nonempty closed convex cone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_p(x)\le\varepsilon_p\) and \(r_d(y)\le\varepsilon_d\); at zero tolerances, \(Ax-b\in-K\), \(A^*y=c\), and \(y\in K^*\).

notation.meaning: The dual cone of K in F.

children.title: Gap–Feasibility Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Regimes organizing the interaction between primal-dual accuracy and feasibility accuracy.

knowledge_statements.title: Gap–Feasibility Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint use of gap and feasibility residuals and transfers supplied by explicit error bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) and \(Y\) be sets, let \(\mathcal D\subseteq X\times Y\) be a candidate domain, and let \(G:\mathcal D\to[0,+\infty)\), \(r_p:X\to[0,+\infty)\), and \(r_d:Y\to[0,+\infty)\) be a gap measure and primal and dual feasibility residuals. For \((x,y)\in\mathcal D\) and tolerances \(\varepsilon_g,\varepsilon_p,\varepsilon_d\ge0\), the joint certificate is the componentwise inequality \[\bigl(G(x,y),r_p(x),r_d(y)\bigr)\le\bigl(\varepsilon_g,\varepsilon_p,\varepsilon_d\bigr).\] If constants \(\alpha_p,\alpha_d\ge0\) satisfy \(r_p(x)\le\alpha_pG(x,y)\) and \(r_d(y)\le\alpha_dG(x,y)\) for every \((x,y)\in\mathcal D\), then \(G(x,y)\le\varepsilon_g\) implies \[r_p(x)\le\alpha_p\varepsilon_g,\qquad r_d(y)\le\alpha_d\varepsilon_g.\] Thus a gap bound transfers to feasibility bounds only through relations that are explicitly assumed or established for the candidate domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Gap and feasibility are jointly certified by componentwise tolerances. A gap tolerance yields feasibility tolerances when explicit error-bound relations between the gap and feasibility residuals hold throughout the candidate domain.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal D\subseteq X\times Y\) is the candidate domain.
\(G\), \(r_p\), and \(r_d\) are finite and nonnegative on their stated domains.
\(\varepsilon_g,\varepsilon_p,\varepsilon_d\ge0\).
Any gap-to-feasibility transfer uses stated constants \(\alpha_p,\alpha_d\ge0\) valid on \(\mathcal D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The joint criterion is componentwise; under \(r_p(x)\le\alpha_pG(x,y)\) and \(r_d(y)\le\alpha_dG(x,y)\), the bound \(G(x,y)\le\varepsilon_g\) yields \(r_p(x)\le\alpha_p\varepsilon_g\) and \(r_d(y)\le\alpha_d\varepsilon_g\).

notation.meaning: A finite nonnegative primal-dual gap measure.
Error-bound transfer constants valid on the candidate domain.

knowledge_statements.title: Last-Iterate Criteria
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Performance evaluation at the final generated iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let an algorithm generate \(x_0,x_1,\ldots,x_N\) in a set \(X\), and let \(M:X\to[0,+\infty]\) be a performance measure whose value zero represents the target condition. The last-iterate output is \(x_N\). For tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge0\), the last-iterate criterion is \[M(x_N)\le\varepsilon.\] The criterion concerns only the prescribed terminal index: bounds on earlier iterates, their average, or their minimum do not establish it unless a separate monotonicity or transfer property relates those quantities to \(M(x_N)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The algorithm is judged solely at its terminal iterate; earlier, averaged, or best-iterate bounds require an additional transfer argument.
assumptions_latex: \(N\) is a nonnegative integer.
\(x_k\in X\) for \(0\le k\le N\).
\(M:X\to[0,+\infty]\) is the selected performance measure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M(x_N)\le\varepsilon\).

children.title: Averaged-Iterate Criteria
children.top_down_role: Performance criteria applied to an aggregate of encoded iterates.

knowledge_statements.title: Averaged-Iterate Criteria
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Performance evaluation at a convex combination of generated iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be convex, let \(x_0,\ldots,x_N\in X\), and choose weights \(w_k\ge0\) with \(W_N:=\sum_{k=0}^Nw_k>0\). Define the averaged output by \[\bar x_N:=\frac{1}{W_N}\sum_{k=0}^Nw_kx_k.\] For a performance measure \(M:X\to[0,+\infty]\), the averaged-iterate criterion with tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge0\) is \(M(\bar x_N)\le\varepsilon\). If \(M\) is convex, then \[M(\bar x_N)\le\frac{1}{W_N}\sum_{k=0}^Nw_kM(x_k),\] so a weighted mean performance bound certifies the averaged output.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A weighted convex combination is the reported output; convexity lets the weighted mean of iterate performances certify its performance.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is convex and contains \(x_0,\ldots,x_N\).
\(M\) is convex for the displayed transfer inequality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M(\bar x_N)\le\varepsilon\), with \(M(\bar x_N)\le W_N^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^Nw_kM(x_k)\) when \(M\) is convex.

knowledge_statements.title: Best-Iterate Criteria
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Performance evaluation by the smallest observed criterion value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_0,\ldots,x_N\in X\) and let \(M:X\to[0,+\infty]\). Choose any index \[k_*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{0\le k\le N}M(x_k)\] and report \(x_{k_*}\). The best-iterate criterion with tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge0\) is \[M(x_{k_*})=\min_{0\le k\le N}M(x_k)\le\varepsilon.\] This output rule is operational only when the values \(M(x_k)\) are observable or are accompanied by computable upper certificates. An existential bound on the minimum need not identify an implementable output when the performance measure is unavailable to the algorithm.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The reported iterate minimizes the observed performance measure; implementability requires evaluating that measure or computable upper certificates.
assumptions_latex: \(N\) is finite and \(x_k\in X\).
\(M:X\to[0,+\infty]\).
Selection is implementable only if criterion values or valid upper certificates are observable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M(x_{k_*})=\min_{0\le k\le N}M(x_k)\le\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: An index attaining the smallest criterion value.

children.title: Output-Regime Comparisons

knowledge_statements.title: Output-Regime Comparisons
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Universal scalar comparisons and limits among last, averaged, and best outputs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nonnegative values \(m_k:=M(x_k)\) and weights \(w_k\ge0\) with \(W_N>0\), \[\min_{0\le k\le N}m_k\le\frac{1}{W_N}\sum_{k=0}^Nw_km_k\le\max_{0\le k\le N}m_k.\] Hence a weighted mean bound implies the same best-value bound. If \(X\) and \(M\) are convex, the averaged point also satisfies \(M(\bar x_N)\le W_N^{-1}\sum_kw_km_k\). There is no universal ordering between \(M(x_N)\) and \(M(\bar x_N)\), nor does a best-value bound imply a last-iterate bound, unless additional trajectory structure such as monotonicity is imposed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Best value never exceeds weighted mean performance, and convexity transfers mean bounds to the averaged point; last-iterate comparisons need extra trajectory structure.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(M\) are convex for the averaged-point inequality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_kM(x_k)\le W_N^{-1}\sum_kw_kM(x_k)\), while no unconditional last-versus-average ordering holds.

notation.meaning: The scalar performance of iterate k.

knowledge_statements.title: Closed Convex Nonsmooth Interpolation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional interpolation by a proper closed convex function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I\) be finite and let \((x_i,g_i,f_i)_{i\in I}\subset\mathbb{R}^d\times\mathbb{R}^d\times\mathbb{R}\). There exists a proper lower-semicontinuous convex function \(f:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) satisfying \[f(x_i)=f_i,\qquad g_i\in\partial f(x_i)\quad(i\in I)\] if and only if \[f_i\ge f_j+\langle g_j,x_i-x_j\rangle\quad(i,j\in I).\] Whenever these inequalities hold, one interpolant is \[f(x)=\max_{j\in I}\bigl\{f_j+\langle g_j,x-x_j\rangle\bigr\}.\] Thus the finite interpolation constraints are both necessary and sufficient for realizability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite value-subgradient data admit a closed convex interpolant exactly when every sampled affine support lies below every sampled value.
assumptions_latex: \(I\) is finite.
\(x_i,g_i\in\mathbb{R}^d\) and \(f_i\in\mathbb{R}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A proper closed convex interpolant exists if and only if \(f_i\ge f_j+\langle g_j,x_i-x_j\rangle\) for all \(i,j\in I\).

notation.meaning: The convex subdifferential of f at x.

knowledge_statements.title: Smooth Convex Interpolation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional interpolation by a convex function with Lipschitz gradient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I\) be finite, let \(L>0\), and let \((x_i,g_i,f_i)_{i\in I}\subset\mathbb{R}^d\times\mathbb{R}^d\times\mathbb{R}\). There exists a convex differentiable function \(f:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}\) whose gradient is \(L\)-Lipschitz and which satisfies \[f(x_i)=f_i,\qquad \nabla f(x_i)=g_i\quad(i\in I)\] if and only if, for every \(i,j\in I\), \[f_i\ge f_j+\langle g_j,x_i-x_j\rangle+\frac{1}{2L}\|g_i-g_j\|^2.\] These pairwise inequalities therefore give an exact finite certificate for smooth convex realizability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Value-gradient data admit an L-smooth convex interpolant exactly when every pair satisfies the strengthened subgradient inequality with the gradient-difference term.
assumptions_latex: \(I\) is finite.
\(x_i,g_i\in\mathbb{R}^d\) and \(f_i\in\mathbb{R}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An \(L\)-smooth convex interpolant exists if and only if the displayed pairwise inequalities hold for all \(i,j\in I\).

notation.meaning: A Lipschitz constant for the gradient.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated pairwise condition is the standard exact finite interpolation criterion for convex functions with L-Lipschitz gradient, but the record supplies no citation. Because this is a nontrivial if-and-only-if theorem, an authoritative source with a specific theorem, section, or page locator is required.

knowledge_statements.title: Strongly Convex Interpolation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite interpolation by proper closed \(\mu\)-strongly convex functions on a finite-dimensional Hilbert space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(I\) be finite, let \(\mu\ge 0\), and prescribe \((x_i,g_i,f_i)\in H\times H\times\mathbb R\) for \(i\in I\). There exists a proper closed \(\mu\)-strongly convex function \(f:H\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) satisfying \(f(x_i)=f_i\) and \(g_i\in\partial f(x_i)\) for every \(i\) if and only if
\[
f_i\ge f_j+\langle g_j,x_i-x_j\rangle+\frac{\mu}{2}\lVert x_i-x_j\rVert^2\qquad(i,j\in I).
\]
Equivalently, the shifted data \((x_i,g_i-\mu x_i,f_i-\mu\lVert x_i\rVert^2/2)\) are interpolable by a proper closed convex function.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strongly convex interpolation is possible exactly when every sampled value lies above every sampled supporting quadratic of curvature μ.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a finite-dimensional real Hilbert space.
\(I\) is finite and \(f_i\in\mathbb R\) for every \(i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists f\) with \(f(x_i)=f_i\) and \(g_i\in\partial f(x_i)\) for all \(i\) if and only if the displayed pairwise inequalities hold.

notation.meaning: convex subdifferential of f at x

knowledge_statements.title: Smooth Strongly Convex Interpolation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finite interpolation criterion for differentiable \(L\)-smooth, \(\mu\)-strongly convex functions when \(0\le\mu<L\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(I\) be finite, prescribe \((x_i,g_i,f_i)\in H\times H\times\mathbb R\), and let \(0\le\mu<L<\infty\). There exists a differentiable \(\mu\)-strongly convex function \(f:H\to\mathbb R\) whose gradient is \(L\)-Lipschitz and satisfies \(f(x_i)=f_i\), \(\nabla f(x_i)=g_i\) for all \(i\) if and only if, for every \(i,j\in I\),
\[
f_i\ge f_j+\langle g_j,x_i-x_j\rangle+\frac{1}{2L}\lVert g_i-g_j\rVert^2+\frac{\mu}{2(1-\mu/L)}\left\lVert x_i-x_j-\frac{g_i-g_j}{L}\right\rVert^2.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A smooth strongly convex interpolant exists exactly when all ordered sample pairs satisfy the coupled value, gradient, smoothness, and curvature inequality.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a finite-dimensional real Hilbert space and \(I\) is finite.
\(0\le\mu<L<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The data admit an interpolant in the \((\mu,L)\)-smooth strongly convex class if and only if the displayed inequalities hold.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed smooth strongly convex interpolation inequality is the standard exact criterion for 0≤μ<L, but no citation is supplied. An authoritative source with a theorem, section, or page locator supporting the exact formula and hypotheses is required.

knowledge_statements.title: Smooth–Nonsmooth Component Interpolation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Componentwise criterion for a smooth convex term plus a proper closed convex term.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(L>0\) and prescribe \((x_i,p_i,a_i,q_i,b_i)\) for finite \(I\), with vectors \(x_i,p_i,q_i\in H\) and scalars \(a_i,b_i\in\mathbb R\). There exist a differentiable convex \(h:H\to\mathbb R\) with \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient and a proper closed convex \(r:H\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) such that \(h(x_i)=a_i\), \(\nabla h(x_i)=p_i\), \(r(x_i)=b_i\), and \(q_i\in\partial r(x_i)\) if and only if, for all \(i,j\in I\),
\[
a_i\ge a_j+\langle p_j,x_i-x_j\rangle+\frac{1}{2L}\lVert p_i-p_j\rVert^2,
\qquad
b_i\ge b_j+\langle q_j,x_i-x_j\rangle.
\]
Then \(F=h+r\) has sampled value \(a_i+b_i\) and sampled subgradient \(p_i+q_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Smooth and nonsmooth component data are jointly realizable exactly when each component satisfies its own interpolation inequalities at the shared sample points.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a finite-dimensional real Hilbert space and \(I\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The component oracle data admit a common-point composite realization \(F=h+r\) if and only if both displayed inequality families hold.

knowledge_statements.title: Indicator-Component Interpolation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite interpolation of indicator values and normal vectors by one nonempty closed convex set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H\) be a finite-dimensional real Hilbert space, let \(I\) be finite and nonempty, and prescribe \((x_i,v_i)\in H\times H\) for every \(i\in I\). There exists a nonempty closed convex set \(C\subseteq H\) such that \(x_i\in C\) and \(v_i\in\partial\delta_C(x_i)=N_C(x_i)\) for every \(i\in I\) if and only if
\[
\langle v_i,x_j-x_i\rangle\le 0\qquad(i,j\in I).
\]
When these inequalities hold, a realizing set is
\[
C=\bigcap_{i\in I}\{x\in H:\langle v_i,x-x_i\rangle\le0\},
\]
and \(\delta_C(x_i)=0\) for every \(i\in I\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The indicator and normal data are realizable if and only if every proposed normal defines a closed halfspace containing all sampled feasible points.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a finite-dimensional real Hilbert space.
\(I\) is finite and nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists C\neq\varnothing\) realizing all indicator and normal data if and only if \(\langle v_i,x_j-x_i\rangle\le0\) for all \(i,j\in I\).

notation.meaning: indicator function of C, equal to zero on C and positive infinity outside C
convex normal cone to C at x

knowledge_statements.title: Indicator–Projection Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility identity linking indicator subgradients, normal cones, and Euclidean projections.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every real Hilbert space \(H\), every nonempty closed convex set \(C\subseteq H\), and every \(z,p\in H\),
\[
p=P_C(z)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
z-p\in N_C(p)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
z-p\in\partial\delta_C(p).
\]
Thus projection data \((z_i,p_i)\) have the canonical indicator-component encoding \((p_i,v_i)\) with \(v_i=z_i-p_i\). Under this identification, finite data are realizable by one nonempty closed convex set if and only if
\[
\langle v_i,p_j-p_i\rangle\le0
g\qquad(i,j\in I).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A point is the projection of an input exactly when the projection residual is a normal, equivalently an indicator subgradient, at that point; identifying each indicator normal with the corresponding residual gives the common finite-data compatibility inequalities.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space.
\(C\subseteq H\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
For the finite-data criterion, \(I\) is finite and nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p=P_C(z)\iff z-p\in N_C(p)\iff z-p\in\partial\delta_C(p)\), and the canonical identification \(v_i=z_i-p_i\) yields the stated finite-data criterion.

children.title: Separable Component Interpolation
children.top_down_role: Realizability of component records organized by separable coordinates or blocks.

knowledge_statements.title: Separable Component Interpolation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinatewise interpolation criterion for proper closed separable convex functions on a finite product space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x_i=(x_{i1},\ldots,x_{id})\in\mathbb R^d\), and prescribe component values \(\beta_{ik}\in\mathbb R\) and component subgradients \(s_{ik}\in\mathbb R\). There exist proper closed convex functions \(\phi_k:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) satisfying \(\phi_k(x_{ik})=\beta_{ik}\), \(s_{ik}\in\partial\phi_k(x_{ik})\), and \(f(x)=\sum_{k=1}^d\phi_k(x_k)\) if and only if
\[
\beta_{ik}\ge\beta_{jk}+s_{jk}(x_{ik}-x_{jk})
\qquad(i,j\in I,\ 1\le k\le d).
\]
For the resulting separable function, \(f(x_i)=\sum_k\beta_{ik}\) and \((s_{i1},\ldots,s_{id})\in\partial f(x_i)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Separable convex data are realizable exactly when each coordinate’s scalar values and subgradients independently satisfy convex interpolation inequalities.
assumptions_latex: \(I\) and the coordinate dimension \(d\) are finite.
All prescribed component values are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A separable convex interpolant exists if and only if every coordinate dataset satisfies the displayed scalar inequalities.

notation.meaning: value of component k at sample i

children.title: Finite-Sum Component Interpolation
children.top_down_role: Realizability of records attached to finitely indexed objective components.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Sum Component Interpolation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independent interpolation of labeled convex components in a finite-sum objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(I\) and \(M=\{1,\ldots,m\}\) be finite. For every \(i\in I\) and \(\ell\in M\), prescribe \((x_i,g_i^{\ell},f_i^{\ell})\in H\times H\times\mathbb R\). There exist proper closed convex functions \(f_\ell:H\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) with \(f_\ell(x_i)=f_i^{\ell}\) and \(g_i^{\ell}\in\partial f_\ell(x_i)\) if and only if
\[
f_i^{\ell}\ge f_j^{\ell}+\langle g_j^{\ell},x_i-x_j\rangle
\qquad(i,j\in I,\ \ell\in M).
\]
Then \(F=m^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^m f_\ell\) satisfies \(F(x_i)=m^{-1}\sum_\ell f_i^{\ell}\) and \(m^{-1}\sum_\ell g_i^{\ell}\in\partial F(x_i)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Labeled finite-sum component data are realizable exactly when each component independently satisfies convex interpolation inequalities on the shared samples.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a finite-dimensional real Hilbert space.
\(I\) and \(M\) are finite, with \(m\ge1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The finite-sum component oracle is realizable if and only if every labeled component passes convex interpolation.

children.title: Separable Finite-Sum Regimes
children.top_down_role: Interpolation settings combining indexed finite sums with separable component structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Separable Finite-Sum Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combined coordinate-separable and labeled finite-sum interpolation regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider objectives
\[
F(x)=\frac1m\sum_{\ell=1}^m f_\ell(x),
\qquad
f_\ell(x)=\sum_{k=1}^d\phi_{\ell k}(x_k),
\]
where every \(\phi_{\ell k}:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) is proper closed convex. Prescribed scalar data \((x_{ik},\beta_{i\ell k},s_{i\ell k})\) are realizable in this regime if and only if
\[
\beta_{i\ell k}\ge\beta_{j\ell k}+s_{j\ell k}(x_{ik}-x_{jk})
\qquad(i,j\in I,\ 1\le\ell\le m,\ 1\le k\le d).
\]
The induced samples are \(F(x_i)=(1/m)\sum_{\ell,k}\beta_{i\ell k}\) and \((1/m)(\sum_\ell s_{i\ell1},\ldots,\sum_\ell s_{i\ell d})\in\partial F(x_i)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For separable finite sums, interpolation decomposes independently across both component labels and coordinates, followed by the prescribed sums and averages.
assumptions_latex: \(I\), \(m\), and \(d\) are finite, with \(m,d\ge1\).
Every prescribed scalar component value is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The joint regime is realizable exactly when all \((\ell,k)\)-indexed scalar interpolation inequalities hold.

notation.meaning: coordinate k of finite-sum component ℓ

children.title: Monotone Operator Interpolation
children.top_down_role: Finite-data realizability for monotone operator records.

knowledge_statements.title: Monotone Operator Interpolation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite graph interpolation by a possibly set-valued monotone operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(I\) be finite and prescribe graph pairs \((x_i,u_i)\in H\times H\). There exists a monotone operator \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\) satisfying \(u_i\in A(x_i)\) for every \(i\in I\) if and only if
\[
\langle u_i-u_j,x_i-x_j\rangle\ge0
\qquad(i,j\in I).
\]
No maximality is required: when the inequalities hold, the finite relation with graph \(\{(x_i,u_i):i\in I\}\) is itself a monotone operator interpolating the data.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite graph data admit a monotone operator interpolant exactly when every pair of samples satisfies the monotonicity inequality.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space.
\(I\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists A\) monotone with \(u_i\in A(x_i)\) for all \(i\) if and only if the pairwise inequalities hold.

children.title: Strongly Monotone Operator Interpolation
children.top_down_role: Finite-data realizability for operator records with a prescribed strong-monotonicity regime.

knowledge_statements.title: Strongly Monotone Operator Interpolation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite graph interpolation by a possibly set-valued operator with prescribed strong-monotonicity modulus.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(I\) be finite, let \(\mu>0\), and prescribe \((x_i,u_i)\in H\times H\). There exists a \(\mu\)-strongly monotone operator \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\) satisfying \(u_i\in A(x_i)\) for every \(i\in I\) if and only if
\[
\langle u_i-u_j,x_i-x_j\rangle\ge\mu\lVert x_i-x_j\rVert^2
\qquad(i,j\in I).
\]
Equivalently, the shifted pairs \((x_i,u_i-\mu x_i)\) are interpolable by a monotone operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strongly monotone interpolation is possible exactly when every sample pair has monotonicity ratio at least the prescribed positive modulus.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space and \(I\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists A\) that is \(\mu\)-strongly monotone and contains all samples if and only if the displayed inequalities hold.

notation.meaning: operator obtained by subtracting μ times the identity

children.title: Strong-Monotonicity Boundary Regimes
children.top_down_role: Transitions between ordinary monotonicity and strictly stronger operator structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Strong-Monotonicity Boundary Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Largest strong-monotonicity modulus permitted by finite operator data, including the monotone boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For finite data \((x_i,u_i)\), assume \(\langle u_i-u_j,x_i-x_j\rangle\ge0\) whenever \(x_i=x_j\) or \(x_i\ne x_j\), and define
\[
\mu_\star=\min_{\substack{i,j\in I\\x_i\ne x_j}}
\frac{\langle u_i-u_j,x_i-x_j\rangle}{\lVert x_i-x_j\rVert^2},
\]
with \(\mu_\star=+\infty\) when no distinct sample locations occur. The data admit a \(\mu\)-strongly monotone interpolant exactly for \(0\le\mu\le\mu_\star\). Thus \(\mu_\star=0\) permits monotone interpolation but no positive strong-monotonicity modulus, whereas a negative pairwise numerator precludes even monotone interpolation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The smallest pairwise monotonicity ratio is the exact maximum strong-monotonicity modulus; zero is the sharp boundary between monotone and strongly monotone realizability.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space and \(I\) is finite.
Strong monotonicity with modulus \(0\) is interpreted as ordinary monotonicity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The admissible moduli are exactly \([0,\mu_\star]\), subject to pairwise monotonicity; \(\mu_\star=0\) is the sharp failure boundary for positive modulus.

notation.meaning: largest modulus compatible with all distinct-location sample pairs

children.title: Lipschitz Operator Interpolation
children.top_down_role: Finite-data realizability for operators with prescribed Lipschitz regularity.

knowledge_statements.title: Lipschitz Operator Interpolation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite interpolation by an unrestricted Lipschitz map between real Hilbert spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(I\) be finite, let \(x_i\in\mathcal H\), \(y_i\in\mathcal G\), and let \(L\ge 0\). There exists a map \(T:\mathcal H\to\mathcal G\) satisfying \(T x_i=y_i\) for every \(i\in I\) and \(\|T x-T z\|\le L\|x-z\|\) for all \(x,z\in\mathcal H\) if and only if
\[\|y_i-y_j\|\le L\|x_i-x_j\|\qquad(i,j\in I).\]
Thus the pairwise inequalities are an exact finite-data realizability certificate in real Hilbert spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite data admit an L-Lipschitz interpolating operator exactly when every output distance is at most L times the corresponding input distance.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal H\) and \(\mathcal G\) are real Hilbert spaces.
\(I\) is finite and \(L\ge 0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists T:\mathcal H\to\mathcal G\text{ with }T x_i=y_i\text{ and }\operatorname{Lip}(T)\le L\iff \|y_i-y_j\|\le L\|x_i-x_j\|\ \forall i,j.\)

children.title: Cocoercive Operator Interpolation
children.top_down_role: Finite-data realizability for operators with prescribed cocoercivity.

knowledge_statements.title: Cocoercive Operator Interpolation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finite interpolation for single-valued cocoercive operators on a real Hilbert space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(I\) be finite, \(x_i,y_i\in\mathcal H\), and \(\beta>0\). A map \(T:\mathcal H\to\mathcal H\) with \(T x_i=y_i\) is \(\beta\)-cocoercive, meaning
\[\langle T x-T z,x-z\rangle\ge\beta\|T x-T z\|^2\quad(x,z\in\mathcal H),\]
for some interpolant \(T\) if and only if
\[\langle y_i-y_j,x_i-x_j\rangle\ge\beta\|y_i-y_j\|^2\quad(i,j\in I).\]
Equivalently, the samples \(x_i-2\beta y_i\) define a nonexpansive interpolation problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cocoercive interpolation is characterized by pairwise cocoercivity inequalities, equivalently by nonexpansiveness of the transformed samples x_i−2βy_i.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal H\) is a real Hilbert space.
\(I\) is finite and \(\beta>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists\,\beta\text{-cocoercive }T\text{ with }T x_i=y_i\iff \langle y_i-y_j,x_i-x_j\rangle\ge\beta\|y_i-y_j\|^2\ \forall i,j.\)

notation.meaning: nonexpansive transform of a beta-cocoercive operator

children.title: Lipschitz–Cocoercive Regime Comparisons
children.top_down_role: Structural comparisons between Lipschitz and cocoercive realizability classes.

knowledge_statements.title: Lipschitz–Cocoercive Regime Comparisons
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compares the two operator classes on a real Hilbert space for a fixed positive cocoercivity parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal H\) be a real Hilbert space and let \(\beta>0\). If \(T:\mathcal H\to\mathcal H\) is \(\beta\)-cocoercive, then
\[\|T x-T z\|\le \beta^{-1}\|x-z\|\qquad(x,z\in\mathcal H).\]
Thus \(\beta\)-cocoercivity implies \(\beta^{-1}\)-Lipschitz continuity. The converse fails for every fixed \(\beta>0\): on \(\mathbb R^2\), define
\[Q_\beta(a,b)=\beta^{-1}(-b,a).\]
Then \(Q_\beta\) is \(\beta^{-1}\)-Lipschitz, while for all distinct \(x,z\in\mathbb R^2\),
\[\langle Q_\beta x-Q_\beta z,x-z\rangle=0<\beta\|Q_\beta x-Q_\beta z\|^2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For every beta>0, each beta-cocoercive operator is beta-inverse-Lipschitz, and the scaled quarter-turn shows that the converse fails at that same fixed parameter.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal H\) is a real Hilbert space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{\beta\text{-cocoercive operators}\}\subsetneq\{\beta^{-1}\text{-Lipschitz operators}\}.\)

notation.meaning: quarter-turn linear isometry scaled by beta inverse

children.title: Nonexpansive Operator Interpolation
children.top_down_role: Finite-data realizability for nonexpansive mappings.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonexpansive Operator Interpolation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finite interpolation by nonexpansive self-maps of a real Hilbert space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(I\) be finite and let \(x_i,y_i\in\mathcal H\). There exists a nonexpansive map \(T:\mathcal H\to\mathcal H\) satisfying \(T x_i=y_i\) for every \(i\in I\) if and only if
\[\|y_i-y_j\|^2\le\|x_i-x_j\|^2\qquad(i,j\in I).\]
The condition is directly checkable from the sample Gram matrix and is sufficient because a nonexpansive map defined on the finite sample set admits a Hilbert-space nonexpansive extension.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite data set admits a nonexpansive interpolant exactly when no pairwise distance increases.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal H\) is a real Hilbert space.
\(I\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists\text{ nonexpansive }T:\mathcal H\to\mathcal H\text{ with }T x_i=y_i\iff \|y_i-y_j\|\le\|x_i-x_j\|\ \forall i,j.\)

children.title: Averaged Operator Interpolation
children.top_down_role: Finite-data realizability for mappings with prescribed averagedness.

knowledge_statements.title: Averaged Operator Interpolation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finite interpolation for a fixed averagedness parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(I\) be finite, \(x_i,y_i\in\mathcal H\), and \(0<\alpha<1\). There exists an \(\alpha\)-averaged map \(T=(1-\alpha)I+\alpha R\), where \(R:\mathcal H\to\mathcal H\) is nonexpansive, satisfying \(T x_i=y_i\) if and only if
\[\|y_i-y_j\|^2+\frac{1-\alpha}{\alpha}\|(x_i-y_i)-(x_j-y_j)\|^2\le\|x_i-x_j\|^2\quad(i,j\in I).\]
These inequalities are equivalent to nonexpansive interpolation of \(r_i=\alpha^{-1}y_i-(1-\alpha)\alpha^{-1}x_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Averaged interpolation is exactly certified by a strengthened nonexpansive inequality involving both output and residual differences.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal H\) is a real Hilbert space.
\(I\) is finite and \(0<\alpha<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists\,\alpha\text{-averaged }T\text{ with }T x_i=y_i\iff \|y_i-y_j\|^2+\frac{1-\alpha}{\alpha}\|(x_i-y_i)-(x_j-y_j)\|^2\le\|x_i-x_j\|^2\ \forall i,j.\)

notation.meaning: nonexpansive component in the averaged representation

children.title: Averagedness Boundary Regimes
children.top_down_role: Regime transitions linking averaged mappings with the broader nonexpansive class.

knowledge_statements.title: Averagedness Boundary Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Describes the endpoint and limiting regimes of the averaged-operator interpolation parameter for fixed finite data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(J\) be finite and let \(x_i,y_i\in\mathcal H\) for \(i\in J\). In the representation \(T=(1-\alpha)\mathrm{Id}+\alpha R\) with nonexpansive \(R\), the endpoint \(\alpha=1\) gives exactly the nonexpansive class. If the fixed data satisfy the \(\alpha_k\)-averaged interpolation inequalities for a sequence \(\alpha_k\downarrow0\), then
\[(x_i-y_i)-(x_j-y_j)=0\qquad(i,j\in J).\]
Thus all sample residuals must coincide in this limiting feasibility regime. The value \(\alpha=0\) is excluded by the usual definition of an averaged operator; formal substitution into the representation gives \(T=\mathrm{Id}\), which interpolates the data only when \(y_i=x_i\) for every \(i\in J\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At alpha=1 the class is exactly the nonexpansive class. If fixed data remain interpolable along averagedness parameters tending to zero, all sample residuals must coincide. Alpha=0 is outside the usual definition and formally yields only the identity map.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal H\) is a real Hilbert space.
\(J\) is finite.
The data \((x_i,y_i)_{i\in J}\) are fixed in the limiting statement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha=1\Rightarrow T\text{ is nonexpansive};\quad (\exists\alpha_k\downarrow0\text{ with feasibility})\Rightarrow x_i-y_i=x_j-y_j\ \forall i,j\in J;\quad \alpha=0\Rightarrow T=\mathrm{Id}.\)

notation.meaning: identity operator on the Hilbert space

knowledge_statements.title: Symmetric Linear-Operator Interpolation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite interpolation by a bounded self-adjoint linear operator without spectral bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(I\) be finite and let \(x_i,y_i\in\mathcal H\). There exists a bounded self-adjoint linear operator \(A:\mathcal H\to\mathcal H\) with \(A x_i=y_i\) for every \(i\in I\) if and only if both conditions hold:
\[\sum_i c_i x_i=0\Longrightarrow\sum_i c_i y_i=0,\]
for every real coefficient vector \(c\), and
\[\langle y_i,x_j\rangle=\langle x_i,y_j\rangle\qquad(i,j\in I).\]
The first condition makes the sampled linear action well defined; the second makes its compression to the sampled span symmetric.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Self-adjoint linear interpolation requires and is certified by linear consistency together with symmetry of all sampled cross inner products.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal H\) is a real Hilbert space.
\(I\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists A=A^*\in\mathcal L(\mathcal H)\text{ with }A x_i=y_i\iff \ker X\subseteq\ker Y\text{ and }X^*Y=Y^*X.\)

notation.meaning: bounded linear operators on the Hilbert space

knowledge_statements.title: Nonsymmetric Linear-Operator Interpolation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite interpolation by an unrestricted bounded linear operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(I\) be finite and let \(x_i\in\mathcal H\), \(y_i\in\mathcal G\). A bounded linear operator \(A:\mathcal H\to\mathcal G\) satisfying \(A x_i=y_i\) for every \(i\in I\) exists if and only if
\[\sum_{i\in I}c_i x_i=0\Longrightarrow\sum_{i\in I}c_i y_i=0\]
for every real coefficient vector \(c\). Equivalently, the assignment \(x_i\mapsto y_i\) defines a linear map on \(\operatorname{span}\{x_i:i\in I\}\); because this span is finite-dimensional, that map has a bounded extension to \(\mathcal H\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unrestricted linear interpolation is possible exactly when every linear relation among the inputs is also satisfied by the outputs.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal H\) and \(\mathcal G\) are real Hilbert spaces.
\(I\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists A\in\mathcal L(\mathcal H,\mathcal G)\text{ with }A x_i=y_i\iff \ker X\subseteq\ker Y.\)

children.title: Adjoint-Operator Interpolation
children.top_down_role: Finite-data realizability for records attributed to adjoint actions.

knowledge_statements.title: Adjoint-Operator Interpolation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite sampled interpolation of an adjoint operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(I\) be finite, let \(u_i\in\mathcal G\), and let \(v_i\in\mathcal H\). There exists a bounded linear operator \(A:\mathcal H\to\mathcal G\) whose adjoint satisfies \(A^*u_i=v_i\) for every \(i\in I\) if and only if
\[\sum_{i\in I}c_i u_i=0\Longrightarrow\sum_{i\in I}c_i v_i=0\]
for every real coefficient vector \(c\). Equivalently, the adjoint samples define a well-defined linear map on \(\operatorname{span}\{u_i:i\in I\}\), which can be extended boundedly and then realized as an adjoint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adjoint samples are interpolable exactly when the proposed outputs preserve every linear relation among the adjoint inputs.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal H\) and \(\mathcal G\) are real Hilbert spaces.
\(I\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists A\in\mathcal L(\mathcal H,\mathcal G)\text{ with }A^*u_i=v_i\iff \ker U\subseteq\ker V.\)

children.title: Forward–Adjoint Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Joint realizability constraints linking forward and adjoint records of a common operator.

knowledge_statements.title: Forward–Adjoint Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint realizability condition for finite forward and adjoint samples.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x_i\in\mathcal H\), \(y_i\in\mathcal G\), \(u_j\in\mathcal G\), and \(v_j\in\mathcal H\) be finite families. A bounded linear operator \(A:\mathcal H\to\mathcal G\) can satisfy simultaneously \(A x_i=y_i\) and \(A^*u_j=v_j\) if and only if each sample assignment is linearly consistent and
\[\langle y_i,u_j\rangle_{\mathcal G}=\langle x_i,v_j\rangle_{\mathcal H}\qquad\text{for every }i,j.\]
The displayed cross identities are the finite-data form of the defining adjoint relation \(\langle A x,u\rangle=\langle x,A^*u\rangle\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Forward and adjoint data share one linear operator exactly when both assignments are linearly consistent and every forward–adjoint cross inner product agrees.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal H\) and \(\mathcal G\) are real Hilbert spaces.
Both sample index sets are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists A\in\mathcal L(\mathcal H,\mathcal G):A x_i=y_i,\ A^*u_j=v_j\iff \ker X\subseteq\ker Y,\ \ker U\subseteq\ker V,\ Y^*U=X^*V.\)

knowledge_statements.title: Convex-Set Interpolation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interpolation of boundary points and prescribed normal-cone vectors by a closed convex set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(I\) be finite and let \(x_i,n_i\in\mathcal H\). There exists a nonempty closed convex set \(C\subseteq\mathcal H\) such that \(x_i\in C\) and \(n_i\in N_C(x_i)\) for every \(i\in I\) if and only if
\[\langle n_i,x_j-x_i\rangle\le0\qquad(i,j\in I).\]
When these inequalities hold, one realizing set is
\[C=\bigcap_{i\in I}\{x\in\mathcal H:\langle n_i,x-x_i\rangle\le0\}.\]
Zero prescribed normals are allowed and impose no supporting halfspace restriction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Points with prescribed normals are convex-set interpolable exactly when every sample point lies in every prescribed supporting halfspace.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal H\) is a real Hilbert space.
\(I\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists C\ne\varnothing\text{ closed convex}:n_i\in N_C(x_i)\ \forall i\iff \langle n_i,x_j-x_i\rangle\le0\ \forall i,j.\)

notation.meaning: outward normal cone of C at x

children.title: Smooth Set Interpolation
children.top_down_role: Finite-data realizability for sets with prescribed boundary smoothness.

knowledge_statements.title: Smooth Set Interpolation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the convex-body interpretation with a globally Lipschitz outward unit-normal field.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix \(L\ge0\). Finite data \((x_i,n_i)_{i\in I}\subset\mathcal H\times\mathcal H\) with \(\|n_i\|=1\) are called \(L\)-smooth-set interpolable if there exists a nonempty closed convex set \(C\subseteq\mathcal H\) whose boundary has a unique outward unit normal \(n_C(x)\) at every \(x\in\partial C\), such that
\[x_i\in\partial C,\qquad n_C(x_i)=n_i\quad(i\in I),\]
and
\[\|n_C(x)-n_C(z)\|\le L\|x-z\|\quad(x,z\in\partial C).\]
This definition selects the \(C^{1,1}\)-boundary convention; alternative notions of smooth sets may yield different interpolation conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the C¹,¹-boundary convention, smooth-set interpolation asks for a convex set matching sampled boundary points and unit normals with an L-Lipschitz normal field.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal H\) is a real Hilbert space.
\(I\) is finite and \(L\ge0\).
\(\|n_i\|=1\) for every \(i\in I\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x_i,n_i)_{i\in I}\text{ is }L\text{-smooth-set interpolable}\iff\exists C\text{ satisfying the stated boundary, normal, and Lipschitz conditions}.\)

notation.meaning: unique outward unit normal to C at x
Lipschitz constant of the boundary normal field

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record selects a substantive C^{1,1}-boundary convention for smooth convex sets but supplies no source. An authoritative locator is required to validate this convention, its applicability in general real Hilbert spaces, and its distinction from strong convexity before the definition can be retained.

children.title: Strongly Convex Set Interpolation
children.top_down_role: Finite-data realizability for sets with prescribed strong-convexity geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Strongly Convex Set Interpolation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite boundary-point and outward-unit-normal interpolation under the supporting-ball definition of strong convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix \(R>0\). Data \(\{(x_i,n_i)\}_{i=1}^m\subset\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb R^d\), with \(\|n_i\|=1\), are interpolable by a nonempty closed set representable as an intersection of radius-\(R\) balls, with \(n_i\) outward at \(x_i\), if and only if
\[
\langle n_i,x_j-x_i\rangle\le -\frac{1}{2R}\|x_j-x_i\|^2\qquad(i,j=1,\ldots,m).
\]
When these inequalities hold, a directly verifiable interpolant is
\[
C=\bigcap_{i=1}^m B(x_i-Rn_i,R).
\]
Indeed, every \(x_j\) belongs to every displayed ball, while \(x_i\) lies on the boundary of its \(i\)-th ball with outward normal \(n_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pairwise quadratic support inequalities exactly certify interpolation by an intersection of equal-radius balls; the intersection itself supplies an explicit strongly convex set.
assumptions_latex: \(R>0\) and the ambient space is finite-dimensional Euclidean space.
\(m\ge 1\) and \(\|n_i\|=1\) for every \(i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{(x_i,n_i)\}\) is realizable by \(C=\bigcap_i B(x_i-Rn_i,R)\) exactly when the stated pairwise inequalities hold.

notation.meaning: Closed Euclidean ball with center c and radius R.
Prescribed outward unit normal at the boundary point x_i.
Common supporting-ball radius; its reciprocal is the strong-convexity curvature parameter.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed inequalities correctly characterize containment in the particular balls centered at x_i-Rn_i, but the stated equivalence with an arbitrary set representable as an intersection of radius-R balls does not follow merely from n_i being an outward normal. It requires a precise supporting-ball definition under which the ball centered at x_i-Rn_i is required at each sampled normal. No source or locator establishes that convention or the necessity claim. The final sentence also contains proof-style justification, which should be removed when a sourced version is supplied.

children.title: Smooth Strongly Convex Set Regimes
children.top_down_role: Set interpolation under simultaneous smoothness and strong-convexity structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Smooth Strongly Convex Set Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-sided chord-normal curvature bounds for finite boundary data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(0<\mu\le L<\infty\). Boundary-normal data \(\{(x_i,n_i)\}_{i=1}^m\), with \(\|n_i\|=1\), satisfy the discrete \((\mu,L)\) smooth strongly convex regime when, for every \(i,j\),
\[
-\frac{L}{2}\|x_j-x_i\|^2
\le \langle n_i,x_j-x_i\rangle
\le -\frac{\mu}{2}\|x_j-x_i\|^2.
\]
The upper inequality imposes uniform strong supporting curvature, while the lower inequality excludes curvature exceeding \(L\). Coincident points must carry compatible prescribed normals whenever the intended smooth-set model requires a unique outward normal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A smooth strongly convex boundary-data regime is encoded by two-sided quadratic bounds on every normal–chord pairing, with curvature between mu and L.
assumptions_latex: \(0<\mu\le L<\infty\).
The data lie in finite-dimensional Euclidean space and each \(n_i\) is a unit vector.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The finite data obey the displayed two-sided \((\mu,L)\) chord-normal compatibility condition.

notation.meaning: Prescribed outward unit normal at x_i.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The two-sided inequalities are dimensionally consistent as a proposed finite-data condition, but their identification with a smooth strongly convex set regime depends on the exact global supporting-ball or curvature convention. In particular, an authoritative source is needed to determine whether these pairwise bounds are necessary, sufficient, or merely a chosen discrete condition. The current record appropriately avoids a realizability theorem, but its geometric interpretation remains source-dependent.

children.title: Projection-Data Interpolation
children.top_down_role: Finite-data realizability for projection observations associated with an unknown set.

knowledge_statements.title: Projection-Data Interpolation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finite interpolation of Euclidean projection observations by a closed convex set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For data \(\{(z_i,x_i)\}_{i=1}^m\subset\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb R^d\), there exists a nonempty closed convex set \(C\) satisfying \(x_i=P_C(z_i)\) for every \(i\) if and only if
\[
\langle z_i-x_i,x_j-x_i\rangle\le 0\qquad(i,j=1,\ldots,m).
\]
When these finitely checkable inequalities hold, one may take
\[
C=\operatorname{conv}\{x_1,\ldots,x_m\}.
\]
The inequalities state that each residual \(z_i-x_i\) belongs to the normal cone of this convex hull at \(x_i\), which is the variational characterization of Euclidean projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projection pairs are jointly realizable by a closed convex set exactly when every residual forms a nonpositive inner product with every anchored displacement.
assumptions_latex: The ambient space is finite-dimensional Euclidean space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_i=P_C(z_i)\) holds for all \(i\) for some closed convex \(C\) exactly under the displayed inequalities.

children.title: Normal-Data Interpolation
children.top_down_role: Finite-data realizability for normal-vector observations associated with an unknown set.

knowledge_statements.title: Normal-Data Interpolation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finite interpolation of convex-set normal-cone observations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(\{(x_i,n_i)\}_{i=1}^m\subset\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb R^d\), there exists a nonempty closed convex set \(C\) such that \(x_i\in C\) and \(n_i\in N_C(x_i)\) for every \(i\) if and only if
\[
\langle n_i,x_j-x_i\rangle\le 0\qquad(i,j=1,\ldots,m).
\]
If these inequalities hold, the explicit interpolant \(C=\operatorname{conv}\{x_1,\ldots,x_m\}\) is valid. Zero normals are allowed and encode no supporting direction beyond membership of the associated point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite point–normal data come from one closed convex set exactly when each proposed normal supports all sampled points at its associated anchor.
assumptions_latex: The ambient space is finite-dimensional Euclidean space.
\(m\ge 1\); prescribed normals may be zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exists closed convex \(C\) with \(n_i\in N_C(x_i)\) for every \(i\) exactly under the pairwise support inequalities.

notation.meaning: Convex-analytic normal cone to C at x.

children.title: Separation-Data Interpolation
children.top_down_role: Finite-data realizability for separating vectors or hyperplane records.

knowledge_statements.title: Separation-Data Interpolation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite compatibility certificate for anchored convex sets and prescribed strict separating halfspaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let anchor points \(x_1,\ldots,x_m\in\mathbb R^d\) and separation data \(\{(z_k,a_k,b_k)\}_{k=1}^r\) be given, with \(a_k\ne0\). A nonempty closed convex set \(C\) can contain every \(x_i\), lie in each halfspace \(\{x:\langle a_k,x\rangle\le b_k\}\), and strictly exclude each \(z_k\) through \(\langle a_k,z_k\rangle>b_k\) if and only if
\[
\langle a_k,x_i\rangle\le b_k<\langle a_k,z_k\rangle
\qquad(i=1,\ldots,m;\ k=1,\ldots,r).
\]
When feasible, \(C=\operatorname{conv}\{x_1,\ldots,x_m\}\) is an explicit interpolant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Anchors and proposed separating hyperplanes are compatible exactly when every anchor lies in each retained halfspace and each designated exterior point lies strictly beyond its hyperplane.
assumptions_latex: The ambient space is finite-dimensional Euclidean space.
\(m,r\ge1\) and \(a_k\ne0\) for every \(k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The stated convex-set separation data are realizable exactly when all displayed finite inequalities hold.

notation.meaning: Normal and offset defining the k-th closed halfspace.
Point required to be strictly separated from the interpolating set.

children.title: Geometric-Data Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Joint compatibility among projection, normal, and separation records for a common set.

knowledge_statements.title: Geometric-Data Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint feasibility of membership, projection, normal, and separation observations for one convex set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X=\{x_1,\ldots,x_m\}\subset\mathbb R^d\). Projection data \((z_p,x_{i(p)})\), normal data \((x_{i(q)},n_q)\), and halfspace data \((a_k,b_k,w_k)\) are jointly compatible whenever
\[
\langle z_p-x_{i(p)},x_j-x_{i(p)}\rangle\le0,
\quad
\langle n_q,x_j-x_{i(q)}\rangle\le0,
\quad
\langle a_k,x_j\rangle\le b_k<\langle a_k,w_k\rangle
\]
for every applicable index and every \(j\). Under these conditions, \(C=\operatorname{conv}X\) simultaneously realizes all membership, projection, normal, and strict-separation observations. Conversely, any realizing convex set containing precisely these required anchors forces the displayed inequalities on the anchors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Heterogeneous geometric observations are jointly compatible when their projection residuals, normals, and separators satisfy all corresponding inequalities against the common anchor set.
assumptions_latex: All observations use one finite-dimensional Euclidean space.
Each projection or normal observation is attached to an anchor in \(X\).
Every separator normal \(a_k\) is nonzero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The convex hull \(C=\operatorname{conv}X\) jointly realizes every listed observation under the displayed compatibility inequalities.

notation.meaning: Indices attaching observations to anchor points.
Point required to lie strictly outside the k-th separating halfspace.

children.title: Scaling Transformations
children.top_down_role: Effects of rescaling problem objects, oracle records, or interpolation parameters.

knowledge_statements.title: Scaling Transformations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive range scaling and nonzero scalar coordinate scaling of convex first-order interpolation data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb R^d\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be a proper convex function interpolating data \(\{(x_i,g_i,f_i)\}_{i=1}^m\), meaning that \(f(x_i)=f_i\) and \(g_i\in\partial f(x_i)\). For \(\alpha>0\) and \(\beta\ne0\), define \(h:\mathbb R^d\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) by \(h(y)=\alpha f(\beta y)\). Then \(h\) interpolates the transformed data
\[
y_i=\beta^{-1}x_i,
\qquad h_i=\alpha f_i,
\qquad s_i=\alpha\beta g_i.
\]
If \(f\) is differentiable, then \(s_i=\nabla h(y_i)\). If \(f\) has an \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient, then \(h\) has an \(\alpha\beta^2L\)-Lipschitz gradient; if \(f\) is \(\mu\)-strongly convex, then \(h\) is \(\alpha\beta^2\mu\)-strongly convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a proper convex interpolant, positive value scaling and nonzero scalar coordinate scaling transform sampled values and subgradients by explicit homogeneous rules; smoothness and strong-convexity parameters scale by alpha beta squared.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^d\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper and convex.
\(m\ge1\), \(\alpha>0\), and \(\beta\ne0\).
\(\partial f\) denotes the convex-analytic subdifferential.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The triples \((\beta^{-1}x_i,\alpha\beta g_i,\alpha f_i)\) are interpolated by \(h(y)=\alpha f(\beta y)\), with any stated smoothness or strong-convexity parameter scaled by \(\alpha\beta^2\).

children.title: Translation Transformations
children.top_down_role: Effects of shifting points, values, sets, or operators within realizability models.

knowledge_statements.title: Translation Transformations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Domain translation, vertical translation, and affine tilt of convex first-order interpolation data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb R^d\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be a proper convex function satisfying \(f(x_i)=f_i\) and \(g_i\in\partial f(x_i)\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\). For \(a,q\in\mathbb R^d\) and \(c\in\mathbb R\), define
\[
h(y)=f(y-a)+\langle q,y\rangle+c.
\]
At \(y_i=x_i+a\), define
\[
h_i=f_i+\langle q,x_i+a\rangle+c,
\qquad s_i=g_i+q.
\]
Then \(h(y_i)=h_i\) and \(s_i\in\partial h(y_i)\). Convexity is preserved; when applicable, differentiability, the gradient Lipschitz constant, and the strong-convexity parameter are also unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a proper convex interpolant, translating coordinates, shifting values, and adding an affine tilt gives explicit transformed values and subgradients while preserving convexity and any applicable smoothness or strong-convexity constants.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^d\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper and convex.
\(f(x_i)=f_i\) and \(g_i\in\partial f(x_i)\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\).
\(a,q\in\mathbb R^d\) and \(c\in\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The triples \((x_i+a,g_i+q,f_i+\langle q,x_i+a\rangle+c)\) are interpolated by \(h\).

notation.meaning: Slope of the added affine tilt.

children.title: Affine Transformations
children.top_down_role: Effects of general affine changes of variables or representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Affine Transformations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Invertible affine coordinate changes combined with positive range scaling and affine tilt for convex first-order data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb R^d\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be a proper convex function satisfying \(f(x_i)=f_i\) and \(g_i\in\partial f(x_i)\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\). Let \(A:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^d\) be invertible, let \(b,q\in\mathbb R^d\), \(c\in\mathbb R\), and \(\alpha>0\), and define
\[
h(y)=\alpha f(Ay+b)+\langle q,y\rangle+c.
\]
Then \(h\) interpolates
\[
y_i=A^{-1}(x_i-b),
\qquad h_i=\alpha f_i+\langle q,y_i\rangle+c,
\qquad s_i=\alpha A^*g_i+q.
\]
Convexity is preserved. If \(f\) has an \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient, then \(h\) has an \(\alpha L\|A\|^2\)-Lipschitz gradient. If \(f\) is \(\mu\)-strongly convex, then \(h\) is \(\alpha\mu\sigma_{\min}(A)^2\)-strongly convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An invertible affine coordinate change, positive value scaling, and affine tilt produce explicit transformed values and covectors; valid smoothness and strong-convexity parameters scale with the largest and smallest singular values of the coordinate map.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^d\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper and convex.
\(A:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^d\) is invertible and \(\alpha>0\).
\(b,q\in\mathbb R^d\) and \(c\in\mathbb R\).
Adjoints and operator norms are induced by the Euclidean inner product.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed transformed triples are interpolated by \(h\), with the stated valid smoothness and strong-convexity parameters whenever the corresponding properties hold for \(f\).

children.title: Transformation Invariants
children.top_down_role: Interpolation features preserved across scaling, translation, or affine changes.

knowledge_statements.title: Transformation Invariants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Invariant interpolation residuals under invertible affine coordinate and value transformations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x_i,g_i\in\mathbb R^d\), \(f_i\in\mathbb R\), let \(A:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^d\) be invertible, let \(b,q\in\mathbb R^d\), \(c\in\mathbb R\), and \(\alpha>0\). Define
\[
y_i=A^{-1}(x_i-b),
\quad s_i=\alpha A^*g_i+q,
\quad h_i=\alpha f_i+\langle q,y_i\rangle+c.
\]
Then every first-order affine residual satisfies
\[
h_i-h_j-\langle s_j,y_i-y_j\rangle
=\alpha\bigl(f_i-f_j-\langle g_j,x_i-x_j\rangle\bigr).
\]
Consequently, the sign and vanishing of each residual, as well as the validity of every homogeneous nonnegative linear combination of residual inequalities, are invariant under the transformation. Convex interpolation feasibility expressed solely through these inequalities is therefore unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An invertible affine transformation multiplies every basic first-order interpolation residual by the same positive factor, preserving its sign, equality status, and homogeneous residual certificates.
assumptions_latex: \(x_i,g_i\in\mathbb R^d\) and \(f_i\in\mathbb R\).
\(A:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^d\) is invertible and \(\alpha>0\).
\(b,q\in\mathbb R^d\) and \(c\in\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: First-order affine residual signs, equalities, and homogeneous residual certificates are invariant under the displayed transformation.

children.title: Sum Transformations
children.top_down_role: Transfer of interpolation records under aggregation of admissible components.

knowledge_statements.title: Sum Transformations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Aggregation of componentwise first-order interpolation data sharing common sample locations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(r\ge1\), suppose each function \(f^{(k)}\) interpolates data \(\{(x_i,g_i^{(k)},f_i^{(k)})\}_{i=1}^m\). Define
\[
f=\sum_{k=1}^r f^{(k)},
\qquad f_i=\sum_{k=1}^r f_i^{(k)},
\qquad g_i=\sum_{k=1}^r g_i^{(k)}.
\]
Whenever the convex subdifferential sum rule applies at every \(x_i\), the aggregate function satisfies \(f(x_i)=f_i\) and \(g_i\in\partial f(x_i)\). If every component is differentiable, no subdifferential qualification is needed. Component smoothness constants and strong-convexity parameters may be summed to obtain valid aggregate parameters.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Component functions sampled at common points can be summed by adding their values and first-order data; their smoothness and strong-convexity parameters also add.
assumptions_latex: All component data use the same sample locations \(x_i\).
Either every component is differentiable or a valid convex subdifferential sum-rule qualification holds.
All component functions are finite at the sampled points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The aggregate triples \((x_i,\sum_k g_i^{(k)},\sum_k f_i^{(k)})\) are interpolated by \(\sum_k f^{(k)}\).
