children.title: Linear-Matrix-Inequality Models
children.top_down_role: Performance models expressed through linear matrix inequality structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Linear-Matrix-Inequality Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine semidefinite models used to encode quadratic performance certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_0,F_1,\ldots,F_d\in\mathbb S^n\). An LMI model has decision vector \(\theta\in\mathbb R^d\) and feasibility predicate \[F(\theta):=F_0+\sum_{i=1}^d\theta_iF_i\preceq0.\] Additional scalar affine equalities and inequalities may be represented by symmetric block-diagonal components. In a performance-estimation certificate, the entries of \(\theta\) may include IQC multipliers, coefficients of a quadratic storage function, and a candidate performance bound. Feasibility is verifiable by checking the affine constraints and that every eigenvalue of \(F(\theta)\) is nonpositive, equivalently that \(-F(\theta)\) admits a positive-semidefinite factorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An LMI model requires an affine symmetric matrix in the decision variables to be negative semidefinite, possibly alongside affine scalar constraints.
assumptions_latex: \(F_i\in\mathbb S^n\) are fixed data matrices.
The dependence of \(F\) on \(\theta\) is affine.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The feasible set \(\{\theta\in\mathbb R^d:F(\theta)\preceq0\}\) is convex.

knowledge_statements.title: IQC-to-LMI Encodings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: State-space conversion of a filtered quadratic dissipation inequality into an LMI.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the augmented linear dynamics \(\eta_{k+1}=A\eta_k+Bw_k\) and filtered signal \(z_k=C\eta_k+Dw_k\). For \(P=P^\top\) and \(M=M^\top\), the pointwise inequality \[(A\eta+Bw)^\top P(A\eta+Bw)-\eta^\top P\eta+(C\eta+Dw)^\top M(C\eta+Dw)\leq0\] for every \((\eta,w)\) is equivalent to the LMI \[\begin{bmatrix}A^\top PA-P&A^\top PB\\B^\top PA&B^\top PB\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}C\\D\end{bmatrix}^\top M\begin{bmatrix}C&D\end{bmatrix}\preceq0.\] Summation converts this local LMI into a finite-horizon storage inequality; valid IQCs can then eliminate the accumulated quadratic supply.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A filtered IQC dissipation inequality is an LMI because its left side is a quadratic form in the augmented state and input.
assumptions_latex: The algorithm, oracle interconnection, and IQC filters admit the displayed finite-dimensional augmented realization.
\(P\) and \(M\) are symmetric.
The pointwise inequality is required for every augmented state and input.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(V(\eta_{N+1})-V(\eta_0)+\sum_{k=0}^{N}z_k^\top Mz_k\leq0\), where \(V(\eta)=\eta^\top P\eta\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: direct quadratic-form expansion underlying IQC-to-LMI conversion

An authoritative IQC/LMI source is also missing, so the intended realization and corrected formula cannot be source-verified.

knowledge_statements.title: Weighted Interpolation Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonnegative aggregation of finite interpolation inequalities in a semidefinite PEP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G\succeq0\) be the Gram matrix of sampled vectors, let \(f\in\mathbb R^s\) collect sampled function values, and suppose class interpolation is characterized by affine inequalities \(q_j(G,f)\geq0\) for \(j=1,\ldots,m\). For an affine performance measure \(t(G,f)\), a weighted interpolation certificate for the upper bound \(t(G,f)\leq\rho\) consists of \(\lambda_j\geq0\) and \(S\succeq0\) satisfying the affine identity \[\rho-t(G,f)=\sum_{j=1}^m\lambda_jq_j(G,f)+\langle S,G\rangle\] for all symmetric \(G\) and all \(f\). Every feasible interpolable data set makes the right-hand side nonnegative, thereby certifying the bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonnegative interpolation weights plus a positive-semidefinite Gram term certify an upper performance bound through an exact affine identity.
assumptions_latex: The listed inequalities completely describe interpolation for the sampled data under the chosen function class.
\(G\succeq0\) represents the sampled vectors.
The displayed equality holds coefficientwise in \((G,f)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(t(G,f)\leq\rho\) for every feasible interpolable data set \((G,f)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Matrix-Positivity Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Checkable positive-semidefinite witnesses for Gram-matrix terms in PEP dual bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G\succeq0\) be a primal Gram matrix and let a proposed dual identity contain the term \(\langle S,G\rangle\), where \(S=S^\top\). A matrix-positivity certificate is a factor \(L\) such that \[S=LL^\top.\] This equality is finitely checkable and implies \(S\succeq0\). Consequently, \[\langle S,G\rangle=\operatorname{tr}(L^\top GL)\geq0.\] Thus the matrix term in the dual identity cannot decrease its certified upper bound. An exact rational or symbolic factorization gives an exact certificate; a numerical factorization alone certifies only to the stated arithmetic tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Factoring a dual matrix as a matrix times its transpose proves positivity and makes its inner product with every Gram matrix nonnegative.
assumptions_latex: \(G\in\mathbb S^n\) satisfies \(G\succeq0\).
The supplied factorization \(S=LL^\top\) is exact, or its verification tolerance is recorded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S\succeq0\) and \(\langle S,G\rangle\geq0\).

Nevertheless, no source with a specific locator supports its use as a matrix-positivity component of a PEP dual certificate; the elementary standard-field rationale does not replace the requested citation at this review layer.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Dual Gap Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak-duality certificates bracketing the worst-case value of a semidefinite PEP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the primal PEP value \(p^*=\sup\{t(G,f):G\succeq0,\ q_j(G,f)\geq0\}\). Suppose \(\rho\), multipliers \(\lambda_j\geq0\), and \(S\succeq0\) satisfy \[\rho-t(G,f)=\sum_j\lambda_jq_j(G,f)+\langle S,G\rangle\] identically. Then \(p^*\leq\rho\). If \((\widehat G,\widehat f)\) is primal feasible with value \(\widehat t=t(\widehat G,\widehat f)\), the computable quantity \(\rho-\widehat t\) is a primal-dual gap certificate: \[0\leq p^*-\widehat t\leq\rho-\widehat t.\] A zero gap certifies simultaneous primal and dual optimality without requiring a separate convergence argument.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible example gives a lower bound and a feasible dual identity gives an upper bound; their difference certifies the remaining optimality gap.
assumptions_latex: The primal data \((\widehat G,\widehat f)\) satisfy all Gram and interpolation constraints.
The dual identity holds coefficientwise with \(\lambda_j\geq0\) and \(S\succeq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat t\leq p^*\leq\rho\), with certified gap at most \(\rho-\widehat t\).

knowledge_statements.title: One-Step Potentials
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A local Lyapunov inequality certifying progress across one algorithmic transition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(s_{k+1}=T_k(s_k,\omega_k)\) denote one admissible algorithm-oracle transition. A one-step potential certificate consists of functions \(\Phi_k,\Phi_{k+1}:\mathcal S\to\mathbb R\) and a progress quantity \(\Delta_k:\mathcal S\times\Omega\to\mathbb R_+\) such that \[\Phi_{k+1}(T_k(s,\omega))+\Delta_k(s,\omega)\leq\Phi_k(s)\] for every admissible \((s,\omega)\). If a target error \(E_{k+1}\) satisfies \(E_{k+1}(s_{k+1})\leq\Phi_{k+1}(s_{k+1})\), the inequality certifies \(E_{k+1}(s_{k+1})\leq\Phi_k(s_k)\) and quantifies the certified one-step decrease by \(\Delta_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A one-step potential bounds the next potential plus nonnegative progress by the current potential for every admissible transition.
assumptions_latex: The state space \(\mathcal S\), oracle data space \(\Omega\), and admissible transitions are fixed.
\(\Delta_k(s,\omega)\geq0\) on every admissible transition.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Horizon Potentials
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Potential sequences tailored to certify a performance target after a fixed number of steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a horizon \(N\geq1\). A finite-horizon potential certificate is a sequence \(\Phi_0^{(N)},\ldots,\Phi_N^{(N)}:\mathcal S\to\mathbb R\), nonnegative progress terms \(\Delta_k^{(N)}\), and a terminal error \(E_N\) satisfying, along every admissible trajectory, \[\Phi_{k+1}^{(N)}(s_{k+1})+\Delta_k^{(N)}\leq\Phi_k^{(N)}(s_k),\qquad 0\leq k<N,\] and \[E_N(s_N)\leq\Phi_N^{(N)}(s_N).\] Therefore \(E_N(s_N)+\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\Delta_k^{(N)}\leq\Phi_0^{(N)}(s_0)\). The sequence may depend on \(N\), so no uniform infinite-horizon potential is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A horizon-specific potential decreases at every step and dominates the terminal error, yielding a certified finite-horizon bound after telescoping.
assumptions_latex: \(N\) is a fixed positive integer.
Every local inequality holds for all trajectories admitted by the algorithm and oracle model.
Each \(\Delta_k^{(N)}\geq0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Local-to-Horizon Composition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Telescoping composition of compatible local potential inequalities over a finite horizon.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(N\geq1\), and suppose an admissible trajectory satisfies \[\Phi_{k+1}(s_{k+1})+\Delta_k\leq\Phi_k(s_k),\qquad k=0,\ldots,N-1,\] where every \(\Delta_k\geq0\). Then summing the inequalities cancels all intermediate potentials and gives \[\Phi_N(s_N)+\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\Delta_k\leq\Phi_0(s_0).\] If \(E_N(s_N)\leq\Phi_N(s_N)\), then \[E_N(s_N)+\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\Delta_k\leq\Phi_0(s_0).\] Compatibility requires the outgoing potential in the certificate for step \(k\) to be exactly the incoming potential used for step \(k+1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compatible one-step potential inequalities telescope, canceling intermediate terms and producing a finite-horizon performance certificate.
assumptions_latex: Each local inequality holds on the same admissible trajectory.

knowledge_statements.title: Time-Varying Potentials
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Step-indexed Lyapunov functions for methods with nonstationary parameters or oracle models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonstationary method \(s_{k+1}=T_k(s_k,\omega_k;\alpha_k)\), a time-varying potential is a sequence \(\{\Phi_k:\mathcal S\to\mathbb R\}_{k\geq0}\) for which there exist \(\Delta_k\geq0\) satisfying \[\Phi_{k+1}(s_{k+1})+\Delta_k(s_k,\omega_k)\leq\Phi_k(s_k)\] for every time \(k\) and every admissible transition at the scheduled parameter \(\alpha_k\). The functional form and coefficients of \(\Phi_k\) may vary with \(k\). Consequently, \(\Phi_N(s_N)+\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\Delta_k\leq\Phi_0(s_0)\) for every finite \(N\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A time-varying potential changes with the iteration index so its local decrease inequality can track a nonstationary parameter schedule.
assumptions_latex: The parameter schedule \(\{\alpha_k\}_{k\geq0}\) is fixed.
The local inequality holds for every transition admissible at time \(k\).
Each progress term is nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Phi_N(s_N)+\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\Delta_k\leq\Phi_0(s_0)\) for every \(N\geq1\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Regret Identity for Time-Varying Legendre Potentials
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact Bregman-divergence decomposition of comparator regret for the associated time-varying-potential linear forecaster.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix a regular loss function \(\ell\). If the gradient-based linear forecaster is run with the time-varying Legendre-potential construction and \(\nabla\Phi^*(\mathbf0)=\mathbf0\), then, for every \(\mathbf u\in\mathbb R^d\),
\[
R_n(\mathbf u)=D_{\Phi_0^*}(\mathbf u,\mathbf w_0)-D_{\Phi_n^*}(\mathbf u,\mathbf w_n)+\sum_{t=1}^nD_{\Phi_t^*}(\mathbf w_{t-1},\mathbf w_t).
\]

knowledge_statements.title: Horizon-Dependent Potentials
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Potential families whose coefficients depend on the prescribed terminal iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A horizon-dependent potential family assigns to every \(N\geq1\) functions \(\Phi_k^{(N)}:\mathcal S\to\mathbb R\) for \(0\leq k\leq N\). For the method under study, the family is certifying when \[\Phi_{k+1}^{(N)}(s_{k+1})\leq\Phi_k^{(N)}(s_k),\qquad 0\leq k<N,\] on every admissible trajectory and when the terminal target obeys \(E_N(s_N)\leq\Phi_N^{(N)}(s_N)\). Dependence on \(N\) is genuine: for some fixed \(k\), the functions \(\Phi_k^{(N)}\) may differ as \(N\) varies. Each chosen horizon nevertheless yields \(E_N(s_N)\leq\Phi_0^{(N)}(s_0)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A horizon-dependent potential is redesigned for each terminal iteration while still decreasing locally and dominating that horizon's target error.
assumptions_latex: A terminal horizon \(N\geq1\) is fixed before selecting the potential sequence.

knowledge_statements.title: Schedule–Horizon Coupling

knowledge_statements.title: State-Augmented Quadratic Lyapunov Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic certificate families on an augmented algorithmic state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z_k\in\mathbb{R}^m\) collect the iterate, auxiliary variables, and any fixed comparison point through affine coordinates. knowledge_statements.statement_title: State-Augmented Lyapunov Function for Nesterov Acceleration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A quadratic potential coupling consecutive iterate errors in the smooth strongly convex Nesterov method.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:

V_k=f(x^k)-f^*+\frac{L}{2}\left\|\widetilde{x}^k-\rho^2\widetilde{x}^{k-1}\right\|^2.

\alpha_k\equiv\frac1L,\qquad \beta_k\equiv\frac{\sqrt\kappa-1}{\sqrt\kappa+1},

\[
V_{k+1}\leq \rho^2V_k.
\]

knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic Potential Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Adapted potentials whose conditional drift controls stochastic optimization error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On a filtered probability space \((\Omega,\mathcal F,(\mathcal F_k),\mathbb P)\), a stochastic potential family is an adapted sequence \((\Phi_k)\) of integrable, nonnegative random variables together with adapted error measures \(E_k\geq0\) and deterministic coefficients \(a_k,b_k\geq0\) satisfying \(\mathbb E[\Phi_{k+1}\mid\mathcal F_k]\leq\Phi_k-a_kE_k+b_k\) almost surely. Iteration and total expectation give \(\mathbb E[\Phi_N]+\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}a_k\mathbb E[E_k]\leq\mathbb E[\Phi_0]+\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}b_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stochastic potential is an adapted nonnegative process whose conditional expected decrease pays for an error measure, up to an explicit additive budget.
assumptions_latex: \(\Phi_k,E_k\) are \(\mathcal F_k\)-measurable and integrable.
\(\Phi_k,E_k,a_k,b_k\geq0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Supermartingale Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonnegative supermartingale certificates for almost-sure and expectation control.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\Omega,\mathcal F,(\mathcal F_k),\mathbb P)\) be filtered. A supermartingale certificate family is an adapted integrable sequence \((M_k)\) with \(M_k\geq0\) and \(\mathbb E[M_{k+1}\mid\mathcal F_k]\leq M_k\) almost surely. More generally, if \(\mathbb E[M_{k+1}+D_k\mid\mathcal F_k]\leq M_k\) for an adapted \(D_k\geq0\), then \(\mathbb E[M_N]+\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\mathbb E[D_k]\leq\mathbb E[M_0]\), and the nonnegative supermartingale \((M_k)\) converges almost surely to a finite random variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative adapted process is a supermartingale certificate when its conditional expectation cannot increase; explicit decrements also yield a cumulative expectation bound.

\(M_k,D_k\geq0\) almost surely.

knowledge_statements.title: Expectation-Level Certificate Relations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expected-performance bounds obtained by telescoping conditional potential inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose integrable adapted variables satisfy \(\mathbb E[\Phi_{k+1}\mid\mathcal F_k]+a_k\mathbb E[E_{k+1}\mid\mathcal F_k]\leq\Phi_k+b_k\) almost surely, where \(a_k,b_k\geq0\) are deterministic and \(\Phi_k,E_k\geq0\). Taking expectations and summing from \(k=0\) to \(N-1\) certifies \(\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}a_k\mathbb E[E_{k+1}]\leq\mathbb E[\Phi_0]+\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}b_k\). If \(a_k>0\), it also certifies \(\min_{1\leq j\leq N}\mathbb E[E_j]\leq(\mathbb E[\Phi_0]+\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}b_k)/(\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}a_k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A conditional drift inequality telescopes into a weighted expected-error bound and, when weights are positive, a best-iterate expected-performance guarantee.
assumptions_latex: \(\Phi_k,E_k\) are nonnegative, adapted, and integrable.
\(a_k,b_k\geq0\) are deterministic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}a_k\mathbb E[E_{k+1}]\leq\mathbb E[\Phi_0]+\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}b_k\).

knowledge_statements.title: Classical Estimate Sequences
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nesterov's deterministic estimate-sequence convention for convex minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper and attain its minimum. A classical estimate sequence for \(F\) is a pair \(((\phi_k),(\lambda_k))\) with \(\lambda_k\geq0\), \(\lambda_k\to0\), and functions \(\phi_k:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) satisfying \(\phi_k(x)\leq(1-\lambda_k)F(x)+\lambda_k\phi_0(x)\) for every \(x\). If iterates obey \(F(x_k)\leq\inf_x\phi_k(x)\), then for every minimizer \(x_\star\), \(F(x_k)-F(x_\star)\leq\lambda_k(\phi_0(x_\star)-F(x_\star))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An estimate sequence globally underestimates a shrinking convex combination of the objective and an initial model, converting model domination into a convergence bound.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is proper and has a minimizer \(x_\star\).
\(\lambda_k\geq0\) and \(\lambda_k\to0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F(x_k)-F(x_\star)\leq\lambda_k(\phi_0(x_\star)-F(x_\star))\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record closely matches the classical estimate-sequence definition and its standard consequence, but no source or inspectable locator is supplied for this convention-sensitive definition.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Recursive Construction of a Classical Estimate Sequence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Construction using strongly convex first-order lower models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\in\mathcal S^{1,1}_{\mu,L}(\mathbb R^n)\), let \(\phi_0\) be an arbitrary function on \(\mathbb R^n\), let \(\{y_k\}_{k\ge0}\subset\mathbb R^n\), and let \(\alpha_k\in(0,1)\) satisfy \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\alpha_k=\infty\). Set \(\lambda_0=1\) and define \[\lambda_{k+1}=(1-\alpha_k)\lambda_k,\] \[\phi_{k+1}(x)=(1-\alpha_k)\phi_k(x)+\alpha_k\left[f(y_k)+\langle f'(y_k),x-y_k\rangle+\frac{\mu}{2}\|x-y_k\|^2\right].\] Then \((\{\phi_k\},\{\lambda_k\})\) is an estimate sequence for \(f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Averaging each estimate function with the strongly convex first-order lower model of f, using weights in (0,1) whose sum diverges, produces an estimate sequence.
assumptions_latex: f\in\mathcal S^{1,1}_{\mu,L}(\mathbb R^n)
\phi_0\text{ is an arbitrary function on }\mathbb R^n
y_k\in\mathbb R^n\quad(k\ge0)
\alpha_k\in(0,1),\quad \sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\alpha_k=\infty
\lambda_0=1
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (\{\phi_k\}_{k\ge0},\{\lambda_k\}_{k\ge0})\text{ is an estimate sequence for }f

children.title: Estimate Functions
children.top_down_role: Surrogate function families used to organize performance certificates.

knowledge_statements.title: Estimate Functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex lower models aggregated into a computable estimate function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper and convex, let \(m_i:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) satisfy \(m_i(x)\leq F(x)\) for every \(x\), and let \(a_i\geq0\) with \(A_k=\sum_{i=1}^k a_i>0\). Let \(d:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper and strongly convex, and assume \(\phi_k=d+\sum_{i=1}^k a_i m_i\) is proper. The function \(\phi_k\) is an estimate function and \(L_k=A_k^{-1}\inf_x\phi_k(x)\) is its normalized minimum. For every minimizer \(x_\star\) of \(F\) such that \(d(x_\star)<+\infty\), one has \(L_k-d(x_\star)/A_k\leq F(x_\star)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An estimate function aggregates weighted global lower models with a strongly convex regularizer. When the aggregate is proper and the regularizer is finite at a minimizer, its normalized minimum gives a regularized lower estimate of the optimum.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is proper and convex and has a minimizer \(x_\star\).
\(m_i(x)\leq F(x)\) for every \(x\) and \(i\).
\(a_i\geq0\), \(A_k>0\), \(d\) is proper and strongly convex, and \(\phi_k=d+\sum_{i=1}^k a_i m_i\) is proper.
\(d(x_\star)<+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A_k^{-1}\inf_x\phi_k(x)-A_k^{-1}d(x_\star)\leq F(x_\star)\).

notation.meaning: global lower model of the objective

children.title: Approximate Duality Gaps
children.top_down_role: Gap-based proof quantities comparing primal progress with lower-bound information.

knowledge_statements.title: Approximate Duality Gaps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Computable upper-minus-lower certificates with controlled lower-bound error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a convex minimization problem with optimum \(F_\star\), let \(U_k\) and \(L_k\) be computable quantities satisfying \(F(x_k)\leq U_k\) and \(L_k\leq F_\star+\varepsilon_k\), where \(\varepsilon_k\geq0\). The approximate duality gap is \(G_k=U_k-L_k+\varepsilon_k\). It is nonnegative and certifies \(F(x_k)-F_\star\leq G_k\). If \(L_k\leq F_\star\) exactly, one may set \(\varepsilon_k=0\), recovering the ordinary primal-upper-minus-dual-lower gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An approximate duality gap combines an upper objective bound, an inexact lower bound, and its error allowance to certify primal suboptimality.
assumptions_latex: \(F(x_k)\leq U_k\).
\(L_k\leq F_\star+\varepsilon_k\) with \(\varepsilon_k\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\leq F(x_k)-F_\star\leq U_k-L_k+\varepsilon_k=G_k\).

children.title: Gap-to-Estimate Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Structural translations between estimate-function and approximate-gap viewpoints.

knowledge_statements.title: Gap-to-Estimate Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic correspondence between estimate-function minima and upper-minus-lower gaps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A_k>0\), let \(\phi_k\) be an estimate function, and suppose \(B_k\) is known with \(B_k\geq d(x_\star)\). Define \(L_k=A_k^{-1}(\inf_x\phi_k(x)-B_k)\). Then any computable upper bound \(U_k\geq F(x_k)\) induces the gap \(G_k=U_k-L_k\), and \(L_k\leq F_\star\) implies \(F(x_k)-F_\star\leq G_k\). Conversely, any certified lower bound \(L_k\leq F_\star\) can be encoded by a constant estimate function \(\phi_k(x)=A_kL_k+B_k\), whose normalized minimum reproduces \(L_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The normalized minimum of an estimate function is a lower bound and therefore defines a gap; any lower bound can conversely be encoded by a constant estimate function.
assumptions_latex: \(A_k>0\) and \(U_k\geq F(x_k)\).
\(L_k=A_k^{-1}(\inf_x\phi_k(x)-B_k)\leq F_\star\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F(x_k)-F_\star\leq U_k-L_k=G_k\), with the converse encoding \(\phi_k(x)=A_kL_k+B_k\).

notation.meaning: lower bound extracted from the estimate

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The forward implication is a valid upper-minus-lower calculation. The converse calls an arbitrary constant function an estimate function, which may conflict with the structured or strongly convex estimate-function convention used by adjacent records. A source is required to determine and support the intended correspondence without weakening it.

children.title: Composite Estimate Mechanisms
children.top_down_role: Estimate constructions reflecting decomposed smooth and nonsmooth objectives.

knowledge_statements.title: Composite Estimate Mechanisms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Estimate functions built from smooth linearizations plus an exact nonsmooth term.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=f+\psi\), where \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) is convex and differentiable and \(\psi:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) is proper closed convex. For query points \(y_i\), define \(m_i(x)=f(y_i)+\langle\nabla f(y_i),x-y_i\rangle+\psi(x)\). Convexity gives \(m_i(x)\leq F(x)\). Thus \(\phi_k(x)=d(x)+\sum_{i=1}^k a_i m_i(x)\), with \(a_i\geq0\) and strongly convex \(d\), is a composite estimate function retaining \(\psi\) exactly while linearizing only \(f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A composite estimate aggregates affine lower models of the smooth term while retaining the nonsmooth term exactly, together with a strongly convex regularizer.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is convex and differentiable.
\(\psi\) is proper, closed, and convex.
\(a_i\geq0\) and \(d\) is strongly convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m_i(x)\leq F(x)\) and \(\phi_k(x)=d(x)+\sum_{i=1}^k a_i m_i(x)\) is a valid aggregate estimate.

knowledge_statements.title: Proximal Estimate Mechanisms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Computable minimization updates for strongly convex composite estimate functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) be symmetric with \(H\succ0\), define \(d(x)=\tfrac12\|x-x_0\|_H^2\), and let \(a_i>0\) and \(m_i:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper closed convex functions. Initialize \(\phi_0=d\). At iteration \(k\), set \(\phi_{k+1}(x)=\phi_k(x)+a_{k+1}m_{k+1}(x)\) and assume this aggregate is proper. Compute \(v_{k+1}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\phi_{k+1}(x)\). The proper closed strongly convex function \(\phi_{k+1}\) has a unique minimizer, so the update is well defined.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The mechanism adds a positively weighted closed convex lower model to a quadratic estimate and computes the unique minimizer of the resulting proper strongly convex aggregate.
assumptions_latex: \(H=H^{\mathsf T}\succ0\) and \(a_i>0\).
Each \(m_i\) is proper, closed, and convex.
Each aggregate \(\phi_{k+1}=d+\sum_{i=1}^{k+1}a_i m_i\) is proper.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v_{k+1}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\{d(x)+\sum_{i=1}^{k+1}a_i m_i(x)\}\) exists and is unique.

children.title: Composite–Proximal Coupling

knowledge_statements.title: Composite–Proximal Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coupling a composite upper iterate with a proximal estimate minimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=f+\psi\), let \(\phi_k\) be a composite estimate with cumulative weight \(A_k>0\), and let \(v_k=\operatorname*{argmin}_x\phi_k(x)\). Suppose \(B_k\geq d(x_\star)\) is known and define \(L_k=A_k^{-1}(\phi_k(v_k)-B_k)\). If the estimate construction ensures \(L_k\leq F_\star\), then any primal iterate \(x_k\) satisfying \(F(x_k)\leq U_k\) has the verifiable certificate \(F(x_k)-F_\star\leq U_k-L_k\). Hence the proximal estimate minimization and composite upper evaluation jointly certify accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proximal estimate minimum supplies a lower bound which, paired with a composite objective upper bound, gives a directly checkable suboptimality certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(A_k>0\), \(v_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_x\phi_k(x)\), and \(B_k\geq d(x_\star)\).
\(L_k\leq F_\star\) and \(F(x_k)\leq U_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F(x_k)-F_\star\leq U_k-A_k^{-1}(\phi_k(v_k)-B_k)\).

children.title: Fejer Mechanisms
children.top_down_role: Operator-geometric arguments based on exact distance monotonicity.

knowledge_statements.title: Fejer Mechanisms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact Fejér decrease relative to a nonempty solution set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) be a nonempty subset of a Hilbert space \(H\). A sequence \((x_k)\) has a Fejér certificate relative to \(C\) if, for every \(z\in C\), \(\|x_{k+1}-z\|^2\leq\|x_k-z\|^2-\delta_k\), where \(\delta_k\geq0\). Then \((\|x_k-z\|)\) is nonincreasing for every \(z\in C\), \((x_k)\) is bounded, and \(\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\delta_k\leq\|x_0-z\|^2\) for every horizon \(N\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fejér decrease makes every distance to the solution set nonincreasing and bounds the cumulative certified decrement by the initial squared distance.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subset H\) is nonempty.
\(\delta_k\geq0\) and the displayed inequality holds for every \(z\in C\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\delta_k\leq\|x_0-z\|^2\) and \((x_k)\) is bounded.

children.title: Quasi-Fejer Mechanisms
children.top_down_role: Operator-geometric arguments allowing controlled deviations from distance monotonicity.

knowledge_statements.title: Quasi-Fejer Mechanisms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Summable-error quasi-Fejér mechanism in a real Hilbert space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be a real Hilbert space, let \(C\subset H\) be nonempty, and let \((x_k)_{k\geq 0}\subset H\). Suppose there are sequences \((\eta_k)\), \((\varepsilon_k)\), and \((r_k)\) in \([0,\infty)\) such that \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\eta_k<\infty\), \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\varepsilon_k<\infty\), and, for every \(z\in C\), \[\|x_{k+1}-z\|^2+r_k\leq (1+\eta_k)\|x_k-z\|^2+\varepsilon_k.\] Then \((x_k)\) is bounded, \(\|x_k-z\|\) converges for every \(z\in C\), and \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}r_k<\infty\). If every weak cluster point of \((x_k)\) belongs to \(C\), then \((x_k)\) converges weakly to a point of \(C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Fejér inequality remains convergent under summable multiplicative and additive errors; its nonnegative residuals are summable, and a cluster-point condition yields weak convergence.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space and \(C\subset H\) is nonempty.
\(\eta_k,\varepsilon_k,r_k\geq 0\), with \(\sum_k\eta_k<\infty\) and \(\sum_k\varepsilon_k<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((x_k)\) is bounded, each distance \(\|x_k-z\|\) converges, and \(\sum_k r_k<\infty\); the stated cluster-point condition implies weak convergence into \(C\).

children.title: Perturbation-Tolerance Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Error regimes separating exact Fejer behavior from quasi-Fejer behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Perturbation-Tolerance Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Vanishing but nonsummable additive errors need not preserve Fejér convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Summability cannot generally be replaced by pointwise decay. Let \(H=\mathbb{R}\), \(C=\{0\}\), \(x_0=0\), and \(x_{k+1}=x_k+e_k\), where \(e_k=1/(k+1)\). Then \(e_k\to 0\), but \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}e_k=\infty\) and \[x_k=\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}\frac{1}{j+1}\longrightarrow +\infty.\] Thus even an iteration perturbed by errors whose norms vanish can be unbounded. Consequently, a quasi-Fejér certificate based only on \(\|e_k\|\to 0\), without summability, cancellation, or a stronger stability estimate, does not certify convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Vanishing errors are not enough: harmonic perturbations tend to zero but accumulate without bound, so convergence requires summability, cancellation, or stronger stability.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Although \(e_k\to 0\), one has \(x_k\to +\infty\); pointwise error decay alone does not preserve convergence.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The harmonic-error counterexample is correct, self-checkable, and appropriately classified as a failure boundary, but the record supplies no source or explicit standard-field rationale as required for the nontrivial perturbation-tolerance claim.

children.title: Averagedness Mechanisms
children.top_down_role: Proof mechanisms based on averaged-operator structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Averagedness Mechanisms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-decrease characterization of averaged mappings on Hilbert space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be a real Hilbert space and let \(T:H\to H\). For \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), the operator \(T\) is \(\alpha\)-averaged, meaning \(T=(1-\alpha)I+\alpha R\) for some nonexpansive \(R\), if and only if, for all \(x,y\in H\), \[\|Tx-Ty\|^2+\frac{1-\alpha}{\alpha}\|(I-T)x-(I-T)y\|^2\leq \|x-y\|^2.\] Hence, if \(z\in\operatorname{Fix}T\), then \[\|Tx-z\|^2\leq \|x-z\|^2-\frac{1-\alpha}{\alpha}\|x-Tx\|^2,\] which supplies a directly checkable Fejér-decrease certificate for the fixed-point iteration \(x_{k+1}=Tx_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Averagedness is equivalent to nonexpansiveness plus a quantified residual decrease, producing a Fejér certificate for fixed-point iteration.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space and \(T:H\to H\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed two-point inequality characterizes \(\alpha\)-averagedness and yields quantified decrease relative to every \(z\in\operatorname{Fix}T\).

children.title: Nonexpansiveness Mechanisms
children.top_down_role: Proof mechanisms based on distance-preserving or distance-contracting operator behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonexpansiveness Mechanisms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distance propagation and fixed-point Fejér monotonicity for nonexpansive operators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be a real Hilbert space and let \(T:H\to H\) satisfy \(\|Tx-Ty\|\leq\|x-y\|\) for all \(x,y\in H\). Then every pair of trajectories \(x_{k+1}=Tx_k\) and \(y_{k+1}=Ty_k\) satisfies \(\|x_k-y_k\|\leq\|x_0-y_0\|\). In particular, for every \(z\in\operatorname{Fix}T\), \[\|x_{k+1}-z\|\leq\|x_k-z\|.\] Thus nonexpansiveness certifies Fejér monotonicity with respect to the fixed-point set, but by itself supplies no strictly positive residual term and therefore does not alone imply asymptotic regularity or convergence of the iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonexpansiveness prevents distances from increasing and gives Fejér monotonicity to fixed points, but alone provides no strict residual decrease.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space.
\(T:H\to H\) is nonexpansive and \(x_{k+1}=Tx_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(z\in\operatorname{Fix}T\), \(\|x_{k+1}-z\|\leq\|x_k-z\|\).

children.title: Averaged-Operator Regimes
children.top_down_role: Regimes linking averaged representations to nonexpansive behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Averaged-Operator Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parameter regimes for relaxation of an averaged fixed-point operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T:H\to H\) be \(\alpha\)-averaged on a real Hilbert space, with \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), and define the relaxed operator \(T_{\lambda}=(1-\lambda)I+\lambda T\). If \(0<\lambda<1/\alpha\), then \(T_{\lambda}\) is \(\lambda\alpha\)-averaged and, for every \(z\in\operatorname{Fix}T\), \[\|T_{\lambda}x-z\|^2\leq\|x-z\|^2-\frac{1-\lambda\alpha}{\lambda\alpha}\|x-T_{\lambda}x\|^2.\] At \(\lambda=1/\alpha\), the operator is guaranteed only to be nonexpansive; for \(\lambda>1/\alpha\), averagedness and the positive residual coefficient are not guaranteed by the averagedness of \(T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relaxation preserves averagedness precisely in the guaranteed regime between zero and the reciprocal averaging parameter; the boundary loses strict residual decrease.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space and \(T\) is \(\alpha\)-averaged.
\(T_{\lambda}=(1-\lambda)I+\lambda T\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The guaranteed averaged regime is \(0<\lambda<1/\alpha\); \(\lambda=1/\alpha\) gives only nonexpansiveness, and larger relaxation lacks this guarantee.

children.title: Monotonicity Mechanisms
children.top_down_role: Operator-geometric certificates based on monotone relations.

knowledge_statements.title: Monotonicity Mechanisms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inner-product inequalities generated by monotone operator graph pairs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be a real Hilbert space and let \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\) be monotone. For any graph pairs \((x,u),(y,v)\in\operatorname{gra}A\), \[\langle x-y,u-v\rangle\geq 0.\] Consequently, whenever an algorithmic relation produces \(u\in Ax\), \(v\in Ay\), and a weighted identity containing the cross term \(-2\gamma\langle x-y,u-v\rangle\) with \(\gamma\geq0\), monotonicity certifies that this term is nonpositive and may be discarded in an upper bound. If \((z,0)\in\operatorname{gra}A\), it also gives \(\langle x-z,u\rangle\geq0\), the basic operator-geometric certificate relative to a zero of \(A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Monotonicity turns pairs of graph relations into nonnegative inner products, allowing adverse cross terms to be removed from quadratic performance bounds.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space.
\(A:H\rightrightarrows H\) is monotone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Graph pairs satisfy \(\langle x-y,u-v\rangle\geq0\), and a zero \(z\) satisfies \(\langle x-z,u\rangle\geq0\) for every \(u\in Ax\).

notation.meaning: set of points whose operator value contains zero

children.title: Cocoercivity Mechanisms
children.top_down_role: Operator-geometric certificates exploiting cocoercive structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Cocoercivity Mechanisms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cocoercivity converts operator differences into quantified forward-step decrease.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be a real Hilbert space and let \(B:H\to H\) be \(\beta\)-cocoercive for some \(\beta>0\), so that \[\langle Bx-By,x-y\rangle\geq\beta\|Bx-By\|^2\] for all \(x,y\in H\). For \(T=I-\gamma B\) and \(0<\gamma<2\beta\), direct expansion gives \[\|Tx-Ty\|^2\leq\|x-y\|^2-\gamma(2\beta-\gamma)\|Bx-By\|^2.\] Equivalently, \(T\) is \(\gamma/(2\beta)\)-averaged. If \(Bz=0\), the same inequality with \(y=z\) is a quantified Fejér certificate for the forward iteration \(x_{k+1}=x_k-\gamma Bx_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cocoercivity yields a strict quadratic decrease for forward steps whenever the step size lies between zero and twice the cocoercivity constant.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space and \(B:H\to H\) is \(\beta\)-cocoercive.
\(0<\gamma<2\beta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(I-\gamma B\) is \(\gamma/(2\beta)\)-averaged and satisfies the displayed quantified decrease inequality.

children.title: Resolvent Mechanisms
children.top_down_role: Operator-geometric certificates organized around resolvent mappings.

knowledge_statements.title: Resolvent Mechanisms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Firm nonexpansiveness certificate for resolvents of maximally monotone operators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be a real Hilbert space, let \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\) be maximally monotone, and let \(\gamma>0\). Its resolvent \(J_{\gamma A}=(I+\gamma A)^{-1}\) is everywhere defined, single-valued, and firmly nonexpansive: for all \(x,y\in H\), \[\|J_{\gamma A}x-J_{\gamma A}y\|^2+\|(I-J_{\gamma A})x-(I-J_{\gamma A})y\|^2\leq\|x-y\|^2.\] Moreover, \(\operatorname{Fix}J_{\gamma A}=\operatorname{zer}A\). Hence, for \(z\in\operatorname{zer}A\), one resolvent step \(x^+=J_{\gamma A}x\) satisfies \(\|x^+-z\|^2+\|x-x^+\|^2\leq\|x-z\|^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A maximally monotone resolvent is firmly nonexpansive, has the operator zeros as fixed points, and supplies a squared-step Fejér decrease.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space and \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\) is maximally monotone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(J_{\gamma A}\) is firmly nonexpansive, \(\operatorname{Fix}J_{\gamma A}=\operatorname{zer}A\), and each resolvent step satisfies the displayed Fejér inequality.

A symmetric matrix \(M\) defines a hard finite-horizon integral quadratic constraint when \[\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}z_k^{\mathsf T}Mz_k\geq0\qquad\text{for every }N\geq1.\] Suppose a nonnegative storage sequence satisfies \[V_{k+1}-\rho^2V_k+p_k+\lambda z_k^{\mathsf T}Mz_k\leq0,\] where \(0
earrowho\leq1\), \(p_k\geq0\), and \(\lambda\geq0\). Summing and invoking the hard IQC certifies \(V_N+\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\rho^{2(N-1-k)}p_k\leq\rho^{2N}V_0\) when the correspondingly weighted IQC is valid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A filtered quadratic constraint, combined with a storage inequality, certifies a finite-horizon bound on storage and accumulated performance.
assumptions_latex: \(M=M^{\mathsf T}\) and the filtered signals satisfy the stated hard, correspondingly weighted IQC.
\(V_k\geq0\), \(p_k\geq0\), \(\lambda\geq0\), and \(0<\rho\leq1\).

children.title: Dissipativity Certificates
children.top_down_role: Control-theoretic certificates organized through supply and storage structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Dissipativity Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-horizon performance certificate obtained by telescoping a dissipation inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a discrete-time system \(x_{k+1}=F(x_k,u_k)\), an output \(y_k=G(x_k,u_k)\), a supply rate \(s(u_k,y_k)\), and a storage function \(V:X\to[0,\infty)\). If every admissible transition satisfies \[V(x_{k+1})-V(x_k)\leq s(u_k,y_k),\] then every trajectory and every horizon \(N\geq1\) satisfy \[V(x_N)-V(x_0)\leq\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}s(u_k,y_k).\] Thus the function \(V\), together with a verifiable one-step dissipation inequality, is a certificate for the accumulated supply bound. If \(s=-p\) with \(p\geq0\), it certifies \(\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}p_k\leq V(x_0)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative storage function satisfying a one-step dissipation inequality certifies an accumulated finite-horizon performance bound by telescoping.
assumptions_latex: \(x_{k+1}=F(x_k,u_k)\) and \(y_k=G(x_k,u_k)\) define admissible trajectories.
\(V:X\to[0,\infty)\) satisfies the stated one-step inequality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(N\geq1\), \(V(x_N)-V(x_0)\leq\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}s(u_k,y_k)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The telescoping dissipation certificate and the specialization to a nonnegative performance expenditure are mathematically standard and the certificate kind fits the leaf, but no source or standard-field rationale is supplied.

children.title: State-Space Certificates
children.top_down_role: Certificates expressed through state, transition, input, or output representations.

knowledge_statements.title: State-Space Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic LMI certificate for an LTI realization interconnected with a quadratic constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_{k+1}=Ax_k+Bu_k\) and \(z_k=Cx_k+Du_k\), and suppose admissible pairs satisfy \(z_k^{\mathsf T}Mz_k\geq0\). If there exist \(P\succeq0\), \(\lambda\geq0\), and \(0<\rho\leq1\) such that \[\begin{bmatrix}A&B\end{bmatrix}^{\mathsf T}P\begin{bmatrix}A&B\end{bmatrix}-\rho^2\begin{bmatrix}P&0\\0&0\end{bmatrix}+\lambda\begin{bmatrix}C&D\end{bmatrix}^{\mathsf T}M\begin{bmatrix}C&D\end{bmatrix}\preceq0,\] then \(V(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Px\) satisfies \(V(x_{k+1})\leq\rho^2V(x_k)\). For \(P\succ0\) and \(\rho<1\), this certifies exponential decay of the state in the \(P\)-norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible quadratic matrix inequality combines system dynamics and a quadratic constraint to certify contraction of a quadratic state storage.
assumptions_latex: \(x_{k+1}=Ax_k+Bu_k\) and \(z_k=Cx_k+Du_k\).
Admissible signals satisfy \(z_k^{\mathsf T}Mz_k\geq0\).
The displayed LMI is feasible with \(P\succeq0\), \(\lambda\geq0\), and \(0<\rho\leq1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The quadratic storage \(V(x)=x^{\mathsf T}Px\) obeys \(V(x_{k+1})\leq\rho^2V(x_k)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed LMI is consistent with the stated pointwise quadratic-constraint sign convention, but that convention requires authoritative support and no source is provided. The record should also state the symmetry of the quadratic multiplier matrix M. These details affect the exact certificate formulation.

children.title: Storage-Function Interpretations
children.top_down_role: Storage-based interpretations connecting dissipativity to state-space performance analysis.

knowledge_statements.title: Storage-Function Interpretations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Storage as recoverable potential and telescoping representation of performance expenditure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(V:X\to[0,\infty)\) and let \(p_k\geq0\) be a performance quantity along an admissible trajectory. The one-step certificate \[V(x_{k+1})-V(x_k)+p_k\leq0\] represents the decrease of stored potential as payment for performance expenditure. It is equivalent, after summation over \(k=0,\ldots,N-1\), to \[\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}p_k\leq V(x_0)-V(x_N)\leq V(x_0).\] More generally, with supply \(s_k\), the inequality \(V(x_{k+1})-V(x_k)\leq s_k\) represents the accumulated bound \(V(x_N)-V(x_0)\leq\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}s_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Storage is potential that pays for performance: its one-step decrease represents, by telescoping, a bound on total expenditure.
assumptions_latex: \(V:X\to[0,\infty)\).
\(p_k\geq0\) and the stated one-step storage inequality holds along every admissible transition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(N\geq1\), \(\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}p_k\leq V(x_0)-V(x_N)\leq V(x_0)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The storage interpretation and telescoped bounds are standard, but no source is supplied. In addition, summation makes the one-step inequality imply the finite-horizon inequality; literal equivalence requires the bound to hold for every shifted admissible trajectory and one-step horizon. The state domain X is also not introduced as a set or space.

knowledge_statements.title: Sum-of-Squares Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polynomial certificate for a performance-estimation inequality on a basic semialgebraic feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K=\{z\in\mathbb R^n:g_i(z)\ge 0,\ i=1,\ldots,m;\ h_j(z)=0,\ j=1,\ldots,r\}\), and let \(p\in\mathbb R[z]\) be the desired performance gap. An SOS certificate of degree at most \(2d\) is an identity \[p(z)=\sigma_0(z)+\sum_{i=1}^m\sigma_i(z)g_i(z)+\sum_{j=1}^r\tau_j(z)h_j(z),\] where each \(\sigma_i\) is a sum-of-squares polynomial, each \(\tau_j\in\mathbb R[z]\), and every summand has degree at most \(2d\). The identity certifies \(p(z)\ge 0\) for every \(z\in K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact polynomial identity combining SOS multipliers for inequalities and arbitrary multipliers for equalities certifies nonnegativity of the performance gap on the feasible set.
assumptions_latex: \(g_i,h_j,p\in\mathbb R[z]\).
The displayed polynomial identity holds coefficientwise.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p(z)\ge 0\) for all \(z\in K\).

Polynomial performance gap to be certified nonnegative.

children.title: Certificate Recovery Verification System
children.top_down_role: Post-solution routes from numerical dual data to independently checkable proof artifacts.

knowledge_statements.title: Numerical Dual-Certificate Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recovery of an approximately feasible dual certificate from floating-point conic-solver output.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given conic data \((A,b,c,K)\), a tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\), an asserted upper bound \(U\in\mathbb R\), and a numerical dual pair \((\widetilde y,\widetilde s)\), compute the residual \(r=A^*\widetilde y-c-\widetilde s\). Correct \(\widetilde s\) to obtain \(s\in K^*\), solve a refinement problem for \(\Delta y\) that reduces \(A^*(\widetilde y+\Delta y)-c-s\), and set \(y=\widetilde y+\Delta y\). Accept \((y,s)\) only if \[\lVert A^*y-c-s\rVert\le\varepsilon,\qquad s\in K^*,\qquad b^Ty\le U+\varepsilon.\] Otherwise report recovery failure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Correct and refine a floating-point dual solution, enforce dual-cone membership, and accept it only after explicit residual and objective checks at the prescribed tolerance.
assumptions_latex: The primal performance-estimation problem has conic form \(\sup\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\in K\}\).
Projection onto, or membership testing for, \(K^*\) is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Acceptance produces an \(\varepsilon\)-feasible numerical dual witness satisfying \(b^Ty\le U+\varepsilon\); without an additional residual-error bound, this is not an exact proof that the primal value is at most \(U+\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: Dual cone of the primal conic constraint.
Asserted upper bound on primal performance.

children.title: Symbolic Certificate Reconstruction

knowledge_statements.title: Symbolic Certificate Reconstruction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reconstruction of an exact symbolic identity from a numerically discovered certificate template.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given numerical coefficients \(\widetilde c\in\mathbb R^q\), a symbolic basis \(B=(B_1,\ldots,B_q)\), and exact certificate equations \(F(c)=0\), first identify candidate rational or algebraic values for the entries of \(\widetilde c\). Substitute the candidates to obtain \(c\), solve any remaining exact linear equations, and expand \[C(c)=\sum_{k=1}^q c_kB_k.\] Output \(C(c)\) only if exact arithmetic verifies \(F(c)=0\) and every required sign, cone, or sum-of-squares constraint; otherwise return reconstruction failure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recognize exact coefficients suggested by numerical data, solve the remaining symbolic equations, and output the certificate only after exact feasibility checks.
assumptions_latex: The numerical vector \(\widetilde c\) is accompanied by a fixed symbolic basis \(B\).
The exact certificate constraints \(F(c)=0\) and side conditions are decidable in the chosen coefficient field.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A successful output is an exactly verified symbolic certificate \(C(c)\).

notation.meaning: Fixed symbolic basis elements for the certificate.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits symbolic reconstruction, and its exact post-verification condition is sound. A source is required to determine the intended recognition method and coefficient field.

children.title: Exact Certificate Recovery

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Certificate Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exactification of a numerical conic certificate by projection onto an exact feasible affine-conic set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the exact certificate set be \(\mathcal C=\{u\in\mathbb F^q:Mu=d,\ u\in\mathcal K\}\), where \(\mathbb F\) is an exact ordered field and \(\mathcal K\) encodes all sign or structured-cone constraints. Given \(\widetilde u\in\mathbb R^q\), reconstruct a candidate \(u_0\in\mathbb F^q\), project \(u_0\) onto the affine space \(Mu=d\) using exact arithmetic, and test membership in \(\mathcal K\). Return the resulting \(u\) only when \(Mu=d\) and \(u\in\mathcal K\) hold exactly; otherwise return failure rather than a certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recover exact coefficients near a numerical solution, enforce all affine equations exactly, and return a certificate only after exact cone-membership verification.
assumptions_latex: The certificate equations \(M\) and \(d\) have entries in \(\mathbb F\).
Exact membership in \(\mathcal K\) can be checked.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Successful recovery returns \(u\in\mathcal C\); an unverified approximation is never returned as exact.

notation.meaning: Chosen exact ordered coefficient field, commonly the rationals or a real algebraic extension.
Exact cone or structured positivity constraints.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits exact certificate recovery, but exact affine projection and structured-cone membership depend on field- and cone-specific conditions that are not sourced.

children.title: Rational-Algebraic Recognition Regimes

knowledge_statements.title: Rational-Algebraic Recognition Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions distinguishing rational recovery from recovery over a real algebraic number field.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\widetilde c\in\mathbb R^q\) approximate exact certificate coefficients. Rational recognition is admissible when prescribed height bounds \(H_k\) and error bounds satisfy \[|\widetilde c_k-p_k/q_k|<\delta_k,\qquad |p_k|,|q_k|\le H_k,\quad q_k\ne0,\] with a unique candidate \(p_k/q_k\) for every \(k\). Algebraic recognition is admissible when each coefficient has a unique real algebraic candidate \(\alpha_k\) of prescribed degree and height within \(\delta_k\), together with an isolating interval. In either regime, recognition becomes a certificate only after exact substitution verifies all certificate identities and inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use rational or algebraic recognition only under uniqueness and size bounds, then verify every recovered identity and inequality exactly.
assumptions_latex: Explicit approximation tolerances and coefficient height bounds are fixed.
Algebraic candidates, when used, have exact defining polynomials and isolating intervals.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Successful exact substitution yields a certificate over \(\mathbb Q\) or a specified real algebraic extension.

notation.meaning: Prescribed numerator, denominator, or algebraic-height bound.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits the recognition-regime leaf, but the rational and algebraic uniqueness criteria are not quantitatively specified or supported by a number-theoretic source.

children.title: Certificate Interpretation
children.top_down_role: Organization of certificate components into recognizable analytic mechanisms.

knowledge_statements.title: Certificate Interpretation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reading a dual performance-estimation certificate as a weighted aggregation of valid primitive inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I_k(z)\ge0\), \(k=1,\ldots,m\), be primitive interpolation, algorithmic, or initial-condition inequalities valid for every feasible instance. A dual certificate interprets the target gap \(G(z)=U-P(z)\) through the identity \[G(z)=\sum_{k=1}^m\lambda_k I_k(z)+R(z),\qquad \lambda_k\ge0,\qquad R(z)\ge0.\] The support \(\{k:\lambda_k>0\}\) identifies the primitive inequalities used by the proof, their coefficients give the aggregation weights, and \(R\) records residual cone positivity. Exact verification of the identity makes the interpretation a valid proof of \(P(z)\le U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dual certificate is interpretable as a nonnegative weighted sum of primitive valid inequalities plus a nonnegative residual establishing the target bound.
assumptions_latex: Every primitive inequality \(I_k(z)\ge0\) is valid on the performance-estimation feasible set.
The residual \(R(z)\) is verifiably nonnegative there.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P(z)\le U\) for every feasible \(z\).

notation.meaning: Primitive valid inequality used in the proof.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind and nonnegative aggregation interpretation fit the leaf, but no source supports the asserted PEP certificate decomposition or the intended primitive inequality classes.

children.title: Sparsity–Interpretability Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Structural tradeoffs between compact certificate support and explanatory clarity.

knowledge_statements.title: Sparsity–Interpretability Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bicriteria principle separating certificate validity from structural simplicity and numerical robustness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a valid certificate coefficient vector \(u\in\mathcal C\), define support size \(s(u)=|\{k:u_k\ne0\}|\) and verification margin \(\rho(u)\), the minimum slack in its required positivity constraints. Certificate selection is naturally bicriteria: minimize \(s(u)\) while maximizing \(\rho(u)\) and preserving the certified value. A certificate \(u\) is Pareto efficient when no \(v\in\mathcal C\) satisfies \[s(v)\le s(u),\qquad \rho(v)\ge\rho(u),\] with at least one strict inequality. Thus sparsity alone does not mathematically imply either easier interpretation or greater numerical reliability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Certificate selection balances support size against positivity margin; a sparsest certificate need not be the most interpretable or numerically robust.
assumptions_latex: All compared certificates belong to the same feasible certificate set \(\mathcal C\).
They certify the same performance value under a fixed representation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The undominated choices form a Pareto frontier in \((s,-\rho)\).

notation.meaning: Minimum verification slack or positivity margin.
Certificates proving the fixed target bound.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle kind fits the tradeoff leaf, but the chosen positivity margin is not canonical and no source connects the proposed bicriteria model to interpretability or numerical reliability.

knowledge_statements.title: Independent Certificate Checking
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Verification of a recovered certificate directly from authoritative problem data without trusting the producing solver.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given original conic data \((A,b,c,K)\), an asserted upper bound \(U\in\mathbb R\), a candidate dual vector \(y\), and a candidate dual slack \(s\), independently recompute \[r=A^*y-c-s,\qquad v=b^Ty.\] Under exact arithmetic, accept the certificate only if \(r=0\), \(s\in K^*\), and \(v\le U\). Under interval arithmetic, accept as rigorous only if the computed enclosures certify these same conditions. A tolerance-only check must be reported as numerical validation unless an explicit residual-error bound converts it into a rigorous upper bound. Every outcome records the arithmetic regime, tolerances, and any failed condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independently recompute dual feasibility, dual-cone membership, and the objective bound from authoritative problem data. Exact or rigorous interval acceptance proves the bound; an unqualified tolerance check provides only numerical validation.
assumptions_latex: The primal problem is \(\sup\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\in K\}\).
The checker has authoritative access to \(A,b,c,K\) and can verify membership in \(K^*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact or rigorous interval acceptance certifies \(c^Tx\le U\) for every primal-feasible \(x\).

notation.meaning: Dual cone used in the independently checked dual constraint.
Asserted upper bound on the primal objective.

children.title: Worst-Case Tightness
children.top_down_role: Extremal geometries, reconstruction mechanisms, and distinctions among finite-horizon, asymptotic, and oracle-level tightness.
