intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the leaf, but the response-relation formulation, adaptive information convention, and exclusions of stronger information require a direct oracle-complexity source with a specific locator.

children.title: Common Oracle Cost Model
children.top_down_role: Shared accounting convention for oracle calls or primitive operations.

knowledge_statements.title: Common Oracle Cost Model
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a shared accounting rule for heterogeneous oracle calls.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathfrak O\) be the permitted oracle types and let \(c:\mathfrak O\to(0,\infty)\) assign each call type a fixed cost. For a transcript containing calls \(O_1,\ldots,O_T\), define its oracle cost by \[C(O_1,\ldots,O_T)=\sum_{t=1}^{T}c(O_t).\] Two methods use a common oracle cost model when the same set \(\mathfrak O\), weights \(c\), batching convention, and treatment of failed or repeated calls apply to both. Query complexity is then the least worst-case cost required to meet the common accuracy criterion, rather than an unqualified iteration count.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Both methods must price every permitted oracle call using the same weights and batching rules; complexity is measured by total priced calls.
assumptions_latex: Every permitted oracle type has a positive finite assigned cost.
Both methods use the same call-accounting convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The resource consumed by either method is measured by the common functional \(C=\sum_{t=1}^{T}c(O_t)\).

notation.meaning: cost of one call to oracle type O
total oracle cost of a transcript

review_flags: no supplied source directly supports the heterogeneous oracle-cost formalization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The selected definition role fits the container, but no cited source supports the weighted heterogeneous-call model, its batching conventions, or the identification of query complexity with least worst-case priced cost.

children.title: Strength-Cost Calibration
children.top_down_role: Alignment between information supplied per query plus charged query cost.

knowledge_statements.title: Strength-Cost Calibration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Calibrates oracle information by the cost of uniform simulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(O_s\) and \(O_w\) be strong and weak oracle models on the same problem class. Suppose every call to \(O_s\), including its response distribution or adversarial response set, can be simulated using at most \(k\) calls to \(O_w\) and method-independent local computation. If one \(O_s\)-call costs \(c_s\) and one \(O_w\)-call costs \(c_w\), consistent calibration requires \(c_s\le k c_w\). Consequently, any algorithm using at most \(T\) calls to \(O_s\) has a simulated implementation of oracle cost at most \(kTc_w\) in the weak model, with the same output law or worst-case guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stronger oracle should cost no more than the uniformly bounded weak-oracle simulation that reproduces each of its responses.
assumptions_latex: The simulation is uniform over the common problem class and all admissible query histories.
Local computation is either free in both models or charged identically.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A \(T\)-call strong-oracle guarantee transfers to weak-oracle cost at most \(kTc_w\), and calibration requires \(c_s\le kc_w\).

notation.meaning: maximum weak calls per simulated strong call

review_flags: uniform oracle-simulation principle needs a direct oracle-complexity source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A direct source is required for the uniform oracle-simulation transfer and for the normative inequality c_s <= k c_w. Simulation establishes a weak-oracle implementation cost bound, but the asserted requirement on assigned prices depends on a separately specified calibration convention.

children.title: Oracle Incomparability Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Cases where differing information models prevent a valid complexity comparison.

knowledge_statements.title: Oracle Incomparability Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifies when oracle guarantees cannot be transferred by finite-cost simulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For oracle models \(O_1\) and \(O_2\) on a common problem class, write \(O_1\preceq O_2\) if one call to \(O_1\) can be simulated from at most a uniform finite number of \(O_2\)-calls for every admissible history. The models cross an incomparability boundary when neither \(O_1\preceq O_2\) nor \(O_2\preceq O_1\). At this boundary no finite, instance-independent conversion factor follows between their query-complexity bounds. A claimed comparison then requires an explicit additional reduction, restricted subclass, or joint cost model; raw call counts alone do not define an oracle-complexity ordering.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Oracles are incomparable when neither can uniformly simulate the other with finitely many calls; their raw query counts then admit no universal conversion.
assumptions_latex: Both oracle models are defined on the same problem class.
Simulation must reproduce all responses relevant to every adaptive query history.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If neither simulation preorder holds, no uniform finite call-count conversion is justified between \(O_1\) and \(O_2\).

notation.meaning: uniform finite simulation of O1 using O2

review_flags: formal simulation preorder and its complexity interpretation require a direct source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role is appropriate, but the simulation preorder and its complexity interpretation lack a source. Failure of finite per-call simulation means that no conversion follows from that simulation relation alone; a source is needed to support the carefully limited conclusion without implying that all possible complexity reductions are impossible.

children.title: Common Output Convention
children.top_down_role: Shared rule for selecting the reported point from an iterate history.

knowledge_statements.title: Common Output Convention
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the shared rule selecting a reported point from an algorithmic transcript.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H_T\) denote the transcript after oracle cost or query horizon \(T\). An output convention is a measurable selector \(S_T\) that maps \(H_T\) to a reported candidate \(\widehat x_T=S_T(H_T)\in X\). Methods use a common output convention when the same selector type is prescribed before evaluation, such as the final iterate, a specified weighted average, or the best queried point according to observable data. Method-specific postselection using unavailable objective values or different averaging weights is excluded unless it is included and charged in the common convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A comparison must prescribe the same transcript-to-candidate rule, such as last iterate or a fixed weighted average, before performance is evaluated.
assumptions_latex: Each method produces a well-defined transcript \(H_T\).
The selector uses only information permitted by the common oracle model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The reported candidate for either method is \(\widehat x_T=S_T(H_T)\in X\) under one shared selector convention.
review_flags: no supplied locator directly supports transcript-level output normalization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports the transcript-level output normalization. Moreover, different methods generally have different transcript spaces, so saying that both use the same selector S_T requires a common transcript encoding or a precisely defined common selector type.

children.title: Common Accuracy Criterion
children.top_down_role: Shared performance metric used to judge competing outputs.

knowledge_statements.title: Common Accuracy Criterion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a single error functional and success threshold for all compared methods.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E:\mathcal P(\mathcal F,X)\times X\to[0,\infty]\) be a fixed error functional and let \(\varepsilon>0\). A reported point \(\widehat x\) is \(\varepsilon\)-accurate when \(E(p,\widehat x)\le\varepsilon\). Methods use a common accuracy criterion when they share the same functional, tolerance, deterministic or probabilistic quantifier, and worst-case instance set. In a randomized comparison with failure level \(\delta\), for example, success means \(\Pr(E(p,\widehat x)\le\varepsilon)\ge1-\delta\) for every admissible \(p\); expected error is a different criterion and cannot be substituted silently.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compared methods must use the same error measure, tolerance, instance quantifier, and deterministic, expected, or high-probability success convention.
assumptions_latex: \(E\) is defined on every admissible problem and reported candidate.
\(\varepsilon>0\), and \(\delta\in[0,1)\) when a probabilistic criterion is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Success is assessed by one fixed predicate, such as \(E(p,\widehat x)\le\varepsilon\) or \(\Pr(E(p,\widehat x)\le\varepsilon)\ge1-\delta\).
review_flags: supplied source hints do not establish a common oracle-complexity accuracy convention

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the leaf and distinguishes deterministic, expected, and high-probability criteria correctly, but no authoritative source with a locator is supplied for this common oracle-complexity accuracy convention.

children.title: Output-Criterion Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Suitability of a chosen output convention for the selected metric.

knowledge_statements.title: Output-Criterion Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States when a reported output can validly be assessed by the selected criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S_T:H_T\mapsto\widehat x_T\) be the common output selector and let \(E(p,x)\) be the common error functional. The output convention and criterion are compatible when \(S_T(H_T)\) lies in the domain of \(E(p,\cdot)\) for every admissible transcript and when the claimed certificate determines a valid upper bound \(U_T(H_T)\) satisfying \[E(p,S_T(H_T))\le U_T(H_T)\] for every problem and every oracle response consistent with that transcript. Thus the stopping rule \(U_T(H_T)\le\varepsilon\) certifies the accuracy of the point actually reported, not merely another iterate or an unobservable selector.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The criterion must apply to the point actually reported, and its transcript certificate must bound that point’s error on every consistent instance.
assumptions_latex: The selector and error functional are fixed before evaluation.
The bound must hold for every admissible problem consistent with the observed transcript.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Whenever \(U_T(H_T)\le\varepsilon\), the reported point satisfies \(E(p,\widehat x_T)\le\varepsilon\).
review_flags: certificate-based compatibility condition lacks a supplied performance-estimation source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports the proposed certificate-based compatibility condition. H_T is used as though it were both a transcript and a selector domain, and requiring a transcript-verifiable upper bound is stronger than ordinary output-criterion compatibility unless the intended terminal sense specifically requires an a posteriori certificate.

children.title: Criterion Mismatch
children.top_down_role: Comparison failures caused by nonequivalent accuracy measures.

knowledge_statements.title: Criterion Mismatch
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shows that gradient-norm and objective-gap criteria need not be uniformly interchangeable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f_a(x)=a x^2/2\) on \(\mathbb R\), where \(a>0\), one has \(\lvert f_a'(x)\rvert=a\lvert x\rvert\) and \(f_a(x)-f_a(0)=\lvert f_a'(x)\rvert^2/(2a)\). Hence a fixed gradient-norm requirement \(\lvert f_a'(x)\rvert\le\varepsilon\) implies only the gap bound \(f_a(x)-f_a(0)\le\varepsilon^2/(2a)\), whose factor is unbounded as \(a\downarrow0\). Therefore gradient-norm and objective-gap complexities cannot be compared through a uniform tolerance conversion unless the common problem class supplies appropriate positive lower curvature or another error-bound relation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Gradient norm and objective gap are not uniformly interchangeable without a common error-bound or curvature parameter; scaled quadratics expose the mismatch.
assumptions_latex: \(a>0\) and \(\varepsilon>0\).
The common problem class permits \(a\) to approach zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No instance-independent conversion from \(\lvert f_a'(x)\rvert\le\varepsilon\) to a fixed objective-gap tolerance exists over this family.
review_flags: elementary mismatch family is self-contained but no supplied source supports the intended boundary

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The quadratic identities and the stated one-way failure of a uniform gradient-to-gap tolerance conversion are correct for a approaching zero, and the failure-boundary kind fits. However, no source or explicit standard-field rationale supports promotion of this nontrivial boundary claim to candidate-review knowledge.

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Budget Worst-Case Performance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the finite-horizon minimax error of a fixed oracle algorithm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal F\) be a class of optimization instances, let \(\mathcal A\) be a deterministic oracle algorithm, and let \(E(f,x)\ge 0\) be an error criterion. After at most \(N\) oracle calls, \(\mathcal A\) returns \(x_N(\mathcal A,f)\). Its fixed-budget worst-case performance is
\[
W_{\mathcal A}(N;\mathcal F,E):=\sup_{f\in\mathcal F}E\bigl(f,x_N(\mathcal A,f)\bigr).
\]
For a method class \(\mathfrak A\), the optimal fixed-budget performance is \(W^*(N):=\inf_{\mathcal A\in\mathfrak A}W_{\mathcal A}(N;\mathcal F,E)\). The budget counts oracle calls under the oracle model defining \(\mathfrak A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Worst-case performance is the largest error remaining after a fixed number of oracle calls; minimizing it over admissible algorithms gives the finite-budget minimax value.
assumptions_latex: \(N\in\mathbb N_0\) and every \(\mathcal A\in\mathfrak A\) makes at most \(N\) oracle calls.
\(E(f,x)\ge 0\) is defined for every admissible instance-output pair.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(W^*(N)=\inf_{\mathcal A\in\mathfrak A}\sup_{f\in\mathcal F}E\bigl(f,x_N(\mathcal A,f)\bigr)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is mathematically precise and fits the fixed-budget performance container, but no inspectable source with a specific locator is supplied for the oracle-model minimax formulation.

knowledge_statements.title: Target-Accuracy Oracle Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines oracle complexity by inversion of a fixed-budget error guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For an algorithm \(\mathcal A\) with worst-case performance \(W_{\mathcal A}(N)\), its target-accuracy oracle complexity is
\[
T_{\mathcal A}(\varepsilon):=\inf\{N\in\mathbb N_0:W_{\mathcal A}(N)\le\varepsilon\},
\]
with \(\inf\varnothing=+\infty\). For an admissible algorithm class \(\mathfrak A\), the minimax target complexity is
\[
T^*(\varepsilon):=\inf\{N\in\mathbb N_0:W^*(N)\le\varepsilon\}.
\]
Thus \(T_{\mathcal A}(\varepsilon)\) is the least oracle budget certifying error at most \(\varepsilon\) uniformly over the instance class.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Target-accuracy complexity is the smallest oracle-call budget whose worst-case error does not exceed the prescribed tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(\varepsilon\ge 0\).
\(W_{\mathcal A}:\mathbb N_0\to[0,+\infty]\) is the fixed-budget worst-case error.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_{\mathcal A}(\varepsilon)=\inf\{N\in\mathbb N_0:W_{\mathcal A}(N)\le\varepsilon\}\).

notation.meaning: Oracle calls required by the algorithm for tolerance epsilon.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The inversion from worst-case error to target-accuracy complexity is precise and the definition content kind fits, but the record has no cited source or locator.

children.title: Finite-Horizon Performance Views
children.top_down_role: Exact or numerical worst-case behavior at specified iteration budgets.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Horizon Performance Views
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Represents performance as the complete budget-indexed sequence of worst-case errors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For fixed \(\mathcal A\), \(\mathcal F\), and \(E\), the finite-horizon performance view through horizon \(H\) is the vector
\[
\mathbf W_{\mathcal A}^{(H)}:=\bigl(W_{\mathcal A}(0),W_{\mathcal A}(1),\ldots,W_{\mathcal A}(H)\bigr).
\]
It retains the error guarantee at every budget up to \(H\), rather than only a limiting order. Two algorithms have identical finite-horizon performance through \(H\) exactly when their corresponding vector entries agree. Algorithm \(\mathcal A\) weakly dominates \(\mathcal B\) through \(H\) exactly when \(W_{\mathcal A}(N)\le W_{\mathcal B}(N)\) for every \(0\le N\le H\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite-horizon view records every worst-case error up to a chosen budget and compares methods componentwise over that range.
assumptions_latex: \(H\in\mathbb N_0\).
\(W_{\mathcal A}(N)\) and \(W_{\mathcal B}(N)\) use the same instance class, error criterion, and oracle accounting.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal A\preceq_H\mathcal B\iff (\forall N\in\{0,\ldots,H\})\;W_{\mathcal A}(N)\le W_{\mathcal B}(N)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation and componentwise finite-horizon comparison are internally consistent and fit the container, but neither is supported by a cited source or explicit standard-field rationale.

children.title: Asymptotic Performance Views
children.top_down_role: Large-horizon rate behavior used for broad method comparison.

knowledge_statements.title: Asymptotic Performance Views
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines asymptotic rate and leading-constant summaries of worst-case performance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(W:\mathbb N\to[0,+\infty)\) be a worst-case error sequence and let \(r:\mathbb N\to(0,+\infty)\) satisfy \(r(N)\to0\). The asymptotic statement \(W(N)=O(r(N))\) means that there exist \(C<\infty\) and \(N_0\) such that \(W(N)\le C r(N)\) for all \(N\ge N_0\). If
\[
\lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{W(N)}{r(N)}=c\in(0,+\infty),
\]
then \(W(N)\sim c r(N)\), and \(c\) is the asymptotic leading constant. These summaries need not determine performance at any prescribed finite horizon.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An asymptotic view records eventual decay order and, when the normalized limit exists, its leading constant, while discarding arbitrary finite-prefix behavior.
assumptions_latex: \(W(N)\ge0\) for every \(N\in\mathbb N\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(W(N)=O(r(N))\iff (\exists C<\infty)(\exists N_0)(\forall N\ge N_0)\;W(N)\le C r(N)\).

source_refs.source_title: Convex Analysis and Minimization Algorithms I: Fundamentals

source_witnesses.source_title: Convex Analysis and Minimization Algorithms I: Fundamentals

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The asymptotic definitions are mathematically standard and correctly delimited, but the cited section on limits of convex functions does not specifically establish support for sequence big-O notation, normalized rates, or leading constants.

children.title: Horizon-to-Rate Translation
children.top_down_role: Structural passage from finite-budget values to asymptotic summaries.

knowledge_statements.title: Horizon-to-Rate Translation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Translates a uniform finite-budget envelope into asymptotic and target-accuracy guarantees.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose a worst-case performance sequence satisfies \(W(N)\le C(N+\beta)^{-p}\) for every \(N\in\mathbb N_0\), where \(C>0\), \(\beta>0\), and \(p>0\). Then \(W(N)=O(N^{-p})\). Moreover, for every \(\varepsilon>0\), the target-accuracy complexity obeys
\[
T(\varepsilon)\le \max\left\{0,\left\lceil(C/\varepsilon)^{1/p}-\beta\right\rceil\right\}.
\]
The translation preserves the explicit constant and offset because the finite-horizon inequality holds uniformly, not merely beyond an unspecified threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A uniform power-law error envelope yields the same asymptotic rate and an explicit oracle budget for any positive target accuracy.
assumptions_latex: \(W(N)\le C(N+\beta)^{-p}\) for all \(N\in\mathbb N_0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(W(N)=O(N^{-p})\) and \(T(\varepsilon)\le\max\{0,\lceil(C/\varepsilon)^{1/p}-\beta\rceil\}\).

notation.meaning: Least budget attaining error at most epsilon.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The uniform power-law envelope correctly yields the stated rate and integer budget bound, and property is the appropriate content kind, but no source with a specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Preasymptotic Divergence
children.top_down_role: Regimes where asymptotic rankings misrepresent practical finite horizons.

knowledge_statements.title: Preasymptotic Divergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shows that equal asymptotic rates do not control finite-horizon discrepancies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix \(p>0\), a horizon \(H\in\mathbb N\), and a factor \(M>1\). Define nonnegative sequences
\[
U(N):=(N+1)^{-p},\qquad
V(N):=\begin{cases}M(N+1)^{-p},&0\le N\le H,\\(N+1)^{-p},&N>H.\end{cases}
\]
Then \(U(N)\sim N^{-p}\) and \(V(N)\sim N^{-p}\), with the same asymptotic leading constant \(1\). Nevertheless, \(V(N)/U(N)=M\) at every budget \(0\le N\le H\). Hence asymptotic rate and leading-constant alignment alone impose no universal bound on an arbitrarily chosen finite prefix.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two error sequences can share both asymptotic rate and leading constant while differing by any prescribed factor throughout any prescribed finite horizon.
assumptions_latex: \(p>0\), \(H\in\mathbb N\), and \(M>1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(U(N)\sim V(N)\sim N^{-p}\), while \(V(N)=M U(N)\) for every \(0\le N\le H\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The constructed sequences form a valid counterexample and match the preasymptotic-divergence container, but the record provides neither a citation nor an explicit standard-field rationale.

children.title: Upper–Lower Bound Interface
children.top_down_role: Interface to information-based lower bounds without relocating resisting-oracle constructions into this chapter.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Lectures on Convex Optimization

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Minimax Alignment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes equality between an algorithmic upper certificate and an information-theoretic lower certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
V_N:=\inf_{\mathcal A\in\mathfrak A}\sup_{f\in\mathcal F}E\bigl(f,x_N(\mathcal A,f)\bigr)
\]
be the \(N\)-call minimax value. An upper certificate \(U_N\) and lower certificate \(L_N\) are exactly minimax aligned when \(L_N=U_N\), where some admissible algorithm satisfies worst-case error at most \(U_N\) and every admissible algorithm has worst-case error at least \(L_N\). Under these two certificate inequalities, exact alignment implies \(V_N=L_N=U_N\), so the certified algorithm is minimax optimal at horizon \(N\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact minimax alignment occurs when matching algorithmic upper and universal lower certificates equal the finite-budget minimax value.
assumptions_latex: \(\sup_{f\in\mathcal F}E(f,x_N(\mathcal A_+,f))\le U_N\) for some \(\mathcal A_+\in\mathfrak A\).
\(\sup_{f\in\mathcal F}E(f,x_N(\mathcal A,f))\ge L_N\) for every \(\mathcal A\in\mathfrak A\).

children.title: Rate Alignment
children.top_down_role: Agreement between upper bounds plus lower bounds at the level of scaling order.

knowledge_statements.title: Rate Alignment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines equality of upper- and lower-bound decay orders without requiring matching constants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(U_N\) be an algorithmic upper bound and \(L_N\) an information-theoretic lower bound for the same minimax performance quantity, with \(0<L_N\le U_N\) eventually. They are rate aligned with reference rate \(r_N>0\) when
\[
0<\liminf_{N\to\infty}\frac{L_N}{r_N}
\le \limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac{U_N}{r_N}<+\infty.
\]
Equivalently, both bounds are \(\Theta(r_N)\). Rate alignment permits distinct leading constants and does not imply exact equality at any finite horizon.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Upper and lower bounds are rate aligned when both remain within positive constant multiples of the same reference decay sequence.
assumptions_latex: \(r_N>0\) for all sufficiently large \(N\).
\(0<L_N\le U_N\) for all sufficiently large \(N\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_N=\Theta(r_N)\) and \(U_N=\Theta(r_N)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Under the stated eventual positivity and ordering assumptions, the displayed condition is equivalent to both certificates being of order Theta(r_N), and condition fits the container. No supporting source or locator is supplied.

children.title: Constant Gap
children.top_down_role: Residual separation between bounds after rate orders coincide.

knowledge_statements.title: Constant Gap
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the multiplicative separation between aligned upper and lower performance certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(0<L_N\le U_N<+\infty\) be lower and upper certificates for the same performance quantity. The finite-horizon multiplicative constant gap is
\[
G_N:=\frac{U_N}{L_N}\ge1.
\]
The asymptotic constant gap is \(G_\infty:=\limsup_{N\to\infty}G_N\). A uniformly constant-tight pair satisfies \(\sup_{N\ge N_0}G_N<+\infty\) for some \(N_0\). Exact minimax alignment at a horizon is the special case \(G_N=1\). Rate alignment with a common reference rate implies that \(G_N\) is eventually bounded, but it need not imply that \(G_N\) converges or tends to \(1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The constant gap is the ratio of a certified upper bound to a positive lower bound for the same normalized performance quantity. Common-rate alignment bounds this ratio eventually but does not determine its limit or make it equal to one.
assumptions_latex: \(0<L_N\le U_N<+\infty\) on the horizons being compared.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G_N=U_N/L_N\ge1\) and \(G_\infty=\limsup_{N\to\infty}G_N\).

children.title: Gap Normalization Regimes
children.top_down_role: Dependence of constant comparisons on metric, budget, or oracle normalization.

knowledge_statements.title: Gap Normalization Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates multiplicative, additive, and rate-normalized comparisons of upper and lower certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For certificates \(0\le L_N\le U_N\) and a positive reference scale \(r_N\), three distinct normalized gaps are
\[
G_N^{\mathrm{mult}}:=\frac{U_N}{L_N}\quad(L_N>0),\qquad
G_N^{\mathrm{add}}:=U_N-L_N,
\qquad
G_N^{\mathrm{rate}}:=\frac{U_N-L_N}{r_N}.
\]
Multiplicative normalization is invariant under common positive rescaling of both certificates. Additive normalization preserves the physical units of the error criterion. Rate normalization measures the discrepancy relative to a declared decay scale. Any tightness claim must identify its regime because boundedness or convergence of one normalized gap does not generally imply the corresponding property for another.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Upper–lower gaps may be normalized multiplicatively, additively, or by a reference rate; conclusions are meaningful only after fixing the regime.
assumptions_latex: \(0\le L_N\le U_N\) and \(r_N>0\).
\(L_N>0\) whenever \(G_N^{\mathrm{mult}}\) is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G_N^{\mathrm{mult}}=U_N/L_N\), \(G_N^{\mathrm{add}}=U_N-L_N\), and \(G_N^{\mathrm{rate}}=(U_N-L_N)/r_N\).

children.title: Rate-Only Tightness Limits
children.top_down_role: Cases where matching rates do not establish sharp finite-horizon performance.

knowledge_statements.title: Rate-Only Tightness Limits
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifies what cannot be inferred from matching asymptotic orders alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose only that positive certificates satisfy \(L_N=\Theta(r_N)\) and \(U_N=\Theta(r_N)\) for some \(r_N>0\). These hypotheses imply the existence of unspecified constants \(0<c\le C<+\infty\) such that \(c r_N\le L_N\le U_N\le C r_N\) eventually. They do not determine \(U_N/L_N\), force that ratio to converge, establish equality of leading constants, or certify exact finite-horizon minimax optimality. Indeed, for any \(M>1\), the pair \(L_N=r_N\), \(U_N=M r_N\) is rate aligned while maintaining constant gap \(M\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Matching asymptotic orders alone cannot identify leading constants, the exact multiplicative gap, or finite-horizon minimax optimality.
assumptions_latex: \(r_N>0\), \(L_N>0\), and \(U_N\ge L_N\) eventually.
\(L_N=\Theta(r_N)\) and \(U_N=\Theta(r_N)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_N=\Theta(r_N)\) and \(U_N=\Theta(r_N)\) do not imply \(U_N/L_N\to1\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure boundary and its constant-factor example are mathematically correct and appropriately classified, but the record supplies neither a cited source nor an explicit standard-field rationale.

children.title: Dimension Alignment
children.top_down_role: Compatibility of ambient or effective dimension across upper-bound and lower-bound settings.

knowledge_statements.title: Dimension Alignment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Requires upper and lower certificates to concern the same ambient-dimension regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(U_{N,d}\) and \(L_{N,d}\) be upper and lower certificates for problems in ambient dimension \(d\). They are dimension aligned on a regime \(D_N\subseteq\mathbb N\) when both certificates use the same oracle model, instance class, and error normalization, and
\[
L_{N,d}\le V_{N,d}\le U_{N,d}
\qquad\text{for every }d\in D_N,
\]
where \(V_{N,d}\) is the corresponding minimax value. A lower bound proved only for \(d\ge d_0(N)\) cannot certify tightness of an upper bound at fixed \(d<d_0(N)\); alignment must be asserted on the intersection of their valid dimension regimes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Upper and lower bounds are dimension aligned only where they apply to the same dimension, problem class, oracle model, and error normalization.
assumptions_latex: \(V_{N,d}\) is defined for a common oracle model, instance class, and error criterion.
\(D_N\) lies within the validity domains of both certificates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((\forall d\in D_N)\;L_{N,d}\le V_{N,d}\le U_{N,d}\).

notation.meaning: Dimension regime common to both certificates.

children.title: Method-Class Alignment
children.top_down_role: Compatibility of admissible algorithm classes across competing bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Method-Class Alignment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility condition for comparing a method upper bound with an oracle lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal F\) be a problem class, \(\mathcal O\) an oracle, and \(\mathcal A\) a class of methods using \(\mathcal O\). An upper certificate \(U_N\) for \(A\in\mathcal A\) and a lower certificate \(L_N\) are method-class aligned when
\[\sup_{F\in\mathcal F}\operatorname{Err}(A,F,N)\le U_N,\qquad L_N\le\inf_{B\in\mathcal A}\sup_{F\in\mathcal F}\operatorname{Err}(B,F,N),\]
with the same initialization constraints, oracle transcript, iteration budget \(N\), output rule, dimension convention, and error functional. Under this condition, \(L_N\le U_N\), and equality certifies worst-case optimality of \(A\) within \(\mathcal A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Upper and lower bounds are comparable only when they use the same problem class, oracle, budget, initialization, output rule, dimension convention, and error measure.
assumptions_latex: \(N\in\mathbb N\) and every method in \(\mathcal A\) uses at most \(N\) calls to \(\mathcal O\).\)
\(\operatorname{Err}(A,F,N)\) is defined using one common output convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_N\le U_N\), with equality implying minimax optimality of \(A\) over \(\mathcal A\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The minimax alignment condition and conclusion are mathematically sound, and the content kind fits the leaf. However, no source is supplied for the certificate-alignment formulation, and the plain statement should explicitly mention alignment of the admissible method class.

children.title: Dimension-Free Regimes
children.top_down_role: Comparisons whose conclusions remain stable beyond a dimension threshold.

knowledge_statements.title: Dimension-Free Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank-realizable performance estimation whose worst case stabilizes in finite dimension.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each dimension \(d\), let \(W_N(d)\) be the worst-case error of a fixed first-order method over the dimension-\(d\) instances satisfying a common interpolation model. Suppose every feasible performance-estimation datum for budget \(N\) has a Gram representation of rank at most \(r_N\), and every such representation is realizable by an instance in \(\mathbb R^{r_N}\). Then
\[\sup_{d\ge 1}W_N(d)=W_N(r_N).\]
Consequently, any upper certificate independent of \(d\) and exact for the rank-reduced formulation is valid over all finite dimensions; the regime is dimension-free once \(d\ge r_N\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If every feasible certificate has a realizable Gram representation of uniformly bounded rank, the all-dimensional worst case is attained in that rank and the bound becomes dimension-free.
assumptions_latex: \(N\in\mathbb N\) is fixed and all dimensions use the same interpolation constraints.
Every feasible datum has a realizable Gram representation of rank at most \(r_N\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_{d\ge1}W_N(d)=W_N(r_N)\).

notation.meaning: worst-case error at budget N in dimension d

children.title: Class-Mismatch Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Invalid comparisons caused by different algorithmic capabilities.

knowledge_statements.title: Class-Mismatch Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of optimality conclusions when upper and lower certificates concern different instance or method classes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(R_N(\mathcal A,\mathcal F)=\inf_{A\in\mathcal A}\sup_{F\in\mathcal F}\operatorname{Err}(A,F,N)\). If \(\mathcal A_1\subseteq\mathcal A_2\) and \(\mathcal F_1\subseteq\mathcal F_2\), then
\[R_N(\mathcal A_2,\mathcal F_1)\le R_N(\mathcal A_1,\mathcal F_1)\le R_N(\mathcal A_1,\mathcal F_2)\]
and
\[R_N(\mathcal A_2,\mathcal F_1)\le R_N(\mathcal A_2,\mathcal F_2)\le R_N(\mathcal A_1,\mathcal F_2).\]
Class inclusion alone gives no ordering between \(R_N(\mathcal A_1,\mathcal F_1)\) and \(R_N(\mathcal A_2,\mathcal F_2)\). Consequently, an upper certificate for a method in \(\mathcal A_1\) evaluated only on \(\mathcal F_1\) cannot be paired with a lower certificate for \(\mathcal A_2\) on \(\mathcal F_2\) to establish optimality unless the missing cross-class risk comparison and the transfer of the method's upper bound to the target instance class are separately established.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Enlarging the method class lowers minimax risk and enlarging the instance class raises it, but changing both classes produces generally unordered cross risks. Mismatched upper and lower certificates therefore cannot establish optimality without separate risk-comparison and performance-transfer results.
assumptions_latex: \(\operatorname{Err}(A,F,N)\) uses the same budget and output convention in all class pairs.
\(\mathcal A_1\subseteq\mathcal A_2\) and \(\mathcal F_1\subseteq\mathcal F_2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The two monotonicity chains hold, but \(R_N(\mathcal A_1,\mathcal F_1)\) and \(R_N(\mathcal A_2,\mathcal F_2)\) are not ordered by class inclusion alone.

notation.meaning: minimax error for a method class and instance class

knowledge_statements.title: Oracle-Strength Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimax comparison under exact simulation of a weaker oracle by a stronger oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal O_1\preceq_c\mathcal O_2\) mean that one query to \(\mathcal O_1\), including its reply, can be simulated from at most \(c\) queries to \(\mathcal O_2\) without additional information about the instance. For a fixed problem class \(\mathcal F\), error functional, and output rule, exact transcript simulation implies
\[R_{cN}(\mathcal O_2,\mathcal F)\le R_N(\mathcal O_1,\mathcal F).\]
Hence a stronger oracle cannot have worse minimax error after simulation cost is charged. Comparisons at the same nominal iteration count are valid only when \(c=1\) or when oracle calls are assigned equal cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stronger oracle improves minimax performance only after accounting for the number of stronger-oracle calls required to simulate each weaker-oracle call.
assumptions_latex: The simulation preserves every adaptive transcript available to the original method.
Both risks use the same instance class, error criterion, and output rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_{cN}(\mathcal O_2,\mathcal F)\le R_N(\mathcal O_1,\mathcal F)\).

notation.meaning: N-query minimax error under oracle O

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exact-transcript simulation argument and cost-adjusted inequality are precise, and the principle content kind fits the tradeoff leaf. No inspectable source is supplied for the oracle simulation preorder or minimax comparison.

knowledge_statements.title: Parameter-Knowledge Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Value of revealing class parameters to a method before oracle interaction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Theta\) index problem subclasses \(\mathcal F_\theta\). Write \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{blind}}\) for methods whose coefficients and stopping rule cannot depend on \(\theta\), and \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{known}}\) for methods that receive \(\theta\) before the first oracle call. Since \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{blind}}\subseteq\mathcal A_{\mathrm{known}}\),
\[\inf_{A\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{known}}}\sup_{\theta\in\Theta}\sup_{F\in\mathcal F_\theta}\operatorname{Err}(A(\theta),F,N)\le
\inf_{A\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{blind}}}\sup_{\theta\in\Theta}\sup_{F\in\mathcal F_\theta}\operatorname{Err}(A,F,N).\]
A parameter-free method matches the informed benchmark only if a single blind rule attains the informed rate uniformly over \(\Theta\), including its constants.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Giving class parameters to a method can only improve minimax performance; a parameter-free method matches that benchmark only through a uniform bound with matching constants.
assumptions_latex: \(\Theta\neq\varnothing\) and every \(\mathcal F_\theta\) uses the same oracle and error convention.
Both method classes receive the same query budget \(N\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The parameter-informed minimax risk is no larger than the parameter-blind minimax risk.

children.title: Adaptive-Method Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Performance benefits or overhead from data-dependent parameter selection.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive-Method Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimax effect of allowing coefficients to depend on the observed oracle transcript.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{fixed}}\) contain methods whose coefficients are fixed before oracle interaction, and let \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{adapt}}\) additionally permit each coefficient and stopping decision at time \(k\) to be measurable with respect to the transcript \(\mathcal T_k\). For any fixed instance class \(\mathcal F\), oracle, budget, and output rule,
\[\inf_{A\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{adapt}}}\sup_{F\in\mathcal F}\operatorname{Err}(A,F,N)\le
\inf_{A\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{fixed}}}\sup_{F\in\mathcal F}\operatorname{Err}(A,F,N).\]
This comparison charges only the declared oracle budget; computational, storage, or extra-evaluation costs of adaptation must be reported separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Transcript-adaptive methods contain fixed-coefficient methods and therefore have no larger minimax error, although adaptation may incur costs outside the declared oracle budget.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{fixed}}\subseteq\mathcal A_{\mathrm{adapt}}\) under the same admissibility rules.
Both sides use the same oracle calls, instance class, and output criterion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The adaptive-class minimax error is no larger than the fixed-class minimax error.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The minimax inequality correctly follows from the declared nesting of fixed and transcript-adaptive method classes, and the external-cost caveat is appropriately scoped. An inspectable source for the adaptive information model is absent.

children.title: Line-Search Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Performance effects of trial evaluations used to select local parameters.

knowledge_statements.title: Line-Search Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Armijo backtracking as a locally checkable descent certificate with explicit evaluation cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\) be differentiable, let \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\), and choose a descent direction \(p_k\) with \(\langle g_k,p_k\rangle<0\). Given \(\alpha_0>0\), \(\beta\in(0,1)\), and \(\sigma\in(0,1)\), select the smallest \(j_k\ge0\) such that
\[f(x_k+\alpha_0\beta^{j_k}p_k)\le f(x_k)+\sigma\alpha_0\beta^{j_k}\langle g_k,p_k\rangle.\]
Then \(x_{k+1}=x_k+\alpha_0\beta^{j_k}p_k\) has certified decrease. The step costs \(j_k+1\) trial function evaluations, so iteration bounds and oracle-evaluation bounds coincide only when these trials are charged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Armijo backtracking certifies descent but may require several trial evaluations; iteration complexity must therefore be distinguished from total oracle-evaluation complexity.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is differentiable and bounded below along the searched ray.
\(\langle\nabla f(x_k),p_k\rangle<0\), \(\alpha_0>0\), and \(\beta,\sigma\in(0,1)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The accepted step satisfies the Armijo decrease inequality and uses \(j_k+1\) trial function evaluations.

children.title: Adaptive Oracle Overhead
children.top_down_role: Additional oracle cost associated with online parameter adjustment.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Oracle Overhead
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Total oracle cost of geometrically expanding backtracking searches.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose iteration \(k\) tests trial parameters \(M_{k,j}=\gamma^jM_{k,0}\), where \(\gamma>1\), until an acceptance predicate holds whenever \(M_{k,j}\ge\widehat M_k\). Then the first accepted index obeys
\[j_k\le\max\left\{0,\left\lceil\log_\gamma\!\left(\frac{\widehat M_k}{M_{k,0}}\right)\right\rceil\right\},\]
and at most \(j_k+1\) trial-oracle evaluations occur at iteration \(k\). Over \(N\) accepted iterations, the trial overhead is at most
\[N+\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\max\left\{0,\left\lceil\log_\gamma\!\left(\frac{\widehat M_k}{M_{k,0}}\right)\right\rceil\right\}.\]
This bound excludes oracle calls used by the accepted update itself unless they are among the trials.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Geometric backtracking adds logarithmically many trial evaluations per accepted iteration, measured by the ratio between the sufficient and initial trial parameters.
assumptions_latex: \(\gamma>1\) and the trial parameters increase as \(M_{k,j}=\gamma^jM_{k,0}\).
Acceptance is guaranteed for every \(M_{k,j}\ge\widehat M_k>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The total number of trial evaluations is bounded by the displayed logarithmic-overhead sum.

notation.meaning: initial trial parameter at iteration k

children.title: Search Acceptance Regimes
children.top_down_role: Comparison across exact, approximate, monotone, or nonmonotone acceptance policies.

knowledge_statements.title: Search Acceptance Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smoothness regime guaranteeing termination of an Armijo backtracking search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\) have an \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient, let \(g=\nabla f(x)\), and take the gradient trial point \(x^+(\alpha)=x-\alpha g\). For \(\sigma\in(0,1)\), the Armijo predicate
\[f(x^+(\alpha))\le f(x)-\sigma\alpha\lVert g\rVert^2\]
is guaranteed whenever
\[0<\alpha\le\frac{2(1-\sigma)}{L}.\]
Therefore geometric backtracking \(\alpha_j=\alpha_0\beta^j\), with \(\alpha_0>0\) and \(\beta\in(0,1)\), terminates after finitely many trials. If \(g=0\), every trial satisfies the non-strict predicate and the point is stationary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an L-smooth objective, sufficiently small gradient steps satisfy Armijo decrease, so geometric backtracking terminates; a zero gradient is already stationary.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is differentiable and \(\nabla f\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz with \(L>0\).
\(\sigma,\beta\in(0,1)\) and \(\alpha_0>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every \(\alpha\in(0,2(1-\sigma)/L]\) is accepted, so geometric backtracking terminates finitely.

children.title: Last-Iterate Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Worst-case strengths or limitations of reporting the final iterate.

knowledge_statements.title: Last-Iterate Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Absence of a generic last-iterate guarantee from an average-error certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An average-error bound does not imply the same bound for the last iterate without additional trajectory structure. Indeed, for \(f(x)=x^2\) on \(\mathbb R\), choose \(x_k=0\) for \(0\le k<N\) and \(x_N=1\). With \(x_\star=0\),
\[\frac{1}{N+1}\sum_{k=0}^{N}\bigl(f(x_k)-f(x_\star)\bigr)=\frac{1}{N+1},\qquad f(x_N)-f(x_\star)=1.\]
Thus the average error vanishes as \(N\to\infty\) while the last-iterate error does not. Monotonicity, contraction, stability, or a dedicated last-iterate analysis is required to transfer an ergodic certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Small average error need not control the final iterate: a sequence can have vanishing average error while its last point remains uniformly suboptimal.
assumptions_latex: Output sequences are not required to have monotone objective values or satisfy a contraction relation.
Performance is measured by objective suboptimality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No universal implication from vanishing average suboptimality to vanishing last-iterate suboptimality exists.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The explicit sequence is a valid counterexample to transferring an average-error certificate to the last iterate, and failure_boundary fits the terminal container. Despite being self-contained, the record has no source or admissible standard-field rationale for the evidence registry.

children.title: Averaged-Iterate Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Performance consequences of reporting an aggregate of iterates.

knowledge_statements.title: Averaged-Iterate Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convexity certificate for a weighted average of generated iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:C\to\mathbb R\) be convex on a convex set \(C\), let \(x_0,\ldots,x_N\in C\), and let weights \(w_k\ge0\) satisfy \(W_N=\sum_{k=0}^{N}w_k>0\). Define
\[\bar x_N=\frac{1}{W_N}\sum_{k=0}^{N}w_kx_k.\]
For every minimizer \(x_\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}f(x)\), convexity gives
\[f(\bar x_N)-f(x_\star)\le\frac{1}{W_N}\sum_{k=0}^{N}w_k\bigl(f(x_k)-f(x_\star)\bigr).\]
A weighted average-error certificate therefore transfers directly to \(\bar x_N\), but forming or returning \(\bar x_N\) requires storing the aggregate and may not preserve guarantees for nonconvex output constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a convex objective, the objective error of a weighted average is at most the weighted average of the iterate errors, at the cost of aggregate output.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is convex and \(f:C\to\mathbb R\) is convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(\bar x_N)-f(x_\star)\le W_N^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^{N}w_k(f(x_k)-f(x_\star))\).

children.title: Best-Iterate Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Benefits or informational costs of selecting the best observed iterate.

knowledge_statements.title: Best-Iterate Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective-value certificate obtained by selecting the best evaluated iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x_0,\ldots,x_N\) be points at which the real-valued objective \(f\) has been evaluated, and choose
\[k_\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{0\le k\le N}f(x_k),\qquad x_N^{\mathrm{best}}=x_{k_\star}.\]
For any comparison point \(x_\star\) and any weights \(w_k\ge0\) with \(W_N=\sum_{k=0}^{N}w_k>0\),
\[f(x_N^{\mathrm{best}})-f(x_\star)\le\frac{1}{W_N}\sum_{k=0}^{N}w_k\bigl(f(x_k)-f(x_\star)\bigr).\]
The certificate requires objective values sufficient to identify \(k_\star\); it is unavailable under a gradient-only oracle unless objective comparison is separately supplied.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The best evaluated iterate has no larger objective error than any weighted average of iterate errors, but selecting it requires objective-value comparisons.
assumptions_latex: Every \(f(x_k)\) is finite and available to the output-selection rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x_N^{\mathrm{best}})-f(x_\star)\le W_N^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^{N}w_k(f(x_k)-f(x_\star))\).

notation.meaning: iterate having the smallest observed objective value

children.title: Output-Selection Separations
children.top_down_role: Regimes where output conventions produce different worst-case guarantees.

knowledge_statements.title: Output-Selection Separations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-horizon separation between prescribed output rules under a common oracle model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a function class \(\mathcal F\), an oracle model, a horizon \(N\), an algorithm \(A\), and an error functional \(E_f\). For an output rule \(S\), define its worst-case value by \[W_N(A,S)=\sup_{f\in\mathcal F,\,x_0\in\mathcal X_0}E_f\bigl(S(x_0,\ldots,x_N)\bigr).\] Two admissible rules \(S_1,S_2\) exhibit a strict output-selection separation for \(A\) when both values are finite and \(W_N(A,S_1)<W_N(A,S_2)\). A class-level separation holds when \(\inf_{A\in\mathcal A}W_N(A,S_1)<\inf_{A\in\mathcal A}W_N(A,S_2)\), with the same admissible algorithm class \(\mathcal A\), initialization set, and oracle budget on both sides.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An output-selection separation is a strict difference between worst-case guarantees obtained under identical function, oracle, initialization, horizon, and algorithm constraints.
assumptions_latex: \(N\in\mathbb N\) and every output rule uses only the transcript available through iteration \(N\).
The two comparisons use the same class \(\mathcal F\), initialization set \(\mathcal X_0\), and error functional \(E_f\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(W_N(A,S_1)<W_N(A,S_2)\), or its algorithm-class analogue, certifies a strict output-selection separation.

notation.meaning: Worst-case error at horizon N for algorithm A and output rule S.
Chosen performance error for objective f.

children.title: Performance-Driven Method Design

children.title: Coefficient Design
children.top_down_role: Performance-driven selection of weights beyond the primary step length.

knowledge_statements.title: Coefficient Design
knowledge_statements.scope_note: PEP-driven design of fixed-step coefficients for a prescribed first-order method template.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a horizon \(N\), choose coefficients \(h=\{h_{ij}:0\le j<i\le N\}\) in an admissible set \(H\) for the template \[x_i=x_0-\sum_{j=0}^{i-1}h_{ij}g_j,\qquad g_j\in\partial f(x_j).\] For each fixed \(h\), let \(\mathcal P_N(h)\) be the performance-estimation problem maximizing the prescribed terminal error over all interpolable oracle data and permitted initial states. Coefficient design solves \[\min_{h\in H}\operatorname{val}\mathcal P_N(h).\] It outputs a minimizing coefficient array when attained, or an admissible array whose certified value is within a declared outer-optimization tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select the coefficients of a fixed first-order template by minimizing its certified finite-horizon worst-case error over an admissible coefficient set.
assumptions_latex: The interpolation constraints used by \(\mathcal P_N(h)\) characterize or safely relax the chosen function class.
\(H\) enforces causality and any required normalization or sign restrictions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned \(h\) minimizes, or approximately minimizes to the declared tolerance, the PEP-certified worst-case error within the template.

notation.meaning: Coefficient multiplying oracle output j in iterate i.
Horizon-N performance-estimation problem for fixed coefficients.

children.title: Stepsize Design
children.top_down_role: Performance-driven selection of iteration step lengths.

knowledge_statements.title: Stepsize Design
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-horizon stepsize optimization using a performance-estimation objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the iteration \(x_{k+1}=x_k-\alpha_k g_k\), with \(g_k\in\partial f(x_k)\) or \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\) as prescribed, choose \(\alpha=(\alpha_0,\ldots,\alpha_{N-1})\) from an admissible set \(A\). For fixed \(\alpha\), form the performance-estimation problem \(\mathcal P_N(\alpha)\) over all oracle transcripts interpolable by the target function class. Solve \[\min_{\alpha\in A}\operatorname{val}\mathcal P_N(\alpha).\] Return a minimizing schedule if attained; otherwise return a feasible schedule with its certified objective value and the declared outer-solver tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Design a stepsize schedule by minimizing the certified worst-case terminal error of the corresponding finite-horizon method.
assumptions_latex: Every \(\alpha_k\) is fixed before using oracle information unavailable at iteration \(k\).
The admissible set \(A\) enforces all stability, positivity, or scaling requirements of the method class.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output schedule is certified optimal or tolerance-optimal among schedules in \(A\) for the selected horizon and performance criterion.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: stepsize design under PEP is a finite-dimensional outer minimization of certified worst-case performance
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

No cited source supports the PEP outer optimization or the stated optimality certification.

children.title: Coupled Parameter Design
children.top_down_role: Joint tuning of stepsizes with momentum, averaging, or extrapolation coefficients.

knowledge_statements.title: Coupled Parameter Design
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint optimization of interacting coefficients and stepsizes in one method template.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\theta=(h,\alpha)\in\Theta\) parameterize a causal first-order template, for example \[y_k=\sum_{j=0}^{k}h_{kj}x_j,\qquad x_{k+1}=y_k-\alpha_k g(y_k).\] Construct the horizon-\(N\) performance-estimation value \(V_N(\theta)\) using the same interpolation, initialization, and output constraints for every \(\theta\). Coupled parameter design solves \[\min_{(h,\alpha)\in\Theta}V_N(h,\alpha),\] without optimizing either block while freezing the other. The procedure returns a jointly feasible parameter pair together with its certified value and, when only locally solved, an explicit stationarity or optimality-gap qualification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Jointly choose coefficients and stepsizes because their interactions determine the certified worst-case behavior of the complete method.
assumptions_latex: \(\Theta\) imposes causality and all algebraic compatibility constraints between \(h\) and \(\alpha\).
\(V_N(h,\alpha)\) evaluates a common horizon, output rule, and error metric.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned pair \((h,\alpha)\) is jointly certified according to the stated global or local outer-optimization guarantee.

notation.meaning: Complete vector of coupled method parameters.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: jointly parameterized method templates require outer optimization over the full feasible parameter vector
