children.title: Coefficient Robustness Regimes
children.top_down_role: Sensitivity of optimized parameters to class or horizon variation.

knowledge_statements.title: Coefficient Robustness Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Robust certification of designed coefficients across uncertain problem parameters.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(h\in H\) be a coefficient array and let \(u\in U\) index uncertain problem data, such as smoothness, strong-convexity, or oracle-noise parameters. If \(V_N(h;u)\) is the corresponding horizon-\(N\) worst-case value and \(B(u)\) is a target bound, then \(h\) is robust on \(U\) precisely when \[V_N(h;u)\le B(u)\qquad\text{for every }u\in U.\] It is uniformly \(\rho\)-competitive on \(U\) when \[V_N(h;u)\le\rho\inf_{\tilde h\in H}V_N(\tilde h;u)\qquad\text{for every }u\in U.\] Both predicates require one fixed \(h\) across the entire uncertainty set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coefficients are robust when one fixed array satisfies the desired bound, or a uniform competitive ratio, for every admitted problem parameter.
assumptions_latex: \(U\) is the declared uncertainty set and does not depend on the realized oracle transcript.
All values \(V_N(h;u)\) use the same horizon and output criterion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed universal inequality is the robustness condition; pointwise redesign of \(h\) after observing \(u\) does not satisfy it.

notation.meaning: Uncertain problem parameter and its uncertainty set.
Worst-case value of coefficients h under parameter u.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: robust optimization fixes the decision before uncertainty and imposes a universal performance constraint
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The universal fixed-decision inequalities correctly express a robustness condition and fit the selected content kind. The particular robust and uniformly competitive PEP regimes are unsupported by an inspectable authoritative citation.

children.title: Potential-Function Design
children.top_down_role: Performance-driven construction of scalar progress measures.

knowledge_statements.title: Potential-Function Design
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Time-indexed potential certificates for finite-horizon first-order convergence bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For states \(z_k\) and objective data generated by a method, select nonnegative potentials \(\Phi_k(z_k)\) and verify, for every admissible one-step transition, \[\Phi_{k+1}(z_{k+1})\le\Phi_k(z_k),\qquad k=0,\ldots,N-1.\] If coefficients \(a_N>0\) and \(C\ge0\) additionally satisfy \[a_N E_N\le\Phi_N(z_N),\qquad \Phi_0(z_0)\le C,\] then the potential sequence is a verifiable certificate of \(E_N\le C/a_N\). In PEP-compatible design, each one-step inequality is obtained as a nonnegative weighted combination of valid interpolation and algorithmic constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A decreasing time-indexed potential certifies a terminal error bound when it upper-bounds the scaled terminal error and has a bounded initial value.
assumptions_latex: Every transition \(z_k\mapsto z_{k+1}\) satisfies the stated algorithm and oracle interpolation constraints.
\(a_N>0\) and every multiplier used to combine inequality constraints is nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(E_N\le C/a_N\).

notation.meaning: Potential assigned to the iteration-k state.
State containing the iterate and any auxiliary data.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: telescoping nonnegative potentials are standard finite-horizon convergence certificates
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record has the correct certificate role and states a consistent finite-horizon potential decrease and terminal-domination mechanism. The PEP-compatible weighted-combination assertion and the certificate formulation need a pertinent source with a precise locator.

children.title: Lyapunov-Function Design
children.top_down_role: Design of state-based energy measures for iterative dynamics.

knowledge_statements.title: Lyapunov-Function Design
knowledge_statements.scope_note: State-based contraction certificates for autonomous or periodically lifted first-order dynamics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let an optimization method induce a state transition \(z^{+}=T_f(z)\) for every objective \(f\) in a prescribed class. A function \(V:Z\to\mathbb R_+\) is a Lyapunov certificate with factor \(q\in[0,1]\) when \[V(T_f(z))\le qV(z)\] for every admissible \(f\) and state \(z\). If the performance error satisfies \(E_f(z)\le cV(z)\) for some \(c>0\), then every generated trajectory obeys \[E_f(z_k)\le c q^k V(z_0).\] Lyapunov-function design chooses a parameterized nonnegative \(V\) and minimizes a certifiable contraction factor \(q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative state function that contracts on every admissible transition certifies geometric decay of any error controlled by that function.
assumptions_latex: The transition map \(T_f\) is time invariant, or time has been included in the state.
\(V(z)\ge0\) and \(E_f(z)\le cV(z)\) on the admissible state set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(E_f(z_k)\le c q^kV(z_0)\) for every \(k\ge0\).

notation.meaning: Lyapunov function on the method state.
One-step state transition induced by objective f.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: a nonnegative one-step contraction inequality yields geometric decay by iteration
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The contraction certificate is mathematically coherent, explicitly handles time invariance through state augmentation, and fits Lyapunov-Function Design. No authoritative optimization or dynamical-systems source with a specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Potential-Lyapunov Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Structural translation between finite-horizon potentials plus dynamical energies.

knowledge_statements.title: Potential-Lyapunov Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-horizon potentials represented as Lyapunov functions on a clock-augmented state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\{\Phi_k:Z\to\mathbb R_+\}_{k=0}^{N}\) satisfy \(\Phi_{k+1}(T_k(z))\le\Phi_k(z)\). Introduce the lifted state \(\widehat z=(z,k)\) and transition \(\widehat T(z,k)=(T_k(z),k+1)\). Then \[V(\widehat z)=\Phi_k(z)\] defines a nonincreasing Lyapunov function because \(V(\widehat T(z,k))\le V(z,k)\). Conversely, any nonnegative Lyapunov function \(V\) for this clock-augmented transition defines potentials \(\Phi_k(z)=V(z,k)\). Thus finite-horizon time-varying potentials and Lyapunov functions on the lifted state are equivalent at the level of their one-step decrease inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A time-varying potential becomes a Lyapunov function after adding the iteration counter to the state, and every such lifted Lyapunov function yields potentials.
assumptions_latex: The clock-augmented state retains all information on which \(\Phi_k\) and \(T_k\) depend.
Only transitions with \(0\le k<N\) are included.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Phi_{k+1}\circ T_k\le\Phi_k\) if and only if \(V\circ\widehat T\le V\) under \(V(z,k)=\Phi_k(z)\).

notation.meaning: Original method state augmented by the iteration counter.
Lyapunov representation of the potential sequence.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: time-varying decrease certificates are exactly autonomous decrease certificates after clock-state lifting
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The clock-lifting representation matches the Potential-Lyapunov Correspondence leaf and limits equivalence to the one-step decrease inequalities. The equivalence is nevertheless uncited and requires an inspectable source locator.

children.title: Certificate Expressiveness Limits
children.top_down_role: Performance guarantees inaccessible to a selected certificate family.

knowledge_statements.title: Certificate Expressiveness Limits
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical boundary of conclusions drawn from failure of a restricted certificate search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal C\) be a restricted family of candidate certificates, such as potentials affine in function values and quadratic in stored vectors. If no \(C\in\mathcal C\) satisfies the required nonnegativity, one-step decrease, and terminal-domination constraints, then the only valid conclusion is \[\text{the proposed bound has no certificate in }\mathcal C.\] This infeasibility does not imply that the bound is false, nor that no certificate exists in a larger family \(\mathcal C'\supsetneq\mathcal C\). Such a stronger conclusion is valid only after establishing completeness of \(\mathcal C\) for the specified algorithm, function class, horizon, and performance criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Failure to find a certificate in a restricted template disproves only representability in that template, unless a separate completeness result is available.
assumptions_latex: The certificate search is exact; otherwise numerical infeasibility must first be distinguished from mathematical infeasibility.
\(\mathcal C\) is the explicitly declared certificate family.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Infeasibility over \(\mathcal C\) alone cannot establish failure of the target performance bound.

notation.meaning: A strictly more expressive certificate family.

review_flags: template-specific completeness qualifications require authoritative support

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary content kind is appropriate, and the record carefully distinguishes template infeasibility from falsity of the target bound. Because the conclusion depends on the logical and completeness status of restricted certificate searches, authoritative support is required.

children.title: Horizon-Aware Design
children.top_down_role: Method design using a known terminal iteration budget.

knowledge_statements.title: Horizon-Aware Design
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Method design specialized to a known terminal iteration budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a known horizon \(N\), an admissible family of causal parameters \(\Theta_N\), and a terminal criterion \(E_N\), define \(V_N(\theta)\) as the worst-case value of \(E_N\) for the method parameterized by \(\theta\in\Theta_N\). Horizon-aware design solves \[\theta_N\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\theta\in\Theta_N}V_N(\theta).\] The resulting coefficients, stepsizes, or output weights may depend explicitly on \(N\), but iteration \(k\) may use only oracle information available by time \(k\). The procedure outputs \(\theta_N\), its finite-horizon certificate, and the output rule used at iteration \(N\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the stopping horizon is known, optimize the entire causal parameter schedule and output rule specifically for that terminal budget.
assumptions_latex: \(N\) is fixed before the run begins.
Every \(\theta\in\Theta_N\) defines a causal method under the stated oracle model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(V_N(\theta_N)=\inf_{\theta\in\Theta_N}V_N(\theta)\) when the minimum is attained.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: finite-horizon minimax design permits parameters to depend on a horizon known before execution
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm formulation fits Horizon-Aware Design and clearly separates horizon dependence from within-run causality. Its finite-horizon minimax design and certificate-output claims lack a pertinent source with a specific locator.

children.title: Restart Design
children.top_down_role: Performance-driven selection of restart triggers or cycle lengths.

knowledge_statements.title: Restart Design
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Restarting a base method using certified finite-run contraction factors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a base method \(M_m\), initialized from \(y\), return \(R_m(y)\) after \(m\) oracle calls and satisfy \[E(R_m(y))\le q(m)E(y)\] on the target class. Choose restart lengths \(m_0,m_1,\ldots\), set \(y_0=x_0\), and update \[y_{r+1}=R_{m_r}(y_r).\] After \(R\) stages and \(K_R=\sum_{r=0}^{R-1}m_r\) oracle calls, output \(y_R\). The restart certificate is \[E(y_R)\le\left(\prod_{r=0}^{R-1}q(m_r)\right)E(y_0).\] Restart design selects the lengths to minimize this certified product under the available oracle budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Run a certified base method in stages, reinitialize each stage at the preceding output, and choose stage lengths to minimize the product of contraction factors.
assumptions_latex: The base-stage guarantee applies anew from every restart point produced by the method.
Each selected stage length satisfies \(m_r\in\mathbb N_{+}\) and \(q(m_r)\ge0\).

notation.meaning: Output map of an m-step base-method run.
Certified error factor for an m-step stage.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: repeated application of a uniform stage contraction yields the product restart certificate
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The staged procedure and multiplicative certificate fit Restart Design, subject to the explicitly stated uniform reinitialization assumption. No restart-analysis source with an inspectable theorem, section, or page locator is provided.

children.title: Scheduled Restart Regimes
children.top_down_role: Comparison of fixed, adaptive, or horizon-derived restart schedules.

knowledge_statements.title: Scheduled Restart Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Predetermined constant, geometric, or general restart schedules with product certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix before execution a sequence of positive stage lengths \((m_r)_{r\ge0}\). Starting from \(y_0=x_0\), run the base method for \(m_r\) steps and restart from its output: \(y_{r+1}=R_{m_r}(y_r)\). Constant schedules use \(m_r=m\); geometric schedules use \(m_r=\lceil m_0\gamma^r\rceil\) with \(\gamma>1\). At budget \(K\), complete every stage satisfying \(\sum_{r=0}^{R-1}m_r\le K\) and output \(y_R\). If stage \(r\) has certified factor \(q(m_r)\), then \[E(y_R)\le\prod_{r=0}^{R-1}q(m_r)E(y_0).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scheduled restart method fixes its stage lengths in advance; constant and geometric schedules inherit a product of certified stage factors.
assumptions_latex: The stage guarantee with factor \(q(m_r)\) holds uniformly at every generated restart point.
The schedule is independent of future oracle responses.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The completed stages at budget \(K\) certify \(E(y_R)\le\prod_{r=0}^{R-1}q(m_r)E(y_0)\).

notation.meaning: Growth factor of a geometric schedule.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: predetermined restart schedules compose uniform stage guarantees multiplicatively
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The predetermined constant and geometric schedules define a valid scheduled-restart algorithm, and the product conclusion is properly conditional on uniform stage guarantees. A specific authoritative citation is required for these restart regimes and their certification framework.

children.title: Unknown-Horizon Penalties
children.top_down_role: Worst-case loss incurred when the terminal budget is unavailable.

knowledge_statements.title: Unknown-Horizon Penalties
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Competitive penalty for a method whose stopping horizon is unavailable during parameter selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal F\) be a problem class, let \(E_N(M,f)\ge 0\) be the error of method \(M\) after \(N\) oracle calls on \(f\in\mathcal F\), and let \(V_N=\inf_{M_N}\sup_{f\in\mathcal F}E_N(M_N,f)\), where \(M_N\) may depend on \(N\). An anytime method \(M\), whose parameters and iterates do not depend on the eventual stopping time, has unknown-horizon penalty \(\rho_M(N)=\sup_{f\in\mathcal F}E_N(M,f)/V_N\), with \(0/0=1\) and positive-over-zero interpreted as \(+\infty\). A bounded penalty requires \(\sup_{N\ge1}\rho_M(N)<\infty\); growth of this ratio quantifies the loss caused by unavailable horizon information.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The unknown-horizon penalty is the worst-case error ratio between one anytime method and the best method allowed to know the stopping horizon.
assumptions_latex: \(V_N\) is defined using the same oracle model, initialization constraints, and performance criterion as \(E_N\).
\(M\) cannot use the eventual horizon \(N\) when generating iterates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_M(N)\) measures the horizon-information penalty, and uniform horizon robustness is equivalent to \(\sup_{N\ge1}\rho_M(N)<\infty\).

notation.meaning: Performance error after N oracle calls.

review_flags: Exact PEP or competitive-analysis source for the unknown-horizon ratio is missing.
standard_field_rationale: comparing an anytime method with the horizon-aware minimax value isolates the cost of unavailable horizon information.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits the leaf, and the ratio is internally coherent, but no citation supports this particular unknown-horizon competitive-ratio convention, including its minimax comparator and zero-denominator rules.

children.title: Robust Method Design
children.top_down_role: Method design retaining performance under parameter or model perturbation.

knowledge_statements.title: Robust Method Design
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimax design against uncertainty in problem parameters or admissible oracle behavior.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Theta\) index admissible problem or oracle models \(\mathcal F_\theta\), let \(\mathcal M\) be an implementable method family, and let \(E_N(M,f)\) be a prescribed performance measure. Robust method design selects \(M^{\mathrm{rob}}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{M\in\mathcal M}\sup_{\theta\in\Theta}\sup_{f\in\mathcal F_\theta}E_N(M,f)\), subject to coefficients and oracle calls that are valid for every \(\theta\in\Theta\). A certificate \(B\) is robust when the same verifiable inequalities establish \(E_N(M^{\mathrm{rob}},f)\le B\) for all \(\theta\in\Theta\) and \(f\in\mathcal F_\theta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Robust design minimizes certified worst-case error over all admissible parameter values using one method and one uniformly valid certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(\Theta\ne\varnothing\) and every class \(\mathcal F_\theta\) uses a common performance scale.
\(\mathcal M\) contains only methods executable without knowing the realized \(\theta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M^{\mathrm{rob}}\) minimizes the uniform worst-case criterion over \(\Theta\), and its bound must hold simultaneously for every admissible model.
review_flags: A source connecting minimax robust design to performance-estimation certificates is required.
standard_field_rationale: robust optimization uses a uniform minimax criterion over an uncertainty set.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle role fits robust method design, but the record lacks a source supporting both the minimax design formulation and the stronger requirement that one common system of certificate inequalities apply uniformly over all models.

children.title: Parameter-Free Method Design
children.top_down_role: Method design avoiding prescribed numerical problem parameters.

knowledge_statements.title: Parameter-Free Method Design
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational definition relative to a declared family of unknown problem parameters.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a parameterized collection \(\{\mathcal F_\theta:\theta\in\Theta\}\) and an oracle transcript \(\mathcal T_k=((x_i,y_i))_{i=0}^{k}\). A first-order method is parameter-free relative to \(\Theta\) if there exist measurable update maps \(\Phi_k\), independent of the realized \(\theta\), such that \(x_{k+1}=\Phi_k(\mathcal T_k)\) for every admissible instance. Any stopping test must likewise depend only on the transcript and user-specified accuracy or confidence inputs. The designation does not exclude dimension, constraints, or an initial point; all information permitted to \(\Phi_k\) must be declared explicitly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A method is parameter-free when its updates and stopping rule use observed oracle data but none of the designated unknown problem parameters.
assumptions_latex: \(y_i\) denotes the response returned by the declared first-order oracle at query \(x_i\).
\(\Theta\) lists exactly the parameters claimed to be unknown.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}\) and the stopping decision are invariant under changes of \(\theta\) that leave the observed transcript and declared user inputs unchanged.
review_flags: A canonical source specifying parameter-free first-order methods in this interface sense is missing.
standard_field_rationale: parameter freedom is an information restriction on update and stopping maps.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition role and transcript-based information restriction fit the leaf. A source is required for this exact parameter-free convention, particularly the measurable-map formulation and inclusion of transcript-based stopping rules.

children.title: Universal Method Design
children.top_down_role: Method design adapting across regularity or curvature classes.

knowledge_statements.title: Universal Method Design
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simultaneous near-oracle performance across a nested or parameterized family of regularity classes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\{\mathcal F_\theta:\theta\in\Theta\}\) be problem classes sharing one oracle model, and define the classwise minimax value \(V_N(\theta)=\inf_{M_\theta}\sup_{f\in\mathcal F_\theta}E_N(M_\theta,f)\), where \(M_\theta\) may know \(\theta\). A method \(U\) is universal for this family with overhead \(a_N(\theta)\ge1\) and remainder \(r_N(\theta)\ge0\) if \(U\) does not use \(\theta\) and \(\sup_{f\in\mathcal F_\theta}E_N(U,f)\le a_N(\theta)V_N(\theta)+r_N(\theta)\) for every \(N\ge1\) and \(\theta\in\Theta\). Universality is meaningful only after the oracle, admissible inputs, and comparison family \(M_\theta\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A universal method ignores the realized regularity class yet nearly matches the minimax performance of methods tuned to each class.
assumptions_latex: All \(\mathcal F_\theta\) use the same oracle transcript and performance criterion.
\(U\) is executable without observing \(\theta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(U\) satisfies a simultaneous classwise comparison bound against \(V_N(\theta)\) for every \(\theta\in\Theta\).
review_flags: The exact universality convention and admissible regularity family require a dedicated source.
standard_field_rationale: universality is expressed by simultaneous comparison with classwise tuned minimax values.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle role fits the container, but no source fixes the broad multiplicative-additive comparison against classwise minimax values as the intended notion of universal method design.

children.title: Adaptation Overhead
children.top_down_role: Worst-case cost of robustness or universality relative to specialized designs.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptation Overhead
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplicative and additive cost of adapting without the parameter available to a tuned comparator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\theta\in\Theta\), let \(R_N^{\mathrm{tun}}(\theta)>0\) be the worst-case error guarantee of a comparator tuned to \(\theta\), and let \(R_N^{\mathrm{ad}}(\theta)\) be the guarantee of an adaptive method that does not know \(\theta\). Its multiplicative adaptation overhead is \(A_N(\theta)=R_N^{\mathrm{ad}}(\theta)/R_N^{\mathrm{tun}}(\theta)\). More generally, a pair \((a_N(\theta),r_N(\theta))\) is a valid overhead certificate when \(R_N^{\mathrm{ad}}(\theta)\le a_N(\theta)R_N^{\mathrm{tun}}(\theta)+r_N(\theta)\). The oracle budget, success probability, initialization, and error criterion must coincide in both guarantees.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adaptation overhead compares an untuned method's certified error with the guarantee of an otherwise identical comparator that knows the hidden parameter.
assumptions_latex: \(R_N^{\mathrm{tun}}(\theta)>0\) for the ratio convention.
Both guarantees use the same oracle budget and performance criterion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A_N(\theta)\ge0\) is the multiplicative price of adaptation, while \((a_N(\theta),r_N(\theta))\) permits mixed multiplicative-additive comparison.
review_flags: A source fixing the adaptation-overhead convention for this taxonomy is missing.
standard_field_rationale: overhead is a like-for-like competitive comparison between adaptive and tuned guarantees.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition role fits adaptation overhead and the formulas are coherent, but the proposed ratio and mixed multiplicative-additive certificate are conventions requiring a dedicated source.

children.title: Problem-Class Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Modeling interfaces for selecting structural problem families.

knowledge_statements.title: Problem-Class Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-data interface translating a problem class into interpolation constraints used by a PEP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I\) index sampled oracle records \(z_i\), and let \(G\) denote the Gram matrix of all sampled vectors. A problem-class interface for \(\mathcal C\) is a family of constraints \(\mathscr I_{\mathcal C}(G,z)\le0\) with the interpolation property: a finite record \((G,z)\) is realizable by some problem in \(\mathcal C\) if and only if it satisfies these constraints, up to the declared dimension convention. In a performance-estimation problem, the interface contributes only these realizability constraints; the method equations, initialization bounds, and performance objective are supplied separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A problem-class interface encodes exactly which finite oracle records can arise from a member of the modeled class.
assumptions_latex: \(G\succeq0\) represents inner products among all sampled vectors.
The interface declares whether realization is dimension-free or restricted to a fixed dimension.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((G,z)\text{ is realizable by }\mathcal C\iff G\succeq0\text{ and }\mathscr I_{\mathcal C}(G,z)\le0\).

children.title: Function Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Modeling interfaces for function objects plus evaluable records.

knowledge_statements.title: Function Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sampled-value and subgradient interface for function-class interpolation in a PEP model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a function class \(\mathcal F\) on a real Hilbert space, a function interface receives finite triples \((x_i,g_i,f_i)_{i\in I}\), where \(f_i\) is a candidate value and \(g_i\) a candidate first-order oracle output. It returns interpolation constraints \(\mathscr I_{\mathcal F}((x_i,g_i,f_i)_{i\in I})\le0\) such that the triples are realizable precisely when there exists \(f\in\mathcal F\) satisfying \(f(x_i)=f_i\) and \(g_i\in\partial f(x_i)\) for every \(i\in I\). Inner products and squared norms are represented through a positive-semidefinite Gram matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A function interface converts sampled points, values, and subgradients into constraints equivalent to interpolation by a function in the chosen class.
assumptions_latex: \(I\) is finite and all \(x_i,g_i\) lie in one real Hilbert space.
The chosen oracle semantics specify \(g_i\in\partial f(x_i)\), or the corresponding single-valued gradient relation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists f\in\mathcal F\ \forall i:\ f(x_i)=f_i,\ g_i\in\partial f(x_i)\iff \mathscr I_{\mathcal F}\le0\) together with Gram consistency.

notation.meaning: Sampled point, subgradient, and function value.
Subdifferential under the declared function model.

children.title: Operator Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Modeling interfaces for monotone or fixed-point operator objects.

knowledge_statements.title: Operator Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Graph-interpolation interface for monotone or structured operators in finite PEP data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal A\) be a class of set-valued operators on a real Hilbert space. An operator interface accepts finite graph samples \((x_i,u_i)_{i\in I}\) and produces constraints \(\mathscr I_{\mathcal A}((x_i,u_i)_{i\in I})\le0\) with the interpolation property that the samples are realizable if and only if there exists \(A\in\mathcal A\) such that \(u_i\in A x_i\) for every \(i\in I\). For example, monotonicity contributes \(\langle u_i-u_j,x_i-x_j\rangle\ge0\) for all \(i,j\in I\); stronger operator classes require their complete interpolation conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An operator interface encodes when finitely many input-output pairs belong to the graph of one operator in the modeled class.
assumptions_latex: \(I\) is finite and all graph samples belong to a common real Hilbert space.
The interface fixes whether operators are single-valued, maximal, Lipschitz, cocoercive, or otherwise structured.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists A\in\mathcal A\ \forall i:\ u_i\in A x_i\iff \mathscr I_{\mathcal A}((x_i,u_i)_{i\in I})\le0\) with Gram consistency.

children.title: Composite Object Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Assembly of compatible functions, operators, or class restrictions.

knowledge_statements.title: Composite Object Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Componentwise modeling of sums, compositions, and coupled optimization objects without collapsing their oracle identities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a modeled object have declared decomposition \(F=\Psi(F_1,\ldots,F_m)\), where each component \(F_j\) belongs to a class \(\mathcal C_j\). A composite object interface introduces separate sampled records \(z^{(j)}\), imposes each component interpolation system \(\mathscr I_{\mathcal C_j}(z^{(j)})\le0\), and adds coupling equations \(\mathscr K_\Psi(z^{(1)},\ldots,z^{(m)})=0\) expressing the decomposition and shared variables. The representation is exact when joint feasibility is equivalent to realization by components \(F_j\in\mathcal C_j\) whose composition through \(\Psi\) produces the modeled object and its declared oracle responses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A composite interface keeps component classes separate and combines their interpolation constraints with equations encoding the declared sum, composition, or coupling.
assumptions_latex: \(m<\infty\) and each component interface has declared oracle semantics.
\(\Psi\) and all variable-sharing rules are fixed before constructing the PEP.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F=\Psi(F_1,\ldots,F_m)\) is finitely realizable exactly when all component constraints and coupling equations are jointly feasible.

children.title: Primitive Oracle Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Software representations of elementary information queries.

knowledge_statements.title: Primitive Oracle Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Typed specification of an atomic oracle query, response, cost, and admissibility relation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A primitive oracle interface is a tuple \(\mathfrak O=(\mathcal Q,\mathcal Y,\Gamma,c)\), where \(\mathcal Q\) is the query space, \(\mathcal Y\) the response space, \(\Gamma\subseteq\mathcal Q\times\mathcal Y\) the admissible query-response relation induced by the modeled object, and \(c:\Gamma\to[0,\infty)\) the accounting cost. An oracle call at \(q\in\mathcal Q\) may return only \(y\in\mathcal Y\) satisfying \((q,y)\in\Gamma\). A PEP encoding must introduce variables for every returned datum and impose the constraints defining \(\Gamma\); deterministic, adversarial, and stochastic response semantics must not be interchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A primitive oracle interface declares valid queries, possible responses, their consistency relation, and how each call is charged.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal Q\) and \(\mathcal Y\) are declared measurable spaces when randomized responses are permitted.
\(\Gamma\) is tied to the same optimization object used by the problem-class interface.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((q,y)\) is an admissible charged oracle event exactly when \((q,y)\in\Gamma\), with cost \(c(q,y)\).

children.title: Method Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Software representations of admissible iterative schemes.

knowledge_statements.title: Method Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transcript-level encoding of admissible first-order update and stopping rules.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a primitive oracle interface \(\mathfrak O\), a deterministic \(N\)-step method interface consists of initialization constraints and maps \(x_{k+1}=\Phi_k(\mathcal T_k)\) for \(k=0,\ldots,N-1\), where \(\mathcal T_k=((x_i,y_i))_{i=0}^{k}\) is the available transcript and every \((x_i,y_i)\) is oracle-admissible. In a finite PEP, each update map is represented by explicit algebraic constraints among sampled vectors and scalars. The output is a declared transcript-measurable quantity \(x_{\mathrm{out}}=\Phi_{\mathrm{out}}(\mathcal T_N)\); no future response may enter an earlier update.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A method interface expresses initialization, causal transcript-based updates, and output selection as explicit constraints compatible with the chosen oracle.
assumptions_latex: The horizon \(N\) and information available before each query are declared.
Each \(\Phi_k\) is representable by constraints accepted by the PEP model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}\) depends only on \(\mathcal T_k\), and \(x_{\mathrm{out}}\) depends only on \(\mathcal T_N\).

notation.meaning: Oracle transcript available after query k.

children.title: Oracle-Method Binding
children.top_down_role: Compatibility between method declarations plus available oracle primitives.

knowledge_statements.title: Oracle-Method Binding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility and causality predicate linking each modeled method call to one oracle instance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a method generate queries \(q_k=\Phi_k(\mathcal T_{k-1})\), and let \(\mathfrak O=(\mathcal Q,\mathcal Y,\Gamma,c)\) model an oracle associated with a single object \(F\). The method and oracle are correctly bound when, for every \(k\), \(q_k\in\mathcal Q\), the response satisfies \(y_k\in\mathcal Y\) and \((q_k,y_k)\in\Gamma_F\), and all occurrences of oracle data in the method constraints refer to that same sampled response. The binding is causal when \(q_k\) is measurable with respect to \(\mathcal T_{k-1}\); its total charged budget is \(C_N=\sum_{k=0}^{N}c(q_k,y_k)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Oracle-method binding requires every causal method query and returned datum to satisfy one declared oracle relation with consistent identity and cost accounting.
assumptions_latex: All calls bound to \(F\) use the same object realization and oracle semantics.
\(\mathcal T_{-1}\) contains only declared initialization data.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\forall k:\ q_k=\Phi_k(\mathcal T_{k-1}),\ (q_k,y_k)\in\Gamma_F\), and \(C_N=\sum_{k=0}^{N}c(q_k,y_k)\).

notation.meaning: Oracle relation induced by object F.
