children.title: Unsupported Primitive Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Modeling limits caused by missing or incompatible oracle operations.

knowledge_statements.title: Unsupported Primitive Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary for primitives lacking a finite Gram-representable oracle model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a PEP model use finitely many sampled vectors and scalars collected in a Gram matrix \(G\succeq0\) and a value vector \(F\). A primitive is supported only if every oracle response and every relation it introduces can be expressed by finitely many affine equalities or inequalities in \((G,F)\). A primitive requiring an unresolved infinite-dimensional constraint, a nonconvex relation in \((G,F)\), or information not determined by the sampled transcript lies outside this interface. Applying the finite semidefinite certificate mechanism to such a primitive without a sound finite reformulation does not certify the original worst-case problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A primitive is unsupported when its sampled behavior lacks a sound finite affine Gram representation; then an SDP certificate for the surrogate does not certify the original problem.
assumptions_latex: The certificate mechanism represents sampled inner products by \(G\succeq0\).
All modeled scalar data are stored in a finite vector \(F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Unsupported primitives cannot be soundly certified without an additional exact or conservative finite reformulation.
review_flags: PEP-specific support boundary lacks an authoritative supplied locator

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits the leaf, but no source or locator supports the asserted support criterion. Requiring every relation to be affine directly in (G,F) may exclude supported finite conic liftings, so the exact boundary cannot be validated without framework documentation.

children.title: Initial-Condition Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Software declarations for admissible starting information.

knowledge_statements.title: Initial-Condition Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite PEP encoding of admissible initial states.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a sampled optimization transcript represented by \((G,F)\), an initial-condition interface is a finite family of affine constraints \[\mathcal I_R=\{(G,F):a_j+\langle A_j,G\rangle+b_j^{\mathsf T}F\le R_j,\ j=1,\ldots,m\}.\] Each constraint specifies information available before the method runs, such as \(\|x_0-x_\star\|^2\le R^2\) or \(f(x_0)-f_\star\le\Delta\). The interface is valid for a problem class when every admissible initial transcript belongs to \(\mathcal I_R\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An initial-condition interface is a finite affine Gram description of all information assumed at iteration zero, including distance, function-gap, or residual bounds.
assumptions_latex: The initial state and a reference solution are among the sampled objects.
Their inner products and scalar values are represented by \((G,F)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every admissible initial transcript must satisfy all constraints defining \(\mathcal I_R\).

notation.meaning: set of transcripts satisfying the initial bounds
trace inner product of symmetric matrices

review_flags: PEP interface definition requires a dedicated modeling reference

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition role fits the interface leaf and the finite affine encoding is plausible, but no cited modeling reference establishes that this is the intended PEP initial-condition interface or supports its exact validity criterion.

children.title: Performance-Metric Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Software declarations for objectives used in worst-case evaluation.

knowledge_statements.title: Performance-Metric Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Epigraph interface for a worst-case performance criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((G,F)\) represent a feasible sampled transcript. A performance-metric interface specifies affine expressions \(p_k(G,F)=\alpha_k+\langle P_k,G\rangle+q_k^{\mathsf T}F\), for \(k=1,\ldots,r\), and introduces an epigraph variable \(\tau\) satisfying \(\tau\le p_k(G,F)\) for every \(k\). Maximizing \(\tau\) therefore evaluates the worst guaranteed value of \(\min_k p_k(G,F)\). For a single terminal criterion, \(r=1\); common choices include a function gap, squared distance, gradient norm, or fixed-point residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A performance-metric interface converts one or more affine transcript criteria into an epigraph objective whose maximization gives the modeled worst-case performance.
assumptions_latex: Each selected metric is affine in the PEP variables \((G,F)\).
The feasible transcript set already encodes the function class and method.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The objective \(\max\tau\) with \(\tau\le p_k(G,F)\) represents \(\max_{(G,F)}\min_k p_k(G,F)\).
review_flags: Objective convention is PEP-framework-specific and lacks a supplied source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition role fits the leaf, and the displayed constraints correctly encode maximization of the minimum of the affine metrics. However, tau <= p_k is conventionally a hypograph construction rather than an epigraph construction, and the framework-specific objective convention has no supporting source.

children.title: Condition-Metric Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Compatibility between starting constraints plus selected performance criteria.

knowledge_statements.title: Condition-Metric Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Homogeneity and representability condition linking initialization to performance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal T_R\) be the feasible transcript set under initial scale \(R>0\), and let \(p\) be the selected performance metric. The pair is compatible with degree \(d>0\) if there exists a scaling map \(S_R\) such that \[\mathcal T_R=S_R(\mathcal T_1),\qquad p(S_R z)=R^d p(z)\quad\text{for every }z\in\mathcal T_1,\] and both the initial condition and metric remain affine in the lifted PEP variables after scaling. Under this condition, the worst-case value satisfies \(W(R)=R^dW(1)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Initialization and metric are compatible when one transcript scaling preserves feasibility and makes the metric homogeneous, allowing a normalized PEP to recover every scale.
assumptions_latex: The initial scale satisfies \(R>0\).
The scaled and normalized transcript sets are nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Compatibility implies the scaling identity \(W(R)=R^dW(1)\).

notation.meaning: feasible transcripts at initial scale R

review_flags: Several PEP frameworks use different normalization conventions
Exact intended compatibility predicate needs a framework source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits the leaf, but the proposed homogeneity predicate is framework-specific and uncited. The domain and action of S_R are not specified beyond transcript-set mapping, so the exact compatibility condition and its applicability cannot be validated.

children.title: Normalization Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Modeling support for scale conventions shared across conditions or metrics.

knowledge_statements.title: Normalization Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scale-one representation of a homogeneous performance-estimation problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose an initial-condition and performance pair is compatible with degree \(d\), so that \(\mathcal T_R=S_R(\mathcal T_1)\) and \(p(S_Rz)=R^dp(z)\). The normalization interface replaces the bound at scale \(R>0\) by its unit-scale form and records the recovery rule \[W(R)=R^dW(1),\qquad W(1)=\sup_{z\in\mathcal T_1}p(z).\] Thus the normalized constraint fixes the homogeneous initial quantity to one; the case \(R=0\) must be treated separately unless continuity or degeneracy establishes the same formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A normalization interface solves the homogeneous PEP at unit initial scale and restores the general bound by the metric’s scaling degree.
assumptions_latex: Condition-metric compatibility holds with degree \(d>0\).
The scale satisfies \(R>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The unit-scale representation recovers the original value through \(W(R)=R^dW(1)\).

notation.meaning: worst-case value at initial scale R

review_flags: PEP normalization interface lacks a supplied authoritative locator

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation role is appropriate and the formula follows from the preceding compatibility condition, but that condition and the claimed normalization interface are unsupported by any inspectable source or locator.

children.title: Custom Interpolation Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Extension points for user-specified finite-data realizability conditions.

knowledge_statements.title: Custom Interpolation Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extension contract for finite interpolation predicates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For sampled triples \((x_i,g_i,f_i)\) indexed by a finite set \(I\), a custom interpolation interface is a finite predicate \[\Phi(G,F)=\bigwedge_{\ell=1}^{m}\{a_\ell+\langle A_\ell,G\rangle+b_\ell^{\mathsf T}F\le0\}\] claimed to be necessary and sufficient for the existence of an object in a declared class \(\mathcal C\) interpolating all samples. Sound use requires both directions: every \(C\in\mathcal C\) generates data satisfying \(\Phi\), and every finite dataset satisfying \(\Phi\) admits an interpolant in \(\mathcal C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A custom interpolation interface supplies finite affine Gram conditions that are both necessary and sufficient for sampled data to come from the declared class.
assumptions_latex: The sample index set \(I\) is finite.
All pairwise inner products and sampled values occur in \((G,F)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The predicate \(\Phi(G,F)\) is exact only when feasibility is equivalent to finite interpolability by \(\mathcal C\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition role fits the custom-interpolation leaf, but no source supports the requirement that a custom interface consist specifically of finite affine Gram inequalities or establishes the stated necessity-and-sufficiency extension contract.

children.title: Custom Constraint Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Extension points for additional admissibility restrictions.

knowledge_statements.title: Custom Constraint Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extension contract for user-supplied transcript constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A custom constraint interface accepts finitely many relations \[c_j(G,F)=\alpha_j+\langle C_j,G\rangle+d_j^{\mathsf T}F\ \mathrel{\unlhd_j}\ 0,\qquad j=1,\ldots,m,\] where each \(\unlhd_j\) is either \(=\) or \(\le\). The relations may restrict sampled iterates, oracle outputs, or scalar values, but their mathematical meaning and quantification must be declared. Adding them is sound for an intended model only if every transcript covered by that model satisfies every \(c_j\mathrel{\unlhd_j}0\); otherwise they silently reduce the worst-case class.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A custom constraint interface adds finite affine equalities or inequalities to transcript variables, with soundness requiring every intended transcript to satisfy them.
assumptions_latex: The base PEP uses a finite Gram matrix \(G\) and scalar vector \(F\).
Each added relation has an explicitly declared semantic interpretation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Valid custom constraints preserve all transcripts in the intended model and define a convex semidefinite-representable restriction.
review_flags: Framework-specific extension semantics lack a supplied source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition role fits the leaf and the affine constraints are internally coherent. The assertion that sound custom constraints must hold for every intended transcript is one particular exact-modeling convention; restriction constraints can instead intentionally define a narrower intended class. A framework source is needed to fix the intended semantics.

children.title: Extension Compatibility Checks
children.top_down_role: Structural checks for interactions among user-provided extensions.

knowledge_statements.title: Extension Compatibility Checks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Static validity checks for custom PEP extensions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A custom extension is compatible with the semidefinite PEP mechanism if: \(\text{(i)}\) every introduced symbol has a finite sampled representation in \((G,F)\); \(\text{(ii)}\) every added relation is affine in \((G,F)\), after explicitly declared conic lifting if needed; \(\text{(iii)}\) dimensions, index domains, and oracle bindings agree with the base model; and \(\text{(iv)}\) the extension preserves the claimed interpolation and initial-condition semantics. Passing these checks establishes syntactic conic representability, but establishes semantic validity only when the extension's necessity or sufficiency claim is independently justified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An extension is compatible when its symbols, dimensions, bindings, and lifted constraints fit the finite conic model; semantic soundness still needs mathematical justification.
assumptions_latex: The base model has finite variables \((G,F)\) and declared oracle bindings.
Any auxiliary conic lifting is finite and explicitly specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Compatibility yields a well-formed conic PEP, but not by itself a sound interpolation theorem or worst-case certificate.

notation.meaning: base Gram and scalar PEP variables

review_flags: Compatibility checklist depends on the intended PEP implementation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits the compatibility-check leaf, but the checklist depends on the concrete PEP implementation and is not sourced. In particular, the admissible lifted cones and the semantic checks are not specified sufficiently to establish a general compatibility criterion.

children.title: Unsupported Extension Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Cases that exceed the representational scope of the modeling layer.

knowledge_statements.title: Unsupported Extension Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary beyond finite sound conic extensions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A custom extension lies outside the supported certificate mechanism if it introduces a relation that has no declared finite conic representation, uses hidden state not determined by the modeled transcript, invokes an oracle whose interpolation semantics are unspecified, or asserts only a sufficient relaxation while reporting an exact worst-case value. If the implemented feasible set \(\widehat{\mathcal T}\) is not proved equal to the intended transcript set \(\mathcal T\), the computed optimum certifies only \(\widehat{\mathcal T}\); its interpretation for \(\mathcal T\) depends on the proved inclusion direction and cannot be labeled exact automatically.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Extensions without finite conic representation or justified transcript semantics are unsupported; their computed optima apply only to the implemented feasible set.
assumptions_latex: The implementation optimizes over a declared feasible set \(\widehat{\mathcal T}\).
The intended mathematical model has transcript set \(\mathcal T\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Without a proved equality or inclusion between \(\widehat{\mathcal T}\) and \(\mathcal T\), no exact certificate transfers to the intended model.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits the leaf, and the warning about distinguishing implemented and intended feasible sets is mathematically important. No source defines this framework's supported extensions, and the record does not state the precise upper- or lower-bound consequence associated with each possible set-inclusion direction.

knowledge_statements.title: Interior-Point Semidefinite Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal-dual interior-point solution regime for a finite PEP SDP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given the primal semidefinite program \[\sup_y\{c^{\mathsf T}y:A_0+\textstyle\sum_i y_iA_i\succeq0,\ By=b\},\] form its conic dual, choose strictly feasible primal-dual iterates when available, and repeatedly compute a Newton direction for perturbed KKT equations with complementarity target \(XS\approx\mu I\). Select a step preserving \(X\succ0\) and \(S\succ0\), reduce \(\mu\), and stop only when scaled primal residual, dual residual, and duality gap meet prescribed tolerances. Output the primal objective, dual objective, residuals, and candidate primal-dual certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: This regime solves the PEP SDP through primal-dual Newton steps and reports both objectives, residuals, and gap as a numerical certificate candidate.
assumptions_latex: The PEP has a finite semidefinite formulation.
A primal-dual interior-point implementation and numerical tolerances are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Termination returns an approximate primal-dual pair whose residuals and gap quantify numerical certificate quality.

notation.meaning: primal and dual positive-semidefinite slack matrices

review_flags: No supplied source covers semidefinite interior-point algorithms

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role is suitable for this solver-regime topic, but no semidefinite interior-point source or locator is supplied. The displayed primal introduces y but later uses slack matrices X and S without explicitly defining their relation to the primal and dual programs, so the precise algorithmic formulation cannot be validated.

knowledge_statements.title: First-Order Conic-Solver Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operator-splitting regime for approximate conic PEP solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Write the finite PEP in conic form \[\min_x\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax+s=b,\ s\in K\},\] together with its dual. A first-order conic regime applies a splitting or homogeneous self-dual embedding iteration using matrix-vector products with \(A\) and projections onto \(K\) and \(K^*\). It stops when normalized primal infeasibility, dual infeasibility, and duality gap are below declared tolerances, or returns an approximate infeasibility certificate. Because termination is tolerance-based, the reported objective is not an exact PEP certificate unless subsequently verified or safely bounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A first-order conic solver uses matrix-vector products and cone projections, returning tolerance-qualified objectives or infeasibility evidence that require verification for rigorous certification.
assumptions_latex: The PEP admits a finite closed-cone formulation with cone \(K\).
Projection or proximal operations for \(K\) and its dual are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is an approximate conic solution or infeasibility certificate qualified by explicit residual and gap tolerances.
review_flags: No supplied locator covers first-order conic solvers

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits the solver-regime topic, but the statement blends generic splitting methods with homogeneous self-dual embedding methods and their certificate behavior. No authoritative conic-solver source or specific locator supports the combined algorithm and stopping claims.

children.title: High-Precision Arithmetic Regime
children.top_down_role: Numerical solution using precision beyond standard floating-point arithmetic.

knowledge_statements.title: High-Precision Arithmetic Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Adaptive multiprecision solution and verification of a PEP conic program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a finite conic PEP, an initial precision \(p_0\), target tolerance \(\varepsilon\), and increment rule, solve the primal-dual pair using \(p\)-digit arithmetic. Recompute primal residual \(r_p\), dual residual \(r_d\), cone violations, and gap \(g\) at the same or higher precision. Accept only if all normalized quantities are at most \(\varepsilon\) and remain stable after increasing \(p\); otherwise increase precision and repeat. Output the approximate primal-dual pair, achieved precision, residuals, gap, and rounding-aware bounds. This regime improves numerical reliability but does not itself establish exact feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The regime repeatedly solves and checks the conic PEP at increasing precision until residuals, cone violations, and gap are stable below tolerance.
assumptions_latex: A multiprecision conic solver is available.
The requested tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\) and precision-escalation rule are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Acceptance produces a precision-qualified approximate certificate, not an exact-arithmetic certificate.
review_flags: High-precision PEP verification procedure lacks a supplied source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role is appropriate for the arithmetic-regime leaf, but no source supports this particular adaptive multiprecision procedure. Stability after increasing precision and unspecified rounding-aware bounds are insufficiently defined to establish the stated acceptance criterion.

children.title: Exact-Arithmetic Regime
children.top_down_role: Symbolic or rational processing for exact computational artifacts.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact-Arithmetic Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact rational computation for finite-dimensional PEP primal-dual certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An exact-arithmetic regime for a performance-estimation problem is a computational model in which all input coefficients belong to \(\mathbb{Q}\), every algebraic operation and comparison is performed over \(\mathbb{Q}\), and the reported primal-dual certificate \((X,y,S)\) has rational entries satisfying \(X\succeq0\), \(S\succeq0\), \(\mathcal A(X)=b\), \(S=C-\mathcal A^*(y)\), and \(\langle C,X\rangle-b^\top y=0\) exactly. Positive-semidefiniteness must be certified by an exact factorization, exact principal-minor test, or another exact algebraic certificate rather than by floating-point eigenvalue tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact arithmetic uses rational data and operations and accepts a PEP certificate only when feasibility, semidefiniteness, and zero duality gap are verified algebraically without tolerances.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal A\), \(b\), and \(C\) have rational coefficients.
The PEP admits a finite rational primal-dual certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((X,y,S)\) is an exactly verifiable optimality certificate.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the Exact-Arithmetic Regime container and is mathematically coherent under the stated rational-certificate assumption. However, no inspectable citation supports the PEP-specific primal-dual certificate formulation or the proposed exact PSD-verification mechanisms.

children.title: Precision Escalation Criteria
children.top_down_role: Numerical signals motivating a transition to higher precision.

knowledge_statements.title: Precision Escalation Criteria
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Trigger conditions for increasing numerical precision in a solved PEP relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given tolerances \(\tau_p,\tau_d,\tau_g,\tau_\lambda>0\), precision must be escalated whenever a computed primal-dual triple \((\widehat X,\widehat y,\widehat S)\) satisfies at least one of \(\|\mathcal A(\widehat X)-b\|>\tau_p\), \(\|C-\mathcal A^*(\widehat y)-\widehat S\|>\tau_d\), \(|\langle C,\widehat X\rangle-b^\top\widehat y|>\tau_g\), \(\lambda_{\min}(\widehat X)<-\tau_\lambda\), or \(\lambda_{\min}(\widehat S)<-\tau_\lambda\). Escalation is also required when repeated solves at increasing precision fail to stabilize the objective or reconstructed certificate within their prescribed tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Increase precision when primal or dual residuals, the duality gap, semidefinite violations, or cross-precision instability exceed their acceptance thresholds.
assumptions_latex: A primal-dual PEP semidefinite formulation and residual norms are fixed.
All acceptance tolerances are positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Failure of any displayed test triggers a solve at strictly greater arithmetic precision.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits the escalation-criteria container, but the claim that precision must be escalated for exactly these tests is a solver policy rather than a universal mathematical rule. A PEP reliability or numerical SDP source with specific residual, eigenvalue, gap, and cross-precision criteria is required.

children.title: Exact-Recovery Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Cases where numerical results do not support reliable exact reconstruction.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact-Recovery Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation conditions governing rational reconstruction from approximate PEP certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let an unknown certificate coefficient be a reduced rational number \(r=p/q\) with \(1\le q\le Q\). If an approximation \(\widehat r\) satisfies \(|\widehat r-r|<1/(2Q^2)\), then at most one reduced rational with denominator at most \(Q\) lies in that error interval, so bounded-denominator rational reconstruction is unambiguous. At or beyond this boundary, uniqueness is not guaranteed: two distinct reduced rationals of denominators at most \(Q\) may be consistent with the approximation. Matrix recovery additionally requires the reconstructed entries to satisfy every affine constraint and an exact positive-semidefinite certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bounded-denominator rational recovery is unique below the half-inverse-square error threshold; outside it, competing rationals may fit and exact feasibility must decide validity.
assumptions_latex: The target coefficient is rational with reduced denominator at most \(Q\).
The reconstruction procedure searches only denominators at most \(Q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The bound \(|\widehat r-r|<1/(2Q^2)\) is a sufficient uniqueness region, not a guarantee beyond its boundary.
review_flags: matrix-level PEP recovery conditions need sourcing

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The scalar separation bound and its interpretation as a sufficient uniqueness region are mathematically plausible and fit the failure-boundary container. No cited theorem supports the bounded-denominator reconstruction threshold, and the additional matrix-level affine-feasibility and exact-PSD requirements also lack PEP-specific sourcing.

children.title: Horizon Growth
children.top_down_role: Computational scaling as the number of modeled iterations increases.

knowledge_statements.title: Horizon Growth
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dimension growth of a Gram-form PEP as the iteration horizon increases.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a horizon-\(N\) PEP in which each iteration introduces at most \(a\) new vector records and \(b\) new scalar records, while \(r_0\) vector and \(s_0\) scalar records are fixed initially. Then the Gram matrix order and scalar-record count obey \(r_N\le r_0+aN\) and \(s_N\le s_0+bN\). A dense semidefinite representation therefore contains at most \(r_N(r_N+1)/2+s_N=O(N^2)\) scalar primal variables, although the number of algorithmic and interpolation constraints may follow a different growth law.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With a bounded number of new records per iteration, Gram order grows linearly with horizon and the dense scalar representation grows quadratically.
assumptions_latex: Each iteration adds at most \(a\) vector and \(b\) scalar records.
No record elimination or symmetry reduction is applied.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The dense PEP variable count is \(O(N^2)\) as \(N\to\infty\).

notation.meaning: Gram matrix order at horizon N
number of scalar records at horizon N

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound kind fits Horizon Growth, and the conditional linear record bounds imply the stated quadratic upper bound for a dense representation. An inspectable PEP source is still required to support the record model and its interpretation as the relevant Gram-form formulation.

children.title: Oracle-Record Growth
children.top_down_role: Computational scaling as stored oracle observations increase.

knowledge_statements.title: Oracle-Record Growth
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Growth induced by storing oracle outputs at queried points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a PEP contains \(q_N\) oracle calls through horizon \(N\), and each call stores at most \(u\) new vector outputs and \(v\) new scalar outputs. If \(r_0\) vector records and \(s_0\) scalar records predate the calls, then \(r_N\le r_0+u q_N\) and \(s_N\le s_0+v q_N\). When pairwise interpolation constraints are imposed between all oracle records, their number is at most \(q_N(q_N-1)=O(q_N^2)\) for ordered pairs, even though the record counts themselves grow only linearly in \(q_N\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Oracle storage grows linearly with the number of calls, while all-pairs interpolation constraints can grow quadratically.
assumptions_latex: Each oracle call creates at most \(u\) vector and \(v\) scalar records.
Interpolation constraints are generated for every ordered pair of distinct oracle records.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Record storage is \(O(q_N)\), whereas pairwise interpolation contributes \(O(q_N^2)\) constraints.

notation.meaning: number of oracle calls through horizon N
per-call vector and scalar record bounds
resulting vector and scalar record counts

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conditional counting argument is coherent and the complexity-bound kind fits Oracle-Record Growth. No source is supplied for the PEP oracle-record convention or for the use of one interpolation constraint per ordered pair of distinct records.

children.title: Record-Reuse Regimes
children.top_down_role: Effects of shared, repeated, or compressed oracle records.

knowledge_statements.title: Record-Reuse Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions under which multiple PEP occurrences may share one stored record.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Two occurrences may reuse one PEP record precisely when the model asserts that they represent the same mathematical vector or scalar and every constraint involving either occurrence remains valid after their identification. Formally, if occurrences indexed by \(i\) and \(j\) are merged, the quotient model adds \(z_i=z_j\) and substitutes one representative throughout all algorithmic, oracle, interpolation, and performance constraints. Reuse is exact only if this quotient preserves the feasible performance values: \(\{\Phi(w):w\in\mathcal F,\ z_i=z_j\}=\{\Phi(\bar w):\bar w\in\bar{\mathcal F}\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Records may be reused only when their equality is part of the model and quotienting by that equality preserves all feasible performance values.
assumptions_latex: The original feasible set \(\mathcal F\) and performance map \(\Phi\) are specified.
The proposed identification is imposed consistently in every constraint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed equality of attainable performance sets characterizes exact record reuse.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind is appropriate, and equality of attainable performance sets is a valid exactness criterion. The asserted characterization of permissible PEP record reuse and the quotient-model construction require an inspectable source; none is provided.

children.title: Growth Bottlenecks
children.top_down_role: Model components that dominate memory or solver cost at larger scales.

knowledge_statements.title: Growth Bottlenecks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dense algebraic bottlenecks caused by horizon-coupled PEP record growth.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r_N\) be the Gram matrix order and \(m_N\) the number of affine constraints in a dense horizon-\(N\) PEP semidefinite program. Explicit storage of the Gram variable requires \(\Theta(r_N^2)\) scalars, while a dense eigenvalue or Cholesky-type factorization requires \(\Theta(r_N^3)\) arithmetic operations. An interior-point Newton system formed in constraint space can require \(\Theta(m_N^2)\) storage and \(\Theta(m_N^3)\) dense factorization work. Thus linear record growth and quadratic interpolation growth can respectively induce cubic cone algebra and still higher constraint-system costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dense Gram factorization is cubic in record count, and dense Newton-system factorization is cubic in the number of constraints, creating the principal scalability bottlenecks.
assumptions_latex: The PEP matrices and Newton systems are treated as dense.
Classical dense direct factorizations are used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Storage and factorization costs scale as \(\Theta(r_N^2)\), \(\Theta(r_N^3)\), \(\Theta(m_N^2)\), and \(\Theta(m_N^3)\) in the stated model.
review_flags: bounds exclude sparsity and iterative linear algebra

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record correctly confines its asymptotic claims to dense storage and classical direct factorization, and the complexity-bound kind fits Growth Bottlenecks. Specific numerical-linear-algebra or SDP-solver sources are required for the stated Theta costs and their application to PEP Newton systems.

children.title: Sparsity Structure
children.top_down_role: Sparse coupling patterns in finite-dimensional performance-estimation models.

knowledge_statements.title: Sparsity Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Aggregate matrix sparsity graph of a semidefinite PEP representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For symmetric coefficient matrices \(C,A_1,\ldots,A_m\in\mathbb S^n\), the aggregate sparsity graph is the undirected graph \(G=(V,E)\) with \(V=\{1,\ldots,n\}\) and \(\{i,j\}\in E\) for \(i\ne j\) exactly when at least one matrix among \(C,A_1,\ldots,A_m\) has a nonzero \((i,j)\) entry. Diagonal positions are retained implicitly. This graph records which Gram entries can participate directly in the objective or affine constraints; absent edges identify entries omitted by the sparse data representation, not entries automatically equal to zero in every positive-semidefinite completion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The aggregate sparsity graph joins indices that co-occur in a nonzero off-diagonal coefficient; missing edges denote unspecified sparse-data positions, not necessarily zero completed entries.
assumptions_latex: The PEP is expressed using symmetric coefficient matrices of a common order \(n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G\) is the aggregate sparsity pattern governing sparse semidefinite representations.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition matches the Sparsity Structure leaf and correctly distinguishes absent sparse-data positions from entries forced to zero in a PSD completion. It nevertheless lacks an inspectable sparse-SDP source defining aggregate sparsity and supporting that completion interpretation.

children.title: Chordal Structure
children.top_down_role: Graph structure supporting decomposed semidefinite representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Chordal Structure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Chordality of the aggregate PEP sparsity graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An aggregate sparsity graph \(G=(V,E)\) is chordal when every cycle of length at least four contains an edge joining two nonconsecutive vertices of that cycle. Equivalently, \(G\) admits a perfect elimination ordering \((v_1,\ldots,v_n)\): for each \(k\), the neighbors of \(v_k\) lying in \(\{v_{k+1},\ldots,v_n\}\) form a clique. The maximal cliques induced by such an ordering determine the principal submatrices used in chordal positive-semidefinite completion and decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sparsity graph is chordal when every long cycle has a chord, equivalently when it has a perfect elimination ordering; its maximal cliques define local PSD blocks.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is a finite undirected graph.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Chordality is equivalent to the existence of a perfect elimination ordering.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and perfect-elimination-ordering equivalence fit the Chordal Structure container and are stated consistently. A graph-theoretic source and a sparse-SDP source with specific theorem or section locators are required for the equivalence and clique-based PSD application.

children.title: Chordal Decomposition Regimes
children.top_down_role: Computational settings where clique-based decomposition is advantageous.

knowledge_statements.title: Chordal Decomposition Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Clique decomposition and completion forms for chordal sparse PSD constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be chordal with maximal cliques \(C_1,\ldots,C_p\), and let \(E_k\) select the coordinates indexed by \(C_k\). A partial symmetric matrix \(X\) specified on the diagonal and edges of \(G\) has a positive-semidefinite completion if and only if \(E_kXE_k^\top\succeq0\) for every \(k\). Dually, every sparse matrix \(Z\succeq0\) whose off-pattern entries vanish admits a clique decomposition \(Z=\sum_{k=1}^p E_k^\top Z_kE_k\) with \(Z_k\succeq0\). Consistency constraints on clique overlaps are required when separate clique variables represent one global partial matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For chordal sparsity, PSD completion is equivalent to PSD clique submatrices, while sparse PSD matrices decompose into embedded PSD clique blocks with overlap consistency.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is chordal and \(C_1,\ldots,C_p\) are all maximal cliques.
Matrix entries are specified on every diagonal position and edge of \(G\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Global sparse semidefinite structure is represented exactly by clique PSD constraints or embedded clique-cone sums, with the appropriate overlap equations.
review_flags: chordal PSD completion and cone-decomposition theorem source required

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind is appropriate, and the record distinguishes the PSD-completion theorem from the dual sparse-cone decomposition. These are nontrivial theorems requiring precise citations; no source is supplied for either equivalence or for the overlap-consistency formulation.

children.title: Fill-In Effects
children.top_down_role: Scalability loss caused by additional couplings introduced during decomposition.

knowledge_statements.title: Fill-In Effects
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complexity impact of chordal extensions introduced during sparse PEP factorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a nonchordal aggregate sparsity graph and \(G^+=(V,E\cup F)\) a chordal extension, where \(F\) is the set of fill edges. Every fill edge introduces an additional matrix position into the extended sparsity pattern and may enlarge the maximal cliques. If the maximal clique sizes of \(G^+\) are \(c_1,\ldots,c_p\), storing dense symmetric clique blocks requires \(\Theta(\sum_k c_k^2)\) scalars and factoring them requires \(\Theta(\sum_k c_k^3)\) arithmetic operations. Consequently, extension orderings with larger fill or cliques can erase the benefit of original sparsity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Chordal fill adds matrix positions and can enlarge cliques; clique storage is quadratic and dense factorization cubic in clique sizes, so excessive fill destroys sparsity gains.
assumptions_latex: A chordal extension \(G^+\) is used for sparse semidefinite decomposition.
Each clique block is stored and factored densely.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The decomposition costs are \(\Theta(\sum_k c_k^2)\) in storage and \(\Theta(\sum_k c_k^3)\) in factorization work.

notation.meaning: order of the k-th maximal clique

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind fits Fill-In Effects, and the stated costs are coherent for separately stored and densely factored clique blocks. An inspectable sparse-factorization or chordal-SDP source is required for the fill-in interpretation and the summed clique-size complexity bounds.

children.title: Symmetry-Reduced Models
children.top_down_role: Reduced PEP formulations obtained from invariant problem structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Symmetry-Reduced Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact invariant-subspace reduction of symmetric PEP semidefinite models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a finite group \(\Gamma\) act orthogonally through matrices \(P_\gamma\) on a PEP semidefinite variable \(X\in\mathbb S^n\). Assume that the feasible set is convex and invariant under \(X\mapsto P_\gamma X P_\gamma^\top\), and that the linear objective is invariant under the same action. Then every feasible \(X\) may be replaced without changing its objective value by the Reynolds average \(\bar X=|\Gamma|^{-1}\sum_{\gamma\in\Gamma}P_\gamma X P_\gamma^\top\). Therefore the original problem and its restriction to the fixed-point subspace \(\{X\in\mathbb S^n:P_\gamma X P_\gamma^\top=X\text{ for every }\gamma\in\Gamma\}\) have the same infimum. If the original problem attains its optimum, an optimal solution exists in this fixed-point subspace, which may be block-diagonalized according to the real invariant components of the representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a convex group-invariant PEP, averaging any feasible Gram matrix over the finite group preserves feasibility and objective value. Restricting the problem to the block-diagonalizable fixed-point subspace therefore preserves the infimum, and it preserves an attained optimum when one exists.
assumptions_latex: \(\Gamma\) is finite, and \(P_\gamma\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) is orthogonal for every \(\gamma\in\Gamma\).
The feasible set is convex and invariant under \(X\mapsto P_\gamma X P_\gamma^\top\).
The objective is linear and invariant under the group action.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The original PEP and its fixed-point restriction have the same infimum; if the original optimum is attained, the restriction contains an optimal solution.

notation.meaning: orthogonal matrix representing the group element gamma
semidefinite decision matrix in the space of real symmetric n-by-n matrices

review_flags: optimum existence made conditional on attainment

children.title: Surrogate Models
children.top_down_role: Simplified formulations used to approximate computational behavior or bounds.

knowledge_statements.title: Surrogate Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a reduced computational proxy for a full semidefinite performance-estimation problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Theta_0\) be a parameter set. For each \(\theta\in\Theta_0\), let the full maximization problem \(P(\theta)\) have feasible set \(\mathcal F(\theta)\subseteq\mathcal X_\theta\), objective \(c_\theta:\mathcal F(\theta)\to\mathbb R\), and finite value \(v(\theta)=\sup_{x\in\mathcal F(\theta)}c_\theta(x)\). A surrogate model consists of a reduced feasible set \(\widehat{\mathcal F}(\theta)\), a reduced objective \(\widehat c_\theta:\widehat{\mathcal F}(\theta)\to\mathbb R\), and a lift \(L_\theta:\widehat{\mathcal F}(\theta)\to\mathcal F(\theta)\), with finite value \(\widehat v(\theta)=\sup_{z\in\widehat{\mathcal F}(\theta)}\widehat c_\theta(z)\). It is an exact surrogate on \(\Theta_0\) when \(c_\theta(L_\theta z)=\widehat c_\theta(z)\) for every reduced feasible point and, for every \(x\in\mathcal F(\theta)\) and every \(\delta>0\), there exists \(z\in\widehat{\mathcal F}(\theta)\) such that \(\widehat c_\theta(z)\geq c_\theta(x)-\delta\). It is an \(\varepsilon\)-surrogate on \(\Theta_0\) when \(|v(\theta)-\widehat v(\theta)|\leq\varepsilon(\theta)\) for every \(\theta\in\Theta_0\), where \(\varepsilon:\Theta_0\to[0,+\infty)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A surrogate is a reduced maximization problem with a feasible lift. It is exact when lifted reduced objectives preserve values and can approximate every full feasible objective arbitrarily closely; it is an epsilon-surrogate when its optimal value has the stated uniform pointwise error.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal F(\theta)\) and \(\widehat{\mathcal F}(\theta)\) are nonempty for every \(\theta\in\Theta_0\).
\(v(\theta)\) and \(\widehat v(\theta)\) are finite for every \(\theta\in\Theta_0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Under the exactness conditions, \(\widehat v(\theta)=v(\theta)\) for every \(\theta\in\Theta_0\); under the error condition, \(|v(\theta)-\widehat v(\theta)|\leq\varepsilon(\theta)\).

notation.meaning: Ambient space of the full problem at parameter theta.
Map lifting reduced feasible points to full feasible points.
Allowed discrepancy between full and surrogate optimal values.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: feasible lifting and quantified objective approximation characterize value fidelity

children.title: Reduction Fidelity
children.top_down_role: Preservation of worst-case values under structural model reduction.

knowledge_statements.title: Reduction Fidelity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantifies how faithfully a reduced maximization PEP reproduces the full problem's feasible objectives and optimal value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) and \(\widehat P\) be maximization problems with nonempty feasible sets \(\mathcal F\) and \(\widehat{\mathcal F}\), objectives \(c:\mathcal F\to\mathbb R\) and \(\widehat c:\widehat{\mathcal F}\to\mathbb R\), and finite values \(v=\sup_{x\in\mathcal F}c(x)\) and \(\widehat v=\sup_{z\in\widehat{\mathcal F}}\widehat c(z)\). Suppose \(\delta_L,\delta_R\geq0\) and maps \(L:\widehat{\mathcal F}\to\mathcal F\) and \(R:\mathcal F\to\widehat{\mathcal F}\) satisfy \(|c(Lz)-\widehat c(z)|\leq\delta_L\) for every \(z\in\widehat{\mathcal F}\) and \(|\widehat c(Rx)-c(x)|\leq\delta_R\) for every \(x\in\mathcal F\). Then \((L,R,\delta_L,\delta_R)\) is a reduction-fidelity certificate and \(|v-\widehat v|\leq\max\{\delta_L,\delta_R\}\). Exact fidelity corresponds to \(\delta_L=\delta_R=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For two maximization problems, feasible transfer maps with uniform objective-distortion bounds in both directions certify that their optimal values differ by no more than the larger distortion.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal F\) and \(\widehat{\mathcal F}\) are nonempty.
\(v\) and \(\widehat v\) are finite.
\(L\) and \(R\) preserve feasibility on their stated domains.
\(\delta_L,\delta_R\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|v-\widehat v|\leq\max\{\delta_L,\delta_R\}\).

notation.meaning: Lifting and reduction maps between the feasible sets.
Nonnegative uniform objective-distortion bounds for the two maps.
Finite supremal values of the full and reduced maximization problems.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: bidirectional feasible objective approximation bounds the two supremal values

children.title: Surrogate Validity Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Regimes where a simplified model no longer represents the target PEP reliably.

knowledge_statements.title: Surrogate Validity Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifies circumstances in which an established reduced-PEP certificate no longer guarantees transfer to the full model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a surrogate certificate establish \(|v(\theta)-\widehat v(\theta)|\leq\varepsilon(\theta)\) for every \(\theta\in\Theta_0\), using a lift \(L_\theta\) that maps every \(z\in\widehat{\mathcal F}(\theta)\) into \(\mathcal F(\theta)\) and a stated objective-distortion bound. The certificate provides no conclusion for \(\theta\notin\Theta_0\). For \(\theta\in\Theta_0\), if lift feasibility or the objective-distortion bound is not verified, that certificate alone no longer establishes an upper or lower bound for \(v(\theta)\). For a maximization PEP, deleting a full constraint enlarges the feasible set; if the deletion permits a point with objective greater than \(v(\theta)\), then \(\widehat v(\theta)>v(\theta)\). Merely deleting a constraint that is active at some optimizer does not by itself imply a strict value change.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A surrogate guarantee applies only on its certified parameter class and while its lift and distortion hypotheses are verified. Failure to verify them removes the guarantee but does not alone prove that the surrogate value is wrong; an omitted constraint changes the value only when it admits a better feasible objective.
assumptions_latex: \(P(\theta)\) and the concrete omitted-constraint surrogate are maximization problems.
\(v(\theta)\) and \(\widehat v(\theta)\) denote their finite supremal values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Outside \(\Theta_0\), or without verified lift-feasibility and distortion hypotheses, the stated surrogate certificate alone does not justify value transfer from \(\widehat P(\theta)\) to \(P(\theta)\).

notation.meaning: Parameter class on which the surrogate certificate was established.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: certificate conclusions require their stated domain and hypotheses

knowledge_statements.title: Primal-Dual Residual Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses normalized SDP residuals and the duality gap to assess numerical PEP certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the primal SDP \(p^\star=\min\{\langle C,X\rangle:\mathcal A(X)=b,\ X\succeq0\}\) and its dual \(d^\star=\max\{b^\top y:C-\mathcal A^*y=S,\ S\succeq0\}\). For computed \((X,y,S)\), define \(r_p=\|\mathcal A(X)-b\|/(1+\|b\|)\), \(r_d=\|C-\mathcal A^*y-S\|_F/(1+\|C\|_F)\), cone violations \(r_X=\max\{0,-\lambda_{\min}(X)\}/(1+\|X\|_2)\) and \(r_S=\max\{0,-\lambda_{\min}(S)\}/(1+\|S\|_2)\), and \(r_g=|\langle C,X\rangle-b^\top y|/(1+|\langle C,X\rangle|+|b^\top y|)\). If all five residuals do not exceed prescribed tolerances, they certify numerical approximate primal-dual feasibility and agreement, but not exact feasibility without validated rounding.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Small normalized equality, cone, and gap residuals certify an approximately feasible and mutually consistent primal-dual SDP solution, subject to the chosen tolerances.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal A\) is linear between finite-dimensional Euclidean spaces.
All displayed norms and eigenvalues are evaluated with sufficient numerical accuracy.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\max\{r_p,r_d,r_X,r_S,r_g\}\leq\tau\) certifies \(\tau\)-level numerical primal-dual consistency under the stated normalization.

notation.meaning: Adjoint of the SDP equality-constraint operator.
Normalized primal and dual equality residuals.
Cone violations and normalized primal-dual gap.

source_refs.source_title: Convex Analysis and Minimization Algorithms II: Advanced Theory and Bundle Methods

source_witnesses.source_title: Convex Analysis and Minimization Algorithms II: Advanced Theory and Bundle Methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited convex-duality section may support primal-dual optimality generally, but it does not inspectably support these particular SDP residual normalizations, eigenvalue-based cone violations, or their interpretation as a numerical certificate. A numerical SDP source with a section or page covering stopping residuals is required.

children.title: Conditioning Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Indicators of sensitivity arising from poorly scaled or nearly singular numerical formulations.

knowledge_statements.title: Conditioning Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Flags sensitivity of a PEP linear system or Schur complement through singular values and backward error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a computed solution \(z\) of \(Kz=q\), let \(\sigma_{\max}(K)\) and \(\sigma_{\min}(K)\) be the largest and smallest singular values. Define \(\kappa_2(K)=\sigma_{\max}(K)/\sigma_{\min}(K)\), with \(\kappa_2(K)=+\infty\) when \(\sigma_{\min}(K)=0\), and define the normwise backward error \(\eta(z)=\|Kz-q\|_2/(\|K\|_2\|z\|_2+\|q\|_2)\). Given thresholds \(\kappa_{\max}\) and \(\eta_{\max}\), the solve passes the conditioning diagnostic exactly when \(\kappa_2(K)\leq\kappa_{\max}\) and \(\eta(z)\leq\eta_{\max}\). A small backward error without the conditioning inequality does not establish small forward error.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A linear solve passes when both its condition number and normalized backward error meet thresholds; a tiny residual alone is insufficient for an ill-conditioned system.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is a finite-dimensional real or complex matrix.
The denominator defining \(\eta(z)\) is nonzero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\kappa_2(K)\leq\kappa_{\max}\) and \(\eta(z)\leq\eta_{\max}\) constitute the joint pass condition.

notation.meaning: Spectral condition number of the diagnostic matrix.
Normwise backward error of the computed solve.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: singular-value conditioning and normwise backward error are standard numerical-linear-algebra diagnostics
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The singular-value condition number and backward-error formula are mathematically standard and fit the diagnostic container, but no inspectable source supports the formula, the joint pass rule, or threshold selection.

children.title: Numerical Rank Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Rank estimates, rank ambiguity, and apparent degeneracy in computed matrix data.

knowledge_statements.title: Numerical Rank Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines tolerance-dependent numerical rank and a stability check based on adjacent singular-value separation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have singular values \(\sigma_1\geq\cdots\geq\sigma_s\geq0\), where \(s=\min\{m,n\}\). For an absolute threshold \(\tau>0\), define \(r_\tau(M)=|\{i:\sigma_i>\tau\}|\). For relative threshold \(\rho>0\), take \(\tau=\rho\sigma_1\) when \(\sigma_1>0\). A reported rank \(r\) passes the separation diagnostic when \(\sigma_r>\tau\geq\sigma_{r+1}\) and the gap ratio \(\sigma_r/\max\{\sigma_{r+1},\tau_{\mathrm{floor}}\}\) exceeds a prescribed \(\gamma>1\), using \(\sigma_0=+\infty\) and \(\sigma_{s+1}=0\) at the endpoints. Otherwise the numerical rank is tolerance-sensitive.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Numerical rank counts singular values above a threshold and is considered stable only when a prescribed gap separates retained and discarded singular values.
assumptions_latex: \(\tau_{\mathrm{floor}}>0\) prevents division by zero in the gap diagnostic.
Singular values are computed to accuracy commensurate with \(\tau\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The numerical rank is \(r_\tau(M)\); it is diagnostically stable only when the threshold and gap conditions hold.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: thresholded singular values define numerical rank and spectral separation measures its stability
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Thresholded numerical rank is standard, but the additional gap-ratio pass rule, floor parameter, and prescribed threshold conventions are unsourced. An authoritative numerical linear algebra locator is required.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Numerical ε-Rank and Its Robustness Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines spectral-norm numerical rank and states its singular-value characterization and reliability condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a matrix \(A\) and tolerance \(\epsilon\ge 0\), its numerical \(\epsilon\)-rank is
\[
r_\epsilon(A)=\min_{\|E\|_2\le \epsilon}\operatorname{rank}(A+E).
\]
If \(\sigma_1\ge\sigma_2\ge\cdots\) are the singular values of \(A\), then \(r_\epsilon\) is characterized by
\[
\sigma_{r_\epsilon}>\epsilon\ge\sigma_{r_\epsilon+1}.
\]
The numerical-rank interpretation is reliable only when this threshold separates a well-determined singular-value gap and the resulting rank is stable under small perturbations of \(\epsilon\) and of the singular values; without such a gap, a numerical rank should not be assigned.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The numerical epsilon-rank of a matrix is the smallest rank attainable by a perturbation whose spectral norm is at most epsilon. Equivalently, it counts the singular values strictly exceeding epsilon. This rank is meaningful only when the threshold lies in a clear, perturbation-stable singular-value gap.
assumptions_latex: A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\text{ or }\mathbb{C}^{m\times n}
\epsilon\ge 0
\sigma_1\ge\sigma_2\ge\cdots\ge 0\text{ are the singular values of }A
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: r_\epsilon(A)=\min_{\|E\|_2\le\epsilon}\operatorname{rank}(A+E),\qquad \sigma_{r_\epsilon}>\epsilon\ge\sigma_{r_\epsilon+1},\text{ with a stable spectral gap required for a robust rank interpretation.}
