children.title: Tolerance Sensitivity Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Changes in validation outcomes across feasibility, optimality, and rank tolerances.

knowledge_statements.title: Tolerance Sensitivity Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tests whether reported PEP values and residual classifications remain stable over a prescribed tolerance grid.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T=\{\tau_1,\ldots,\tau_k\}\) be solver tolerances, and let a fixed PEP instance produce objective estimates \(v_i\), residual vectors \(r_i\), and status labels \(s_i\) at \(\tau_i\). With reference scale \(V=1+\max_i|v_i|\), define \(\Delta_v=\max_{i,j}|v_i-v_j|/V\) and \(\Delta_r=\max_{i,j}\|r_i-r_j\|_\infty/(1+\max_\ell\|r_\ell\|_\infty)\). For prescribed limits \(\epsilon_v\) and \(\epsilon_r\), the computation is tolerance-stable on \(T\) exactly when \(\Delta_v\leq\epsilon_v\), \(\Delta_r\leq\epsilon_r\), and all \(s_i\) agree. This condition concerns the tested grid only and does not imply stability at untested tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeated solves are tolerance-stable when their normalized objectives and residuals vary little and their status labels agree across the tested tolerance grid.
assumptions_latex: All runs use the same mathematical instance and objective normalization.
Only numerical tolerances vary across the compared runs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Delta_v\leq\epsilon_v\), \(\Delta_r\leq\epsilon_r\), and \(s_1=\cdots=s_k\) define tolerance stability on \(T\).

notation.meaning: Finite grid of tested numerical tolerances.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: controlled parameter sweeps quantify numerical sensitivity by output variation
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-grid comparison is internally coherent and properly limits its conclusion to tested tolerances, but the exact normalization and pass thresholds are a local diagnostic protocol without inspectable support.

children.title: Diagnostic Interaction Patterns
children.top_down_role: Cases where conditioning, numerical rank, or tolerance choices produce coupled diagnostic signals.

knowledge_statements.title: Diagnostic Interaction Patterns
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combines conditioning, rank, residual, and tolerance signals into reproducible interaction classifications.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each run, let \(c\) denote failure of the conditioning thresholds, \(q\) failure of numerical-rank separation, \(p\) failure of primal-dual residual thresholds, and \(t\) failure of tolerance stability. Define the interaction signature \(I=(c,q,p,t)\in\{0,1\}^4\). The patterns \((1,1,0,1)\) and \((1,1,1,1)\) indicate that apparent rank and output instability coexist with ill-conditioning; \((0,0,1,0)\) isolates a residual inconsistency not explained by these conditioning or rank tests; and \((0,0,0,0)\) records simultaneous passage. These signatures are diagnostic classifications, not causal conclusions: causation requires a controlled perturbation or higher-accuracy rerun.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A four-bit signature records interacting diagnostic failures, distinguishes isolated residual problems from coupled conditioning-rank instability, and avoids treating correlation as causation.
assumptions_latex: Each component flag is computed using fixed, documented thresholds.
The four diagnostics refer to the same PEP instance and numerical run family.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(I=(c,q,p,t)\) provides a reproducible joint classification but does not by itself identify a causal failure mechanism.

notation.meaning: Conditioning, rank, primal-dual, and tolerance failure indicators.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Boolean signatures provide a checkable representation of jointly observed diagnostic outcomes
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The four-bit signature is a reproducible representation, but the selected patterns and their interpretations are locally invented rather than established mathematical properties. Evidence or empirical validation is needed for the asserted interaction meanings.

children.title: Cross-Solver Agreement Checks
children.top_down_role: Consistency of objectives, residuals, statuses, and certificates across solver implementations.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Solver Agreement Checks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compares independently configured solvers using normalized objectives, residuals, and status classifications.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Run solvers \(S_1,\ldots,S_k\) on the same PEP formulation and scaling. Let solver \(S_i\) return objective \(v_i\), residual summary \(r_i\), and status \(s_i\). Define \(D_v=\max_{i,j}|v_i-v_j|/(1+\max_\ell|v_\ell|)\) and \(D_r=\max_{i,j}\|r_i-r_j\|_\infty/(1+\max_\ell\|r_\ell\|_\infty)\). For prescribed tolerances \(\epsilon_v\) and \(\epsilon_r\), cross-solver agreement holds when \(D_v\leq\epsilon_v\), \(D_r\leq\epsilon_r\), and all status labels are compatible under a declared status map. Agreement is corroborative evidence only; shared modeling or scaling errors may affect every solver.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solvers agree when normalized objective and residual discrepancies meet thresholds and mapped statuses are compatible, although common modeling errors can survive the comparison.
assumptions_latex: Every solver receives the same mathematical formulation, data, and scaling.
Solver-specific statuses are translated by a documented compatibility map.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_v\leq\epsilon_v\), \(D_r\leq\epsilon_r\), and compatible statuses constitute cross-solver agreement.

notation.meaning: Largest normalized objective discrepancy across solvers.
Largest normalized residual discrepancy across solvers.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: independent implementations are compared through normalized outputs and compatible statuses
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The check fits the leaf and appropriately treats agreement as corroborative only, but the discrepancy normalization, tolerances, and compatible-status mapping are unsupported and materially determine the condition.

children.title: Cross-Precision Stability Checks
children.top_down_role: Stability of computed conclusions across arithmetic precision levels.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Precision Stability Checks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Checks invariance of a fixed solver configuration under increasing arithmetic precision.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a solver, formulation, scaling, and stopping rule, and run them at precisions \(p_1<\cdots<p_k\). Let \(v_i\), \(r_i\), and \(s_i\) be the objective, residual vector, and status at precision \(p_i\). Relative to the highest-precision run, define \(E_v(i)=|v_i-v_k|/(1+|v_k|)\) and \(E_r(i)=\|r_i-r_k\|_\infty/(1+\|r_k\|_\infty)\). Cross-precision stability holds on the tested set when \(E_v(i)\leq\epsilon_v\), \(E_r(i)\leq\epsilon_r\), and \(s_i\) is compatible with \(s_k\) for every \(i\). Monotone decrease of these errors strengthens, but is not required by, the check.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A computation is stable across tested precisions when objectives, residuals, and statuses remain close to the highest-precision run under fixed solver settings.
assumptions_latex: Precision is the only intentionally varied computational parameter.
The highest-precision output is used as a comparison reference, not presumed exact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\max_{i<k}E_v(i)\leq\epsilon_v\), \(\max_{i<k}E_r(i)\leq\epsilon_r\), and compatible statuses define cross-precision stability.

notation.meaning: Arithmetic precision used in run i.
Objective discrepancy from the highest-precision run.
Residual discrepancy from the highest-precision run.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: precision sweeps isolate finite-arithmetic sensitivity when other settings are fixed
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The statement correctly avoids treating the highest-precision run as exact, but the reference-run metric, compatibility rule, and stability thresholds are an unsourced local protocol.

children.title: Solver-Specific Discrepancy Tracing
children.top_down_role: Discrepancies attributable to solver conventions, preprocessing, scaling, or termination behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Solver-Specific Discrepancy Tracing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Localizes disagreement by controlled solver swaps and stagewise comparison of normalized outputs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a fixed PEP instance, solvers \(S_1,\ldots,S_k\), common tolerances, and discrepancy limits. First canonicalize formulation, scaling, and status labels. Run every solver and record \(z_i=(v_i,r_i,s_i)\). For each disagreeing pair, rerun after separately equalizing presolve, scaling, stopping criteria, and initialization; after each intervention compute \(d_{ij}=\max\{|v_i-v_j|/(1+\max\{|v_i|,|v_j|\}),\ \|r_i-r_j\|_\infty/(1+\max\{\|r_i\|_\infty,\|r_j\|_\infty\})\}\). Stop when agreement is restored or all interventions are exhausted. Output the earliest intervention that removes the discrepancy, together with all run records; otherwise output an unresolved solver-dependent discrepancy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Run solvers under matched settings, equalize one solver feature at a time, and report the earliest intervention restoring agreement or an unresolved solver-dependent discrepancy.
assumptions_latex: All compared runs solve the same mathematical PEP instance.
Interventions change one documented solver feature at a time.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is a reproducible trace identifying the first agreement-restoring solver intervention or declaring the discrepancy unresolved.

notation.meaning: Objective, residual, and status record from solver i.
Combined normalized discrepancy for a solver pair.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: controlled one-factor interventions localize implementation-dependent discrepancies
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind and local container fit, but the tracing algorithm and intervention order are not sourced. Because the reported earliest intervention depends on the chosen ordering and may not identify a unique mechanism, an authoritative or explicitly validated protocol is required.

children.title: Precision-Induced Discrepancy Tracing
children.top_down_role: Discrepancies attributable to rounding, numerical resolution, or precision-sensitive classification.

knowledge_statements.title: Precision-Induced Discrepancy Tracing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates arithmetic-precision effects from solver and formulation effects through controlled precision escalation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a fixed PEP instance, solver configuration, precisions \(p_1<\cdots<p_k\), and agreement thresholds. Run the identical configuration at every precision and record \(z_i=(v_i,r_i,s_i)\). For each \(i<k\), compare \(z_i\) with \(z_k\) using normalized objective and residual discrepancies. If the discrepancies cross below threshold at some precision, return the least \(p_j\) for which every run at precision at least \(p_j\) agrees with the highest-precision run. If discrepancies persist, repeat at the two highest precisions with tighter stopping tolerances. Output precision-induced discrepancy only when precision escalation changes the result while the tightened high-precision runs stabilize; otherwise output unresolved or stopping-rule-induced discrepancy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Escalate precision under fixed settings, find the least stable precision, and distinguish arithmetic effects from stopping-rule effects using tighter high-precision reruns.
assumptions_latex: The formulation, solver implementation, scaling, and initialization remain fixed across precisions.
At least two distinct arithmetic precisions are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure outputs a stability precision \(p_j\), a stopping-rule attribution, or an unresolved discrepancy classification.

notation.meaning: Objective, residual, and status record at precision i.
Least tested precision above which agreement persists.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: controlled precision escalation isolates finite-arithmetic effects from fixed model and solver choices
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind fits, but the rule for attributing a discrepancy to arithmetic precision versus stopping criteria lacks cited support. Status compatibility, exact discrepancy thresholds, and the tightened-rerun decision rule must be documented before the classification is reliable.

knowledge_statements.title: Certificate Replay
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic revalidation of a stored primal-dual PEP certificate under recorded tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a replay artifact contain PEP data \(D\), primal and dual candidates \((X,y)\), claimed bound \(B\), and tolerances \((\varepsilon_p,\varepsilon_d,\varepsilon_g)\). A deterministic verifier reconstructs the conic program from \(D\), computes primal infeasibility \(r_p\), dual infeasibility \(r_d\), and duality gap \(g\), and accepts exactly when \[r_p\leq\varepsilon_p,\qquad r_d\leq\varepsilon_d,\qquad |g|\leq\varepsilon_g,\] and the recomputed certified objective agrees with \(B\) within the recorded objective tolerance. Acceptance certifies numerical consistency of the archived certificate with the reconstructed PEP; it does not by itself certify that \(D\) faithfully models the intended algorithm and function class.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replay reconstructs the PEP and accepts a stored primal-dual certificate only when feasibility, gap, and objective discrepancies satisfy recorded tolerances.
assumptions_latex: The artifact fixes a deterministic reconstruction map from \(D\) to one conic PEP.
Residual norms, scaling conventions, and tolerances are recorded.
The verifier uses the archived numerical candidates without silently repairing them.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Replay acceptance implies tolerance-level primal-dual validity for the reconstructed PEP, but not semantic validity of the PEP model.

notation.meaning: serialized PEP definition and reconstruction data
archived primal and dual certificate candidates
recomputed primal residual, dual residual, and duality gap

review_flags: PEP-specific replay criterion lacks a supplied authoritative locator

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate content kind and local scope fit the Certificate Replay leaf, and the numerical-consistency limitation is appropriately stated. However, no source or inspectable locator supports the proposed PEP-specific acceptance criterion, including the residual, gap, and objective-tolerance conditions.

knowledge_statements.title: Worst-Case Instance Replay
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Re-execution of an archived finite-dimensional worst-case realization extracted from a PEP solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input an archived function-instance representation \(I\), initial state \(x_0\), method parameters \(\theta\), horizon \(N\), claimed trajectory \((\widehat{x}_k)_{k=0}^N\), and tolerance \(\varepsilon\). Reconstruct every oracle response prescribed by \(I\), initialize \(x_0\), and apply the recorded method recurrence to obtain \((x_k)_{k=0}^N\). Recompute the performance measure \(P_I(x_0,	heta,N)\). The replay succeeds when all method-side conditions hold and \[\max_{0\leq k\leq N}\|x_k-\widehat{x}_k\|\leq\varepsilon,\qquad |P_I(x_0,	heta,N)-\widehat{P}|\leq\varepsilon.\] Output the recomputed trajectory, performance value, residuals, and pass/fail decision.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reconstruct the archived worst-case instance, rerun the method, and compare its trajectory and performance with the stored realization.
assumptions_latex: The archived representation \(I\) defines evaluable oracle responses on every replayed query.
The recurrence and numerical comparison conventions are fully recorded.
The realization and method use compatible ambient dimensions and oracle semantics.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A successful replay verifies reproducibility of the archived realization within \(\varepsilon\); it does not prove global worst-case optimality.

notation.meaning: performance measure evaluated on the reconstructed instance

review_flags: No supplied source specifies a standard worst-case-instance replay protocol

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm content kind fits Worst-Case Instance Replay, and the statement correctly distinguishes reproducibility from global worst-case optimality. No cited source with a specific locator establishes this replay protocol or its success conditions.

children.title: Benchmark Provenance Records
children.top_down_role: Origins, identifiers, parameterizations, and revisions of benchmark instances.

knowledge_statements.title: Benchmark Provenance Records
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimum mathematical identity record for a PEP benchmark and its reported result.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A benchmark provenance record for a PEP computation is a tuple \[R_B=(\iota,
u,H,A,O,P,N,\rho),\] where \(\iota\) identifies the benchmark family, \(\nu\) identifies its immutable revision, \(H\) specifies the function or operator class and parameter domain, \(A\) specifies the algorithmic recurrence, \(O\) specifies admissible oracle information, \(P\) specifies the performance criterion and normalization, \(N\) is the horizon, and \(\rho\) identifies the serialized instance or generator. Two reported values are benchmark-comparable only if these fields agree, except for fields explicitly declared experimental variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A benchmark record identifies the exact problem class, method, oracle, criterion, horizon, normalization, and immutable benchmark revision.
assumptions_latex: Each identifier resolves to immutable content or a content digest.
Parameter domains and normalization conventions are represented explicitly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Equality of declared fixed fields is necessary for treating two outputs as results for the same benchmark.

notation.meaning: problem class, algorithm, oracle, and performance specifications

review_flags: Proposed provenance schema is not supported by the supplied optimization textbook locators

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition content kind fits the records leaf, but the proposed tuple and the benchmark-comparability rule are prescriptive schema claims without an authoritative provenance or reproducibility source.

children.title: Execution Environment Records
children.top_down_role: Hardware, operating-system, runtime, and numerical-backend context for reported runs.

knowledge_statements.title: Execution Environment Records
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Environment metadata required to interpret and reproduce a numerical PEP execution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An execution-environment record is a tuple \[R_E=(S,V,C,F,M,E,Q),\] where \(S\) identifies the operating platform, \(V\) the runtime and language versions, \(C\) the processor architecture, \(F\) floating-point and linear-algebra settings, \(M\) solver options and termination tolerances, \(E\) relevant environment variables, and \(Q\) random seeds and deterministic-execution settings. The record is replay-sufficient for an execution only if every environment component capable of changing program control flow, generated PEP data, solver termination, or reported residuals is either fixed by \(R_E\) or explicitly classified as uncontrolled.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An execution record fixes platform, runtime, arithmetic, solver settings, environment variables, seeds, and determinism controls affecting a PEP run.
assumptions_latex: Recorded values are captured at execution time rather than inferred afterward.
Sensitive values may be represented by reproducible nonsecret references or digests.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Replay sufficiency requires recording or declaring every environment component that can materially affect the reported computation.
review_flags: No supplied source establishes this execution-environment schema

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition content kind fits Execution Environment Records. The asserted fields and replay-sufficiency condition are plausible but schema-dependent, and no source with an inspectable locator supports them.

children.title: Versioned Dependency Records
children.top_down_role: Solver, library, package, and toolchain versions affecting reproducibility.

knowledge_statements.title: Versioned Dependency Records
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Content-addressed identification of software and solver dependencies used by a PEP artifact.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A versioned dependency record is a finite directed graph \(G=(V,E)\). Each vertex \(v\in V\) represents a direct or transitive dependency and stores its package identity, resolved version, source origin, content digest, build options, and platform-specific artifact identity. An edge \((u,v)\in E\) means that dependency \(u\) was resolved or built using \(v\). The record is exact when every executable component loaded by the benchmark, PEP generator, conic-modeling layer, solver, and certificate verifier is represented and each content digest matches the executed artifact.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dependency record is a complete content-addressed graph of the software, solver, libraries, and build choices used in an execution.
assumptions_latex: Dependency identities and digests are obtained from the resolved execution environment.
Edges distinguish direct and transitive resolution dependencies.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exactness holds only when the recorded graph covers every executable component affecting generation, solution, or verification.

notation.meaning: dependency relation from artifact u to artifact v

review_flags: No supplied source supports the proposed dependency-record completeness criterion

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition content kind fits Versioned Dependency Records. The graph representation is coherent, but the exactness criterion is a strong provenance requirement that lacks a supporting source and specific locator.

children.title: Provenance Completeness Checks
children.top_down_role: Coverage of the metadata needed to identify, rerun, and compare computational artifacts.

knowledge_statements.title: Provenance Completeness Checks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Checkable completeness predicate for reproducible PEP provenance bundles.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R=(R_B,R_E,R_D,R_O)\) be a provenance bundle containing benchmark, execution-environment, dependency, and output records. Define \(\operatorname{Complete}(R)=1\) exactly when: every required field is present and schema-valid; every identifier resolves or has a matching content digest; all cross-record identifiers and parameter values agree; all random, numerical, solver, and stopping conventions affecting the output are fixed or declared uncontrolled; and the output record links each reported bound, residual, certificate, and replay artifact to the execution that produced it. Otherwise \(\operatorname{Complete}(R)=0\). Completeness concerns traceability and does not imply mathematical correctness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Provenance is complete when required records resolve, agree across references, fix influential choices, and link every reported output to its execution.
assumptions_latex: A versioned schema specifies mandatory fields and consistency constraints.
Digest verification and identifier resolution are available for referenced artifacts.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\operatorname{Complete}(R)=1\), the bundle is traceability-complete under its schema, without thereby validating the modeled guarantee.

notation.meaning: benchmark, environment, dependency, and output records

review_flags: Completeness predicate is schema-dependent and lacks a supplied authoritative provenance standard

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition content kind correctly matches a completeness check. The predicate is explicitly schema-relative, but neither the governing schema nor an authoritative provenance standard is cited, so its required fields and completeness implications cannot be reviewed reliably.

children.title: Problem-Class Specification Drift
children.top_down_role: Departures between the modeled function class and the class governing the intended conclusion.

knowledge_statements.title: Problem-Class Specification Drift
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of guarantee when the implemented problem class differs from the class encoded by the PEP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{PEP}}(p)\) be the class encoded by a PEP with parameter vector \(p\), and let \(\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{run}}\) be the class actually used to interpret an implementation. Specification drift occurs when \(\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{run}}\nsubseteq\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{PEP}}(p)\), including disagreement in convexity, smoothness, strong-convexity constants, domain restrictions, dimension assumptions, or initial conditions. A bound \(P(f,A,N)\leq b\) certified only for every \(f\in\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{PEP}}(p)\) cannot be transferred to all \(f\in\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{run}}\) unless the required inclusion is independently established.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A PEP guarantee does not transfer to an entire deployed problem class when that class includes instances outside the class encoded by the certificate.
assumptions_latex: The certificate establishes \(P(f,A,N)\leq b\) only for every \(f\in\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{PEP}}(p)\).
The deployed interpretation admits at least one instance outside \(\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{PEP}}(p)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Without \(\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{run}}\subseteq\mathcal{F}_{\mathrm{PEP}}(p)\), the certified universal guarantee is not valid for the entire deployed class.

notation.meaning: problem class encoded by the PEP
problem class used in deployment or interpretation
performance of method A on instance f after N steps

review_flags: Exact PEP model-scope failure formulation lacks a supplied supporting locator

children.title: Oracle Capability Mismatch
children.top_down_role: Conflicts between assumed oracle outputs and the information actually available to the method.

knowledge_statements.title: Oracle Capability Mismatch
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mismatch between oracle information assumed by a PEP method and information available to the implemented method.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(k\), let \(\mathcal{I}^{\mathrm{PEP}}_k\) denote the information assumed available by the PEP recurrence and \(\mathcal{I}^{\mathrm{run}}_k\) the information returned by the deployed oracle. A capability mismatch occurs if some update map \(\Phi_k\) certified by the PEP is not measurable with respect to \(\mathcal{I}^{\mathrm{run}}_k\), although it is measurable with respect to \(\mathcal{I}^{\mathrm{PEP}}_k\). Then the certified recurrence \(x_{k+1}=\Phi_k(\mathcal{I}^{\mathrm{PEP}}_k)\) is not implementable using the deployed oracle, so its performance bound does not certify an implementation restricted to \(\mathcal{I}^{\mathrm{run}}_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a certified update needs information that the deployed oracle cannot provide, the PEP method is not implementable under that oracle and its bound does not transfer to such an implementation.
assumptions_latex: Updates must be measurable functions only of information available through the declared oracle and prior history.
The deployed oracle provides insufficient information for at least one certified update.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Nonmeasurability of some \(\Phi_k\) with respect to \(\mathcal{I}^{\mathrm{run}}_k\) places an implementation restricted to that information outside the certified method class.

notation.meaning: information assumed by the PEP through iteration k
information actually available through iteration k
certified update map at iteration k

review_flags: Information-based oracle mismatch statement lacks a supplied PEP-specific source

children.title: Oracle Fidelity Failures
children.top_down_role: Inexact, noisy, biased, or otherwise nonconforming oracle behavior outside the modeled regime.

knowledge_statements.title: Oracle Fidelity Failures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure caused by oracle responses that violate the response relations encoded in the PEP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal{O}_{mathrm{PEP}}(f,x)\) be the admissible response set encoded for querying instance \(f\) at \(x\). Oracle fidelity holds along a run only if every returned response \(z_k\) satisfies \[z_k\in\mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{PEP}}(f,x_k).\] A fidelity failure occurs when this inclusion fails, for example because gradients are biased, proximal points are inexact beyond the modeled tolerance, function values are corrupted, or stochastic moments violate their assumed bounds. Since the resulting transcript is infeasible for the PEP interpolation and oracle constraints, a certificate quantified over faithful transcripts does not apply to that run.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A PEP guarantee fails to cover a run when any returned gradient, value, proximal point, or stochastic response violates the modeled oracle relation.
assumptions_latex: The PEP certificate is valid only for transcripts satisfying its oracle constraints.
At least one deployed response lies outside the encoded admissible response set.

children.title: Guarantee Invalidity Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits on transferring a PEP conclusion after the problem class or oracle model changes.

knowledge_statements.title: Guarantee Invalidity Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical boundary separating certified PEP executions from executions to which the guarantee cannot be transferred.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C(f,\tau,\theta)\) be the conjunction of the PEP's problem-class, oracle-transcript, method-recurrence, initialization, parameter, and numerical-model assumptions. Suppose the certificate establishes \[C(f,\tau,\theta)\Longrightarrow P(f,\tau,\theta)\leq b.\] The guarantee is applicable to a deployed run only after establishing \(C(f,\tau,\theta)\). If any conjunct is false or unverified, the certificate alone yields no conclusion about \(P(f,\tau,\theta)\leq b\) for that run. This is an applicability boundary, not a claim that the inequality must be false outside the certified domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A PEP bound applies to a deployed run only when every modeled class, oracle, recurrence, initialization, parameter, and numerical assumption has been established for that run.
assumptions_latex: The certificate proves the conditional guarantee \(C(f,\tau,\theta)\Longrightarrow P(f,\tau,\theta)\leq b\).
Applicability is assessed for a particular deployed instance and transcript.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Failure or nonverification of \(C(f,\tau,\theta)\) prevents transfer of the certified bound to the deployed run.

notation.meaning: conjunction of all certificate applicability assumptions

children.title: Hidden-Information Requirements
children.top_down_role: Unstated problem data or global quantities required by the modeled method.

knowledge_statements.title: Hidden-Information Requirements
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonimplementability caused by a certified update's dependence on unavailable instance information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H_k=\sigma(x_0,z_0,\ldots,x_k,z_k,\xi)\) be the information sigma-algebra generated by permitted oracle observations and declared randomness \(\xi\) through iteration \(k\). A hidden-information requirement occurs when the certified update \(x_{k+1}\) depends on a quantity \(q(f)\) that is not measurable with respect to \(H_k\), and no value or valid bound for \(q(f)\) is supplied as a declared input. If there exist instances indistinguishable under \(H_k\) but having different values of \(q(f)\) that require different certified updates, then no \(H_k\)-measurable update map \(x_{k+1}=\Phi_k(H_k)\) can realize the certified rule uniformly over those instances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A method is not implementable under the stated information model when its certified update requires undeclared instance information that cannot be inferred from the permitted history.
assumptions_latex: Admissible updates must be measurable functions of \(H_k\).
There exist oracle-indistinguishable instances with different values of \(q(f)\) that require different certified updates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Dependence on undeclared, nonmeasurable \(q(f)\) makes the certified update inadmissible under the stated information model.

notation.meaning: permitted information sigma-algebra through iteration k
declared randomness available to the method

children.title: Method Information Budget
children.top_down_role: The observations and prior knowledge legitimately available to the method.

knowledge_statements.title: Method Information Budget
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Filtration-based specification of information legally available to a first-order method.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For horizon \(N\), a method information budget is a filtration \((H_k)_{k=0}^{N}) together with declared inputs \(J\). Here \(H_k\) is generated by \(J\), public or permitted private randomness, previous iterates, and oracle responses available no later than iteration \(k\). A method respects the budget when each query and update is measurable with respect to the information available before that action; in particular, \(x_{k+1}) must be \(H_k\)-measurable. Instance parameters, future oracle responses, optimal solutions, and objective values outside the transcript are unavailable unless explicitly included in \(J\) or inferable from \(H_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An information budget specifies the inputs, randomness, iterates, and oracle observations available at each step; every method action must depend only on that history.
assumptions_latex: The oracle protocol specifies when each response becomes observable.
Declared inputs \(J\) distinguish public side information from unknown instance data.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A recurrence is implementable under the budget only if every action satisfies the corresponding measurability constraint.

notation.meaning: declared side information supplied before execution

children.title: Unauthorized Information Leakage
children.top_down_role: PEP encodings that inadvertently grant access to information excluded by the intended method model.

knowledge_statements.title: Unauthorized Information Leakage
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure caused by allowing a deterministic PEP-modeled method to use information that cannot be recovered from its prescribed oracle transcript.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal I_k\) be the authorized transcript available when iteration \(k+1\) is selected. The prescribed deterministic method class requires a common admissible map \(\Phi_k\) satisfying \(x_{k+1}=\Phi_k(\mathcal I_k)\) on every modeled problem instance. Suppose instead that the modeled update is \(x_{k+1}=\Psi_k(\mathcal I_k,h)\), where \(h\) is unavailable from \(\mathcal I_k\), and that no admissible map \(\Phi_k\) factors this update through \(\mathcal I_k\) uniformly over the modeled instances. The formulation then uses an enlarged information model, so its bound does not certify implementability for the prescribed transcript-based method class.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unauthorized information leakage occurs when an update genuinely cannot be generated from the authorized transcript alone; a bound for that enlarged-information formulation does not certify the prescribed deterministic method class.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal I_k\) contains the oracle information authorized when \(x_{k+1}\) is selected.
\(h\) is unavailable from \(\mathcal I_k\).
The prescribed method class is deterministic and uses decision rules common to all modeled problem instances.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If no admissible \(\Phi_k\) satisfies \(\Psi_k(\mathcal I_k,h)=\Phi_k(\mathcal I_k)\) uniformly over the modeled instances, then the update is not implementable under the information budget \(\mathcal I_k\).

children.title: Implementability Failure Boundary
children.top_down_role: Cases where an optimized method description cannot be realized under the intended information restrictions.

knowledge_statements.title: Implementability Failure Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transcript-based criterion separating algebraically feasible families of PEP trajectories from families generated by an admissible deterministic first-order method.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix an oracle model, a finite horizon \(N\), and a class \(\Omega\) of modeled problem instances. For each \(\omega\in\Omega\), let \(\mathcal I_k(\omega)\) be the authorized transcript available before selecting \(x_{k+1}(\omega)\). A family of PEP trajectories is implementable by the prescribed deterministic method class only if there exist common admissible maps \(\Phi_0,\ldots,\Phi_{N-1}\) such that \(x_{k+1}(\omega)=\Phi_k(\mathcal I_k(\omega))\) for every \(\omega\in\Omega\) and every \(k<N\). The implementability boundary is crossed when no such common family of maps exists. Algebraic consistency of sampled values, gradients, iterates, and Gram entries alone does not imply this transcript-based implementability condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A modeled family of PEP trajectories is implementable only when the same admissible decision rule at each iteration generates the next iterate from the authorized transcript for every modeled problem instance.
assumptions_latex: \(N\in\mathbb N\) is finite.
\(\Omega\) is the modeled class of problem instances.
\(\mathcal I_k(\omega)\) is the prescribed transcript before \(x_{k+1}(\omega)\) is selected.
The prescribed method class is deterministic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\neg\exists(\Phi_k)_{k=0}^{N-1}\;\forall\omega\in\Omega\;\forall k<N:\ x_{k+1}(\omega)=\Phi_k(\mathcal I_k(\omega))\) implies implementability failure.

children.title: Initialization Set Mismatch
children.top_down_role: Conflicts between admissible starting states in the PEP model and those in the target setting.

knowledge_statements.title: Initialization Set Mismatch
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transfer boundary when the target initial states are not covered by the initialization set used in the certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S_{\mathrm{cert}}\) be the set of initial configurations allowed by a PEP certificate and suppose it proves \(\sup_{z_0\in S_{\mathrm{cert}}}P(z_N)\le B\). For a target initialization set \(S_{\mathrm{tar}}\), this certificate transfers directly only when \(S_{\mathrm{tar}}\subseteq S_{\mathrm{cert}}\), or when a separate argument maps every target initialization into the certified set without worsening the claimed bound. If \(S_{\mathrm{tar}}\nsubseteq S_{\mathrm{cert}}\), the certificate imposes no bound on excluded initializations, so the same inequality over \(S_{\mathrm{tar}}\) is not justified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A certificate over one initialization set does not cover a target set containing excluded initial states unless a valid reduction supplies that coverage.
assumptions_latex: \(P(z_N)\) is the certified terminal performance measure.
\(B\in\mathbb R\) is uniform over \(S_{\mathrm{cert}}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S_{\mathrm{tar}}\nsubseteq S_{\mathrm{cert}}\) prevents direct inference of \(\sup_{z_0\in S_{\mathrm{tar}}}P(z_N)\le B\).

children.title: Performance Metric Mismatch
children.top_down_role: Conflicts between the optimized criterion and the quantity used to interpret performance.

knowledge_statements.title: Performance Metric Mismatch
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transfer boundary between a certified performance functional and a different target functional.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a PEP certificate establish \(P(z_N)\le B\) for every admissible trajectory, while the desired guarantee concerns another metric \(Q(z_N)\). The certificate yields \(Q(z_N)\le\psi(B)\) if an independently valid comparison \(Q(z)\le\psi(P(z))\) holds on every reachable terminal state and \(\psi\) is nondecreasing on the relevant range of \(P\). Without an established uniform comparison between \(P\) and \(Q\), the certified bound on \(P\) does not by itself justify the claimed bound on \(Q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bound for one performance metric cannot be transferred to another unless a uniform comparison inequality connects the metrics on all reachable terminal states.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) and \(Q\) are real-valued on the reachable terminal states.
\(P(z_N)\le B\) holds uniformly for the certified model.
\(\psi\) is defined and nondecreasing on the relevant range of \(P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(Q(z)\le\psi(P(z))\) for every reachable terminal state \(z\), then \(Q(z_N)\le\psi(B)\); without such established control, that transfer is not justified by the certificate alone.

children.title: Reference-Point Incompatibility
children.top_down_role: Incompatible choices of optimizer, solution set, initial scale, or normalization reference.

knowledge_statements.title: Reference-Point Incompatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of a certified bound after replacing its optimizer or comparison point by an incompatible reference point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a certificate is formulated relative to a point \(x_\star\) satisfying a predicate \(R_\star\), such as optimality and oracle consistency, and proves \(P(x_N,x_\star)\le B\). Replacing \(x_\star\) by \(\bar x\) is valid only if \(\bar x\) satisfies every reference-point constraint used by the PEP, or if a separate uniform comparison bounds \(P(x_N,\bar x)\) by the certified quantity. If \(R_\star(\bar x)\) fails, interpolation, normalization, or optimality constraints involving the reference point may fail, and the original bound does not transfer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A guarantee relative to an optimizer cannot be reused with another reference point unless that point satisfies the same constraints or a comparison theorem applies.
assumptions_latex: \(R_\star(x_\star)\) encodes all reference-point conditions used by the certificate.
\(P(x_N,x_\star)\le B\) holds under those conditions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\neg R_\star(\bar x)\) precludes direct inference of \(P(x_N,\bar x)\le B\).

children.title: Guarantee Transfer Failures
children.top_down_role: Loss of validity when initialization or metric conventions differ across formulations.

knowledge_statements.title: Guarantee Transfer Failures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: General boundary for transporting a PEP certificate between differing problem, initialization, algorithm, or metric specifications.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal F_c\) be the feasible trajectory set of a certified PEP with metric \(P_c\), and assume \(\sup_{z\in\mathcal F_c}P_c(z)\le B\). For a target model \((\mathcal F_t,P_t)\), the same bound transfers if there is a map \(T:\mathcal F_t\to\mathcal F_c\) satisfying \(P_t(z)\le P_c(Tz)\) for every \(z\in\mathcal F_t\). If no such inclusion-preserving or comparison-preserving reduction is established, differences in initialization, reference points, information rules, function class, or metric invalidate direct transfer of the numerical guarantee \(B\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A PEP guarantee transfers only through a reduction sending every target trajectory to a certified trajectory while dominating the target performance metric.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal F_c\) and \(\mathcal F_t\) are the certified and target feasible trajectory sets.
\(P_c\) and \(P_t\) are their respective performance metrics.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T(\mathcal F_t)\subseteq\mathcal F_c\) and \(P_t\le P_c\circ T\) imply \(\sup_{z\in\mathcal F_t}P_t(z)\le B\).

knowledge_statements.title: Insufficient Interpolation Information
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exactness failure when imposed sampled-data constraints do not characterize interpolation by the modeled function or operator class.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal D\) denote finite sampled data and let \(\mathcal C(\mathcal D)\) be the constraints imposed by a PEP relaxation. Exact interpolation requires the equivalence \(\mathcal D\text{ is realizable by some }f\in\mathcal F\) if and only if \(\mathcal C(\mathcal D)\) holds. If the imposed constraints are necessary but not sufficient, the relaxation admits some \(\widehat{\mathcal D}\) satisfying \(\mathcal C(\widehat{\mathcal D})\) that no member of \(\mathcal F\) realizes. Maximizing performance over this enlarged set remains an upper bound on the true worst case, but its value and optimizer need not be exact or realizable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Necessary but insufficient interpolation constraints enlarge the PEP feasible set, preserving an upper bound while potentially destroying exactness and realizability.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal F\) is the modeled function or operator class.
\(\mathcal C(\mathcal D)\) is necessary for interpolation by \(\mathcal F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists\widehat{\mathcal D}:\mathcal C(\widehat{\mathcal D})\land\neg\operatorname{Interp}_{\mathcal F}(\widehat{\mathcal D})\) implies that the relaxation need not be exact.

children.title: Rank-Constraint Violations
children.top_down_role: Computed Gram data whose required rank exceeds the imposed realization limit.

knowledge_statements.title: Rank-Constraint Violations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional realizability failure caused by a feasible Gram matrix whose rank exceeds the prescribed ambient dimension.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v_1,\ldots,v_m\) be all vectors represented in a Gram formulation and let \(G\in\mathbb S_+^m\) satisfy \(G_{ij}=\langle v_i,v_j\rangle\). Such data admit a realization by vectors in \(\mathbb R^d\) if and only if \(\operatorname{rank}(G)\le d\). Consequently, a relaxed PEP solution with \(\operatorname{rank}(G)>d\) violates the dimension constraint and cannot represent a trajectory in the prescribed space. Dropping the rank restriction therefore preserves an upper relaxation but may destroy finite-dimensional exactness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-semidefinite Gram solution is realizable in dimension d exactly when its rank is at most d; higher rank violates the modeled dimension.
assumptions_latex: \(G\in\mathbb S_+^m\).
\(d\in\mathbb N\) is the prescribed ambient dimension.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{rank}(G)>d\) implies that no \(v_1,\ldots,v_m\in\mathbb R^d\) have Gram matrix \(G\).

children.title: Ambient-Dimension Shortfall
children.top_down_role: Target spaces too small to support the geometry represented by the finite data.

knowledge_statements.title: Ambient-Dimension Shortfall
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exactness boundary when the prescribed space is too small to realize the independent directions required by sampled PEP data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a feasible sampled-data solution, form the Gram matrix \(G\) of every independent vector quantity needed to reconstruct its trajectory. If the prescribed ambient space is \(\mathbb R^d\) and \(r=\operatorname{rank}(G)>d\), then that sampled solution cannot be realized in the target dimension. An unconstrained semidefinite PEP may still return its objective value, but this value is only a dimension-relaxed upper bound unless an alternative optimal feasible solution with Gram rank at most \(d\) is exhibited.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a PEP solution requires more independent vector directions than the target dimension supplies, that solution is unrealizable and exactness needs a lower-rank alternative.
assumptions_latex: \(G\in\mathbb S_+^m\) represents all vectors required for reconstruction.
\(d\in\mathbb N\) is the target dimension.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{rank}(G)>d\) makes the represented data unrealizable in \(\mathbb R^d\).

notation.meaning: rank of the reconstruction Gram matrix

review_flags: PEP-specific dimension-relaxation exactness source is absent

The statement correctly distinguishes unrealizability of a particular high-rank solution from exactness of the optimal value when a lower-rank optimum may exist, but the PEP-specific interpretation lacks a cited source and locator.

children.title: Minimal Realization Dimension
children.top_down_role: Dimension thresholds associated with realizing candidate worst-case data.

knowledge_statements.title: Minimal Realization Dimension
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smallest Euclidean dimension supporting a vector realization of a positive-semidefinite Gram matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(G\in\mathbb S_+^m\), define its minimal realization dimension by \[d_{\min}(G):=\min\left\{d\in\mathbb N_0:\exists v_1,\ldots,v_m\in\mathbb R^d\text{ with }G_{ij}=\langle v_i,v_j\rangle\text{ for all }i,j\right\}.\] Then \(d_{\min}(G)=\operatorname{rank}(G)\). Thus the rank of the complete Gram matrix is precisely the least ambient dimension in which the represented sampled vectors, and hence their mutual inner products and squared distances, can be realized.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The minimal Euclidean dimension realizing a positive-semidefinite Gram matrix equals the matrix rank.
assumptions_latex: \(G\in\mathbb S_+^m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_{\min}(G)=\operatorname{rank}(G)\).

notation.meaning: minimal Euclidean realization dimension of G

review_flags: Standard linear-algebra definition and identity require a precise source locator

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Definition is an appropriate content kind for this leaf, and the identity between minimal Euclidean realization dimension and PSD Gram rank is precise. No authoritative source with a specific definition, theorem, section, or page locator is cited.

children.title: Dimension-Lifted Realizability
children.top_down_role: Recovery of realizability after permitting a larger ambient space.

knowledge_statements.title: Dimension-Lifted Realizability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Realizability restoration by embedding Gram data into a Euclidean space whose dimension meets the rank requirement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G\in\mathbb S_+^m\) have rank \(r\). There exists a factorization \(G=V^{\mathsf T}V\) with \(V\in\mathbb R^{r\times m}\); the columns \(v_1,\ldots,v_m\in\mathbb R^r\) therefore realize all prescribed inner products. For every \(d\ge r\), padding these columns with \(d-r\) zero coordinates gives a realization in \(\mathbb R^d\). Hence a dimension-relaxed PEP solution becomes geometrically realizable after lifting the ambient dimension to at least \(\operatorname{rank}(G)\), provided its non-Gram interpolation and algorithmic constraints are also sufficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any positive-semidefinite Gram solution of rank r is realizable in every dimension at least r by factorization and zero-padding.
assumptions_latex: \(G\in\mathbb S_+^m\) and \(r=\operatorname{rank}(G)\).
\(d\ge r\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists v_1,\ldots,v_m\in\mathbb R^d\) such that \(G_{ij}=\langle v_i,v_j\rangle\) for all \(i,j\).

notation.meaning: Gram factor whose columns realize the modeled vectors
rank and minimal realization dimension of G

children.title: Positive Duality Gaps
children.top_down_role: Regimes where primal and dual optimal values do not coincide.

knowledge_statements.title: Positive Duality Gaps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificate exactness failure when the PEP primal value lies strictly below its dual certificate value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a primal maximization PEP with value \(p^\star\) and its dual minimization certificate problem with value \(d^\star\). Weak duality gives \(p^\star\le d^\star\). A positive duality gap occurs when both values are finite and \(p^\star<d^\star\). In that case, every dual feasible point still provides a valid upper certificate for the primal worst case, but no sequence of dual certificates can converge in value to \(p^\star\); consequently, the dual optimum does not certify the exact primal performance value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the finite dual optimum strictly exceeds the primal optimum, dual feasibility still yields upper bounds but cannot certify the exact worst-case value.
assumptions_latex: \(p^\star,d^\star\in\mathbb R\).
Weak duality \(p^\star\le d^\star\) holds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d^\star-p^\star>0\) prevents an exact value certificate from the dual problem.

children.title: Primal Nonattainment
children.top_down_role: Finite primal bounds lacking an attaining feasible performance configuration.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Nonattainment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of primal attainment in a finite-dimensional convex performance-estimation problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a finite-dimensional Euclidean space, let \(C\subseteq X\) be nonempty, and let \(f:C\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper. Write \(p^\star=\inf_{x\in C}f(x)\). Primal nonattainment occurs precisely when \(p^\star\in\mathbb{R}\) and \(\{x\in C:f(x)=p^\star\}=\varnothing\). Equivalently, there may exist a minimizing sequence \((x_k)\subset C\) with \(f(x_k)\to p^\star\), while no feasible point realizes the limiting value. Consequently, a finite PEP value need not supply an exact worst-case primal instance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite primal infimum may be approached by feasible instances without being achieved, so the PEP value need not correspond to an exact worst-case instance.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is finite-dimensional and \(C\neq\varnothing\).
\(f\) is proper and \(p^\star\in\mathbb{R}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}f(x)=\varnothing\) although a sequence \((x_k)\subset C\) can satisfy \(f(x_k)\to p^\star\).

children.title: Dual Nonattainment
children.top_down_role: Valid dual bounds lacking an attaining multiplier or certificate representation.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Nonattainment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of dual attainment despite a finite dual supremum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a primal minimization problem with dual feasible set \(D\) and concave dual objective \(g:D\to[-\infty,+\infty)\), write \(d^\star=\sup_{y\in D}g(y)\). Dual nonattainment occurs when \(d^\star\in\mathbb{R}\) but \(\{y\in D:g(y)=d^\star\}=\varnothing\). This may hold even when strong duality gives \(d^\star=p^\star\): a maximizing sequence \((y_k)\subset D\) can satisfy \(g(y_k)\to p^\star\), yet no optimal multiplier exists from which to extract an attained exact dual certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong duality can hold while no dual optimizer exists; maximizing multipliers approach the primal value but never furnish an attained optimal certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(D\neq\varnothing\) and \(g\) is concave on \(D\).
\(d^\star\in\mathbb{R}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmax}_{y\in D}g(y)=\varnothing\), possibly while \(d^\star=p^\star\).

children.title: Certificate Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits on extracting exact proof artifacts under gap or nonattainment phenomena.

knowledge_statements.title: Certificate Failure Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Attainment requirements for exact multiplier-based PEP certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a primal-dual pair with values \(p^\star\) and \(d^\star\), and suppose the intended PEP certificate is an optimal dual point \(y^\star\in D\) whose feasibility and objective identity \(g(y^\star)=p^\star\) prove the bound. Such an exact certificate exists only if the dual supremum is attained and the duality gap is zero. If \(d^\star<p^\star\), or if \(d^\star=p^\star\) but no \(y^\star\in D\) attains \(d^\star\), this certificate mechanism fails; convergent objective values alone provide only approximate certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact optimal-dual certificate requires zero duality gap and an attained dual optimum; otherwise only approximate value certificates may remain.
assumptions_latex: The prescribed certificate must be represented by a feasible optimal dual point.
Weak duality \(g(y)\leq p^\star\) holds for every \(y\in D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An exact certificate of this form requires \(y^\star\in D\) with \(g(y^\star)=d^\star=p^\star\).

children.title: Ill-Conditioning Signatures
children.top_down_role: Numerical symptoms associated with scaling imbalance, near-dependence, or unstable feasibility judgments.

knowledge_statements.title: Ill-Conditioning Signatures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Numerical signatures indicating sensitivity of a conic PEP solution or certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let conic data \(d\) define a solution mapping \(S(d)\), and let \(z\in S(d)\) denote primal-dual variables. Local ill-conditioning is present when the modulus \(\kappa(d)=\limsup_{d'\to d}\operatorname{dist}(S(d'),S(d))/\lVert d'-d\rVert\) is large or infinite. Observable signatures include large changes in objective or recovered variables under small scaling-preserving perturbations, rapidly growing multiplier norms, near-zero eigenvalues of primal or dual slack matrices, and residuals that vary substantially with solver tolerance or precision. These signatures warn that small residuals need not imply a stable reconstructed certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Extreme sensitivity, growing multipliers, nearly singular slack matrices, and tolerance-dependent residuals signal that a numerical PEP certificate may be unstable.
assumptions_latex: The PEP has a finite-dimensional conic formulation depending on data \(d\).
Distances and perturbations use fixed, scaling-consistent norms.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A large or infinite \(\kappa(d)\) makes numerical solutions and reconstructed certificates sensitive to small data errors.

notation.meaning: primal-dual solution set for data d

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports the asserted conditioning signatures, and the displayed modulus for the set-valued solution map uses a distance between sets without defining whether this is an excess, Hausdorff distance, or another set distance. The relationship among that modulus, multiplier growth, slack eigenvalues, and tolerance-dependent residuals therefore cannot be reliably reviewed as one mathematical condition.

children.title: Ambiguous Solver Statuses
children.top_down_role: Unknown, indeterminate, or limit-terminated outcomes that do not support a definitive conclusion.

knowledge_statements.title: Ambiguous Solver Statuses
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical boundary between a solver label and a verifiable PEP conclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a solver return a status \(s\) and candidate primal-dual data \((x,y)\) for a conic PEP. If \(s\) does not distinguish among optimality, infeasibility, unboundedness, numerical failure, and termination at an iteration or time limit, then \(s\) alone entails none of those mathematical conclusions. A bound may be accepted only after independent checks establish the relevant primal or dual feasibility, objective relation, and residual tolerances. In particular, labels such as unknown or indeterminate are not certificates of either a finite worst-case bound or failure of the PEP model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An indeterminate solver label proves neither optimality nor infeasibility; mathematical conclusions require independently checked residuals, feasibility, and objective relations.
assumptions_latex: The solver status lacks a unique mathematical interpretation.
Candidate data may be available but have not yet been independently verified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The status \(s\) alone certifies neither \(p^\star\), infeasibility, nor unboundedness.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The logical warning is plausible and the failure_boundary kind fits, but solver labels and their meanings vary across implementations. An authoritative solver or conic-optimization reference with a specific locator is required to support the stated status categories and validation requirements.

children.title: Inaccurate Solution Statuses
children.top_down_role: Approximate optimality or feasibility statuses requiring additional validation.

knowledge_statements.title: Inaccurate Solution Statuses
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity boundary for solutions returned with relaxed numerical accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a conic PEP solver returns \((x,y)\) with an inaccurate-optimal status. Let \(r_p\), \(r_d\), \(r_c\), and \(\gamma=p(x)-g(y)\) denote normalized primal, dual, cone, and gap residuals. For a prescribed acceptance tolerance \(\tau>0\), the returned point is not a verified certificate unless \(r_p\leq\tau\), \(r_d\leq\tau\), \(r_c\leq\tau\), and the sign and magnitude of \(\gamma\) satisfy the certificate's required inequality. A solver's relaxed status cannot substitute for these checks, especially when reconstruction amplifies perturbations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inaccurate-optimal label is not a certificate unless independently computed feasibility, cone, and duality-gap residuals meet the intended tolerance.
assumptions_latex: Residuals are normalized using fixed problem-dependent scales.
A certificate acceptance tolerance \(\tau>0\) is specified before validation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Acceptance requires \(\max\{r_p,r_d,r_c\}\leq\tau\) together with the required objective-gap inequality.

notation.meaning: normalized primal, dual, and cone residuals

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The validation principle is plausible, but the normalized primal, dual, and cone residuals are not mathematically defined, and the required sign of the objective gap depends on the certificate orientation. A specific conic-solver or numerical-certification source is needed before this solver-independent formulation can be accepted.

children.title: Status Reliability Checks
children.top_down_role: Consistency checks linking reported status to residuals, bounds, conditioning, and independent reruns.

knowledge_statements.title: Status Reliability Checks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-based validation of a reported conic PEP status.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given conic PEP data, a reported status, and candidate primal-dual variables \((x,y)\), recompute in higher precision the affine residuals, distances to the primal and dual cones, and objectives \(p(x)\) and \(g(y)\). An optimality status is numerically certified at tolerance \(\tau\) only when both points are \(\tau\)-feasible and the normalized gap is at most \(\tau\). An infeasibility or unboundedness status is accepted only from a separately checked alternative-system or improving-ray certificate. Re-solving after equilibration or increased precision must preserve the claimed conclusion within the stated tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Validate solver statuses by recomputing residuals and gaps, checking rays for exceptional statuses, and confirming stability under scaling or higher precision.
assumptions_latex: A tolerance \(\tau>0\) and normalization convention are fixed.
Candidate variables or an exceptional-status certificate are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Only independently verified feasibility, gap, or ray conditions constitute a status certificate at tolerance \(\tau\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Residual, cone-distance, gap, and ray checks are appropriate certificate concepts, and certificate is a suitable content kind. However, no source defines the normalization or supports the assertion that re-solving after equilibration or increased precision must preserve the conclusion. The latter is a robustness check rather than a generally necessary mathematical certificate condition.

knowledge_statements.title: Unstable or Nonverifiable Dual Data
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Numerical dual output that cannot support a reproducible PEP bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((y_k)\) be computed dual candidates with objectives \(g(y_k)\to\beta\). The value \(\beta\) is not certified by these data when dual feasibility cannot be verified at the retained precision. Warning mechanisms include \(\lVert y_k\rVert\to\infty\), absence of a convergent subsequence, negative slack eigenvalues exceeding the validation tolerance, or feasibility residuals that increase after rounding or higher-precision recomputation. Objective convergence without stable dual feasibility establishes neither an attained dual certificate nor a reproducible bound; the original conic constraints must be checked using the exported multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convergent dual objectives do not certify a bound when multipliers diverge or their feasibility disappears under rounding or higher-precision checking.
assumptions_latex: \((y_k)\) is a sequence of numerical dual candidates.
Certificate verification uses the original, unrounded dual constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The limit \(\beta\) is nonverifiable unless sufficiently accurate dual data satisfy the required feasibility and objective inequalities.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The central claim that objective convergence without verified dual feasibility does not certify a bound is sound, but the listed numerical warning mechanisms and their relation to reproducibility require an authoritative numerical conic-optimization or PEP source. The failure_boundary kind fits the topic.

knowledge_statements.title: Spurious or Unrealizable Instance Reconstruction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of numerical Gram data to define a valid worst-case instance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A numerical PEP solution represented by a Gram matrix \(G\), function values, and interpolation data yields a realizable instance only if \(G\succeq0\) and every class-interpolation and algorithmic constraint is satisfied. If the computed matrix has a materially negative eigenvalue, or a truncated factorization \(G\approx P^{\mathsf T}P\) causes reconstructed vectors to violate those constraints beyond tolerance, the reconstruction is spurious. Likewise, arbitrary projection of \(G\) onto the positive-semidefinite cone is invalid unless all remaining constraints and the claimed performance value are rechecked afterward.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reconstructed worst-case instance is unrealizable if its Gram matrix is not positive semidefinite or its recovered vectors violate interpolation or algorithmic constraints.
assumptions_latex: The finite PEP uses Gram-representable vectors and explicit interpolation constraints.
A reconstruction tolerance is fixed relative to the problem scaling.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Realizability requires \(G=P^{\mathsf T}P\succeq0\) and satisfaction of every defining constraint by the reconstructed data.

notation.meaning: factor whose columns realize the modeled vectors

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Gram-matrix and constraint-satisfaction requirements are mathematically plausible and match the reconstruction-failure container, but the PEP-specific claim about interpolation, factor truncation, and post-projection revalidation has no cited evidence. A PEP interpolation or worst-case reconstruction source with a precise locator is required.

children.title: Finite-Horizon Conclusions
children.top_down_role: Claims supported only for the fixed iteration horizons represented in a PEP.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Horizon Conclusions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interpretation of a PEP bound computed for one fixed iteration horizon.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix an algorithm, a problem class \(\mathcal F\), an initialization set \(\mathcal I\), a performance measure \(\Phi_N\), and a horizon \(N\in\mathbb N\). If the corresponding PEP has value \(B_N\), then every admissible execution represented by that PEP satisfies \(\Phi_N\leq B_N\). This conclusion concerns iteration \(N\) and the modeled initialization, oracle, and dimension assumptions only. Without a theorem relating different horizons, it implies neither \(\Phi_M\leq B_N\) for \(M\neq N\), nor monotonicity of \((B_N)\), nor an asymptotic convergence rate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A horizon-N PEP bound controls the modeled performance at iteration N only; it does not automatically control other horizons or establish an asymptotic rate.
assumptions_latex: The PEP exactly or conservatively represents all admissible executions through horizon \(N\).
Its optimal value \(B_N\) is a valid upper bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_{(f,I)\in\mathcal F\times\mathcal I}\Phi_N(f,I)\leq B_N\), with no automatic conclusion for \(M\neq N\).

notation.meaning: PEP upper bound at horizon N

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: fixed-index optimization bounds do not quantify unmodeled indices
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

children.title: Asymptotic Claims
children.top_down_role: Long-run interpretations proposed from horizon-dependent performance results.

knowledge_statements.title: Asymptotic Claims
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient uniform information for deriving an asymptotic rate from finite-horizon PEP bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(W_N=\sup_{(f,I)\in\mathcal F\times\mathcal I}\Phi_N(f,I)\). A sequence of certified finite-horizon inequalities \(W_N\leq B_N\) yields the asymptotic claim \(W_N=O(r_N)\) only when there exist constants \(C<\infty\) and \(N_0\), independent of \(N\) and of the admissible instance, such that \(B_N\leq Cr_N\) for every \(N\geq N_0\). Numerical values for finitely many horizons, or horizon-dependent constants without a uniform bound, do not establish this conclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite-horizon certificates imply an asymptotic rate only through a uniform analytic bound whose constant is independent of both horizon and problem instance.
assumptions_latex: \(r_N>0\) for all sufficiently large \(N\).
Each inequality \(W_N\leq B_N\) is valid for the same modeled class and algorithm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(B_N\leq Cr_N\) uniformly for \(N\geq N_0\), then \(W_N=O(r_N)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: definition of a uniform big-O bound applied to worst-case performance
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

children.title: Limit-Exchange Pitfalls
children.top_down_role: Invalid inferences involving optimization, supremum operations, parameter limits, or growing horizons.

knowledge_statements.title: Limit-Exchange Pitfalls
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise convergence does not justify exchanging horizon limits with worst-case suprema.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the instance parameter be \(\theta\in[0,1)\) and define \(a_N(\theta)=\theta^N\). For every fixed \(\theta<1\), one has \(a_N(\theta)\to0\), so \(\sup_{\theta\in[0,1)}\lim_{N\to\infty}a_N(\theta)=0\). However, \(\sup_{\theta\in[0,1)}a_N(\theta)=1\) for every \(N\), and hence \(\lim_{N\to\infty}\sup_{\theta\in[0,1)}a_N(\theta)=1\). Thus instancewise convergence does not imply convergence of worst-case performance; exchanging the limit and supremum requires additional uniformity or compactness hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every fixed instance can converge while the worst-case value stays constant, so horizon limits cannot generally be exchanged with optimization over instances.
assumptions_latex: The admissible parameter set is \([0,1)\).
The horizon-dependent performance is \(a_N(\theta)=\theta^N\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_{\theta}\lim_{N\to\infty}a_N(\theta)=0\neq1=\lim_{N\to\infty}\sup_{\theta}a_N(\theta)\).

notation.meaning: performance of instance theta at horizon N

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: explicit elementary counterexample directly verifies failure of limit-supremum interchange
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

children.title: Horizon Extrapolation Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits on extending fixed-horizon evidence to unmodeled iteration counts.

knowledge_statements.title: Horizon Extrapolation Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes a fixed-horizon PEP certificate from a rate or asymptotic guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a method, an instance class \(\mathcal I\), a family of performance measures \((R_k)_{k\in\mathbb N}\) with \(R_k:\mathcal I\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\), and one horizon \(N\in\mathbb N\). A certificate \(R_N(I)\le B_N\) for every \(I\in\mathcal I\) constrains only the specified horizon. Without a cross-horizon assumption, it does not imply any proposed family of bounds \(R_k(I)\le\widehat B_k\) for every \(I\in\mathcal I\) and \(k\ne N\), monotonicity of \((R_k(I))_{k\in\mathbb N}\), or convergence \(R_k(I)\to0\). Such conclusions require hypotheses covering the relevant horizons and any regularity needed for a limiting operation. In particular, the fixed-horizon certificate is logically compatible with arbitrarily large later values because no relation between \(R_N\) and \(R_k\) for \(k>N\) has been assumed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A certificate at one iteration cannot be extrapolated to other horizons or to convergence without additional uniform bounds and cross-horizon assumptions.
assumptions_latex: N\in\mathbb N
R_k:\mathcal I\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\quad(k\in\mathbb N)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bigl(\forall I\in\mathcal I,\ R_N(I)\le B_N\bigr)\not\Rightarrow\bigl(\forall k\in\mathbb N\setminus\{N\}\ \forall I\in\mathcal I,\ R_k(I)\le\widehat B_k\bigr)

notation.meaning: admissible problem instances and initial data
performance of the method on instance I after k steps
a proposed upper bound at horizon k

children.title: Worst-Case Regime
children.top_down_role: Extremal performance over the modeled problem class, oracle, initialization, and method constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Worst-Case Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the deterministic worst-case quantity optimized by a standard finite-horizon PEP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal I\) be the instance class encoded by a performance-estimation problem and let \(R_N(I)\) be the selected performance criterion after \(N\) oracle calls or iterations. The worst-case value is
\[W_N:=\sup_{I\in\mathcal I}R_N(I).\]
A number \(U_N\) is a class-wide worst-case guarantee precisely when \(R_N(I)\le U_N\) for every \(I\in\mathcal I\), equivalently \(W_N\le U_N\). If the PEP formulation is exact, its optimal value equals \(W_N\); if it is a relaxation, its optimal value is only an upper bound on \(W_N\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Worst-case performance is the supremum over every admissible instance. An exact PEP computes it; a relaxation may only upper-bound it.
assumptions_latex: N\in\mathbb N
R_N:\mathcal I\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: W_N=\sup_{I\in\mathcal I}R_N(I),\qquad W_N\le U_N\iff \forall I\in\mathcal I,\ R_N(I)\le U_N

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and definition content kind fit the worst-case-regime leaf, but no evidence is supplied for the PEP-specific claims distinguishing exact formulations from relaxations. An authoritative PEP source with a precise theorem or section locator is required.

children.title: Typical-Case Regime
children.top_down_role: Performance characterized relative to a distribution, sampling process, or representative population.

knowledge_statements.title: Typical-Case Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines distribution-relative performance rather than a class supremum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) be a probability measure on a measurable instance space \((\mathcal I,\mathscr F)\), let \(R_N:\mathcal I\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be measurable, and fix \(\alpha\in(0,1)\). A typical-case performance descriptor is a specified distributional functional of \(R_N(I)\) for \(I\sim P\). For example, when \(R_N\in L^1(P)\), its mean is \[T_N(P):=\mathbb E_P[R_N(I)].\] Its lower \(\alpha\)-quantile is \[q_{N,\alpha}(P):=\inf\{t\in\mathbb R:P(R_N(I)\le t)\ge\alpha\}.\] A typical-case descriptor is not determined until both \(P\) and the functional are specified, and it need not equal the supremum of \(R_N\) over \(\mathcal I\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Typical-case performance is an expectation, quantile, or other specified distributional functional under a specified law on instances, not a class supremum.
assumptions_latex: (\mathcal I,\mathscr F,P)\text{ is a probability space}
R_N:\mathcal I\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\text{ is }\mathscr F\text{-measurable}
\alpha\in(0,1)
R_N\in L^1(P)\text{ when }T_N(P)\text{ is used}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: T_N(P)=\mathbb E_P[R_N(I)],\qquad q_{N,\alpha}(P)=\inf\{t\in\mathbb R:P(R_N(I)\le t)\ge\alpha\}
